title: [Triton/Gluon] Add MXFP8 Flash Attention v2 (gfx950 / CDNA4)
body:
## Summary

  Adds a pure-Triton MXFP8 Flash Attention v2 implementation for gfx950 (CDNA4 / MI300X), including forward and backward passes.

  Uses MXFP8 block-scaling (E8M0 microscales, one uint8 per 32 elements along the head dimension). Requires gfx950; asserts at runtime on other architectures.

  ## Changes

  - `_triton_kernels/attention/mxfp8_attention_kernel.py`: Triton kernels for forward (`attn_fwd_mxfp8`) and backward (`_bwd_kernel_dkdv_mxfp8`, `_bwd_kernel_dq_mxfp8`, `_bwd_preprocess_use_o_mxfp8`). All 6 public kernels have repr decorators. Autotune configs resolved via `get_tuned_kernel_config()` backed by JSON. Dead code removed (`get_padded_headsize`, `get_input_shapes`).
  - `attention/mxfp8_attention.py`: Python wrappers `mxfp8_attention_forward` and `mxfp8_attention_backward`.
  - `utils/_triton/arch_info.py`: Add canonical `is_cdna4()` definition (was used in `__init__.py` and the wrapper but missing from the module).
  - `configs/gfx950/triton/attention/mxfp8_attn/DEFAULT.json`: Per-arch pinned tile config.
  - `__init__.py`: Export `mxfp8_attention` under the `_CDNA4_ONLY` gate.
  - `triton_tests/attention/test_mxfp8_attention_kernel.py`: Correctness  tests (skip on non-gfx950 architectures).
  - `bench_mxfp8_attention.py`: Benchmark across representative shapes.

  ## Test results

  Verified on **MI350X (gfx950)**:
  ✅ MHA / GQA (num_q_heads ≠ num_kv_heads)
  ✅ causal on / off
  ✅ bf16 and fp16 (use_mxfp8=False: verifies core attention correctness without MXFP8 quantization)

title: fix(custom_all_reduce): send the real IPC offset instead of 0
body:
## Problem

`_broadcast_ipc` (`aiter/dist/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py:602`) pins the IPC offset to `0`:

```python
self._ipc_handle_fn(data_ptr, handle.data_ptr())
return self._gather_ipc_meta((handle, 0))
```

`hipIpcGetMemHandle` always returns a handle for the **whole allocation** containing the pointer, never for the pointer itself, and the importing rank maps that allocation at its own base. A buffer that is a sub-block of a larger allocation therefore has to carry its `ptr - base` offset. Offset `0` is only correct when the pool pointer happens to *be* an allocation base.

Whether it is depends on the state of PyTorch's caching allocator:

- **Fresh allocator** — the IPC pool is the first large allocation and gets its own segment, so `ptr == base` and offset `0` is accidentally right. This is why single-engine runs are fine.
- **Allocator already holding a cached large segment** — a co-resident second engine on the same node, or simply any earlier allocate-and-free — the pool lands as a sub-block, `ptr != base`, and peers read from the base of that segment instead. **No error is raised; the all-reduce just returns data from whatever else lives there.**

The C++ graph path already does this correctly, and even carries the comment — `get_graph_buffer_ipc_meta` in `csrc/include/custom_all_reduce.cuh:3947`:

```cpp
// note: must share the base address of each allocation, or we get wrong address
if (hipPointerGetAttribute(&base_ptr, HIP_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_RANGE_START_ADDR, ...))
offsets[i] = ((char*)ptr) - ((char*)base_ptr);
```

Only the Python side, for the named pool buffers (`meta` and `input`), was missing it. The C++ importers already apply `offsets[i]` (`custom_all_reduce.cuh:3911`, `:4001`, `:4025`, `:4124`), so no kernel-side change is needed.

## Fix

Resolve the base with `hipMemGetAddressRange` and send the real offset. New helper `_ipc_base_ptr`; `_broadcast_ipc` exports the handle from the base and gathers `data_ptr - base`. Raw `hipMalloc` / `hipExtMallocWithFlags` buffers are their own base, so this is a no-op for them.

## Relation to `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_RAW_INPUT_POOL`

That env var forces a raw `hipMalloc` input pool, whose pointer is always an allocation base — which is exactly why setting it made the problem disappear. It stays as an escape hatch and is still the right thing under `expandable_segments` (VMM pointers genuinely cannot be exported, #4174), but it should no longer be needed for co-resident engines. That matters in practice: a raw pool is invisible to torch's memory accounting, so an engine that sizes its KV cache from torch's numbers over-estimates free memory and can OOM later.

This is a different bug from #4921 (which was `init_dist_env` reading `_pool["input"].tensor` on a raw pool); they were both reachable in the same co-resident configuration, which is why the env var looked like the cure.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs on this repo for `custom_all_reduce ipc offset` and `RAW_INPUT_POOL` — no open PR touches `_broadcast_ipc` or the IPC offset. #4921 is closed and addressed a different failure in the same file.

## Tests

`op_tests/test_ipc_base_ptr.py` (new, single-GPU) pins the offset arithmetic: sub-blocks of one allocation share a base and report distinct non-zero offsets; a raw `hipMalloc` buffer is its own base.

`op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_init_dist_env.py` gains a `dirty` mode that leaves a large segment in the caching allocator before `init_dist_env`, so the pool comes back as a sub-block — the shape a co-resident second engine produces incidentally. Each rank's pool offset is reported, so a run that never landed on a sub-block is distinguishable from one that did and handled it; the existing allreduce-correctness check is what proves the result.

**Validated on gfx950 (MI350X)** — full before/after table in [this comment](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5775#issuecomment-5788840837). Summary: three allocator states that put the input pool at a non-zero offset produce **silently wrong** all-reduce results on the unpatched tree and correct results with this patch; states that leave the pool at offset 0 are unaffected either way.

## Note

AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every changed line.

title: [ASM] [HIP] [JIT] [Kernel] [gfx1250] Add F8GEMM 256x256 split-K and 128x128 AP0/AP1 kernels
body:
## Motivation

Support the six gfx1250 MXFP8 x MXFP8 (a8w8) cases with both row-major A (AP0) and preshuffled A (AP1). The 256x256 Split-K kernels expose more parallel work for small-M cases; the 128x128 K128/PF8 kernels serve the `(M,N,K)=(512,8192,1536)` indexer case. Split-K support added by this PR is limited to MXFP8 × MXFP8 (a8w8). MXFP8 × MXFP4 (a8w4) remains unchanged and continues to use a single split.

## Technical Details

- Update five existing files: `aiter/ops/gemm_op_a8w8.py`,`aiter/jit/core.py`, `csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mxfp8fp4gemm.cu`, the existing kernel CSV, and `op_tests/test_mxfp8fp4gemm.py`. Add the tuned config `aiter/configs/asm_mfxp8fp4gemm.csv` and four code objects: 256x256 cluster 4x2 and 128x128 cluster 4x4, each for AP0/AP1.
- Keep the a8w8 interface in `gemm_op_a8w8.py`. When `splitk` is omitted (`None`), the operator looks up the tuned CSV by gfx, M/N/K, `b_intype`, A layout, and output dtype. The six shapes have separate AP0/AP1 entries (12 rows) supplying `kernelName` and `splitK`. The `b_intype` column uses the HSA registry's `mxfp8`/`mxfp4` values; all 12 shipped rows currently use `mxfp8`. Override the config file through `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_MXFP8FP4`.
- A config miss passes an empty kernel name and defaults to `splitk=1`, using the original native dispatch. An explicit positive `splitk` overrides the configured count. An explicit `kernelName` bypasses the CSV and defaults to one split unless `splitk` is also specified. Split counts are literal counts, not log2 values; `splitk=0` is not an automatic-selection mode.
- Split-K (`splitk > 1`) is supported only by the new 256x256 a8w8 kernels, for both AP0 and AP1. The 128x128 a8w8 kernels support `splitk=1` only. The a8w4 API, dispatch, and single-split behavior remain unchanged. Keep the eight original code objects unchanged.
- Supported split counts allocate BF16 partials; the public API sums them and returns `[M,N]`. A local fake implementation preserves the public output shape for `torch.compile`.
- Preserve the 76-byte launch arguments for original kernels and use 80-byte arguments for the four additions. Validate Split-K counts, partition sizes, output capacity, and 128x128 shape restrictions.
- The existing test entry point reuses the operator's config resolution, with no hardcoded six-shape table in either the test or native dispatch. `--splitk` overrides the configured count; `--no-reduce` measures GEMM only and compares BF16 partials to separate partition references. Shared data initialization and timing files are unchanged. Functional mode covers both AP layouts.

## Test Plan

Both the public API and test driver use the following tuned CSV entries when `splitk` is omitted. A config miss uses native dispatch with `splitk=1`.

| Case | M | N | K | Configured Split-K | Tile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| wqkv_a | 512 | 2048 | 7168 | 8 | 256x256 |
| wo_b | 512 | 7168 | 16384 | 4 | 256x256 |
| gate_up_proj | 512 | 6144 | 7168 | 4 | 256x256 |
| w2 | 512 | 7168 | 3072 | 4 | 256x256 |
| wq_b | 512 | 65536 | 1536 | 1 | 256x256 |
| indexer_wq_b | 512 | 8192 | 1536 | 1 | 128x128 |

Run on gfx1250 with a fresh JIT directory after the native-code change. Use a fresh TorchInductor cache when validating the updated optional-argument schema with `torch.compile`:

```bash
python -m op_tests.test_mxfp8fp4gemm --mode func --intype a8w8 --apre 0 1 --shape 512,2048,7168 512,7168,16384 512,6144,7168 512,7168,3072 512,65536,1536 512,8192,1536 --no-reduce --data-init constant uniform --scale-init constant auto --seed 0 --warmup 0 --iters 5 --rotate 1

python -m op_tests.test_mxfp8fp4gemm --mode func --intype a8w8 a8w4 --apre 0 1 --shape 32,2048,2048 128,1280,8192 --data-init constant --scale-init constant --seed 0 --warmup 0 --iters 5 --rotate 1
```

## Test Result

Validation of commit `16857b1b2` used gfx1250 and an isolated TorchInductor cache for compile checks.

- 38/38 constant-input, constant-scale GPU cases passed: 12 six-shape partial-output cases, 12 six-shape reduced-output cases, 8 legacy a8w8/a8w4 regression cases, 4 empty-config fallback cases, and 2 explicit `splitk=1` override cases. All groups cover AP0/AP1.
- An empty CSV supplied through `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_MXFP8FP4` sent both `(512,2048,7168)` and `(512,8192,1536)` back to the original 256x256, 4x4 native dispatch with `splitk=1`.
- Verified all 12 config rows against registered kernels, config hits/misses, explicit split-count overrides, and explicit-kernel bypass behavior.
- Verified that `mxfp8` and `mxfp4` entries for the same shape coexist in one CSV and resolve independently. The shipped table has no `mxfp4` tuning rows; an `mxfp4` lookup returns no config.
- FakeTensor passed. Six actual GPU `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` checks passed with `splitk` omitted: AP0/AP1 for `(512,2048,7168)`, `(512,8192,1536)`, and the config-miss shape `(128,1280,8192)`. Default eager outputs matched the constant-input reference; compiled outputs matched eager outputs exactly. Launch capture confirmed selected kernels, resolved split counts, and partial-buffer shapes.
- Black, Ruff 0.16.0, and whitespace checks passed.

Numerical warnings remain unresolved and tolerances are unchanged. Prior uniform/auto testing at commit `775435acd` reported warnings on all 12 six-shape AP0/AP1 partial-output cases; those inputs were not re-evaluated for this CSV revision. Earlier same-input diagnostics showed that BF16 partition rounding accounts for most of the increased error after reduction, with residual differences. Constant-input and partial-output checks do not establish reduced-output accuracy on uniform inputs.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: MLA v4 nm: faster cross-split merge for small decode grids
body:
## Motivation

In `mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm`, the cross-split merge `_fwd_kernel_stage2_asm` runs one 1-wave CTA per (seq, head) and walks the splits serially. At decode sizes that underfills the GPU: for DeepSeek-V4-Pro at TP8 (16 heads, bs 8, 16 splits), the merge is ~40% of the gap between the fp8 and bf16 decode attention in SGLang's fp8 unified_kv path (sgl-project/sglang#37413).

## Changes

- Add `_fwd_kernel_stage2_dchunk`. It does the same merge, but splits `Lv` over a third grid axis and reduces the splits as one `[MAX_SPLITS, D_CHUNK]` tile. This is the `vec` variant from `test_mla_stage2_merge.py`, chunked so the tile stays small at large split counts.
- `mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm` uses it when `num_seqs * num_heads <= 2048`. Larger grids are bandwidth-bound and keep `_fwd_kernel_stage2_asm` unchanged.
- `test_mla_stage2_merge.py`: add a `dchunk` candidate.

## Results (MI355X)

Merge only (`test_mla_stage2_merge.py`), µs, base → dchunk:

| heads | seqs | 4 splits | 16 splits | 32 splits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 8 | 3.82 → 3.10 | 6.17 → 3.70 | 9.17 → 4.29 |
| 16 | 64 | 4.46 → 3.64 | 8.99 → 5.95 | 18.51 → 13.81 |
| 128 | 8 | 4.42 → 3.83 | 9.20 → 6.15 | 16.80 → 13.75 |

- All 150 cases match the torch reference.
- Inside the dispatch range, dchunk is 1.00–2.27× faster.
- Above it, dchunk would be 0.76–1.02×, which is why the existing kernel is kept there.

End to end, on SGLang with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8, fp8 unified_kv, 8192/1024, c=8 and CUDA graphs: median ITL goes from **13.94 → 13.74 ms** (3 runs each; bf16 reference is 13.36 ms).

## Scope

This is a low-concurrency optimization. At 16 heads, the speedup over the base merge by decode rows T:

| T | merge only | whole v4 nm call |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ 32 | 1.02–1.61× | up to 1.12× |
| 64–128 | 0.98–1.26× | 1.00–1.03× |
| > 128 | not dispatched (unchanged) | unchanged |

With speculative decoding, T is several times the concurrency (6× for DSpark with gamma 5), so there the gain only shows up at small batch.

## Test

```
python3 op_tests/test_mla_stage2_merge.py -b 1 8 16 64 256 --heads 16 128 --splits 2 4 8 16 32
pytest op_tests/test_mla_v4_nm.py   # 11 passed
```

Tested with this diff applied on aiter `4ad998328`, the version in `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260921`. The diff also applies cleanly on main.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add SonicMoE pure-Triton grouped GEMM MoE
body:
## Summary
- Add SonicMoE: a pure-Triton, expert-major grouped GEMM MoE with full autograd.
- Cover top-k routing, general routing, and pre-routed (expert-major) inputs used by Qwen3-style all-to-all dispatch.
- Support GLU and elementwise activations (SWIGLU, GEGLU, REGLU, RELU, RELU_SQ, GELU, SILU) plus optional blockwise FP8 scales on the grouped GEMM.
- Ship gfx942/gfx950 nested `DEFAULT.json` configs, unit tests, and a Triton benchmark.

Public API (`aiter.ops.triton.sonicmoe`):
- `moe_TC_softmax_topk_layer`
- `moe_general_routing_inputs`
- `moe_pre_routed_inputs`

Kernels live under `aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/moe/sonicmoe/`. Autograd wrappers and the public entry points are in `aiter/ops/triton/sonicmoe.py`.

This is the first of two PRs. A follow-up adds an opt-in hipBLASLt / multi-stream grouped GEMM backend. The default path here is Triton-only.

## Test plan

title: [HIP] [FlyDSL] [JIT] Support Conv3d for Qwen-Image / Wan2.1 VAE on MI35X
body:
## Motivation

aiter has no conv3d (only Triton conv2d). Two diffusion VAEs need one:

- **Wan2.1** encodes in 4-frame chunks and prepends 2 cached feature frames
  after the first chunk. Those frames are real, not causal-pad zeros, so the
  `T=1` `conv3d -> conv2d` identity fails. That is **67.7% of one encode's 650
  convolution calls**.
- **Qwen-Image** is the same VAE fine-tuned at `T=1`, where the identity holds,
  so it needs this kernel's 2-D path.

A GEMM library cannot absorb these shapes: N is the 96/192/384 channel ladder,
and 7 of 18 Qwen-Image shapes have `K` not a multiple of 64 or `N=3`, which
A16W16 cannot express.

## Technical Details

### 1. Vendored implicit-GEMM convolution (`flydsl_conv_implicit`)

Same vendoring as `gemm_a16w16_gfx950`. Dispatches 1D/2D/3D off filter rank;
gathers from the source instead of im2col (~9× less activation traffic).
Keyword surface unchanged (`groups`, `padding_mode`, `splitk`, `stream`,
`tile`, `wgm`, `autotune`, `input_layout`, `output_layout`).

Three mechanical edits vs upstream: local `buffer_atomic_add` (flydsl wheel
has no `kernels/common/`); `kt` -> `k_tile` (filter temporal extent); one
`if` collapsed to `and`. 54/56 top-level definitions byte-identical.

Named `flydsl_conv_implicit` because the entry point dispatches on rank.

### 2. Offline tile tuner

The heuristic N tiles are powers of two. Against 96/192/384, two rungs sit at
**75% N occupancy**; masked B columns still issue MFMA. `TILE_N` 96/192 is
legal but was unreachable: `TILE_{M,N} % (16 * WAVE_M * WAVE_N) == 0` excludes
the eight-wave shape every shipped candidate uses.

- `conv3d_policy.py` enumerates that closed form (reject = arithmetic, not a
  compile), then prunes on N fill, waves, LDS, accumulators.
- `csrc/flydsl_conv3d/conv3d_tune.py` writes per-model CSVs under
  `aiter/configs/model_configs/` (`qwenimage_vae_*`, `wan21_vae_*`).
- `_lookup_tuned_tile` reads them. Miss / missing file / malformed row falls
  back to the unmodified heuristic.

Launch config is five integers, not a `solidx` (reordering candidates must not
silently invalidate the table).

**Tune with `--compare --update_improved`.** `mp_tuner` times across eight GPU
processes; production runs one. A bare sweep regressed three shapes by up to
4.8%. The compare gate re-times on the production path and rejects gains below
`--min_improvement_pct` (default 3%).

Also fixes `autotune=True` / `FLYDSL_CONV3D_AUTOTUNE=1`, which imported a
FlyDSL-repo path and raised `ImportError`.

### 3. A16W16 pruner fix

`GemmConfigPruner` `keep_ratio` climbs with M: at M=27556 it kept only tiles
wasting <0.44% on padding. HTI needs `block_n=256`, so N=384 (pad to 512)
dropped the whole HTI catalog (~30% loss). Cap lets a tile pad up to 30%.

### 4. Tests

`op_tests/test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py`: keyword surface plus Wan / Qwen
shapes from an input resolution (`--wan-res`, `--wan-frames`, `--qwen-res`),
traced on meta-device encodes. Benches:
`op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_three_way.py` (conv vs
A16W16 vs hipBLASLt) and `bench_conv_tuned_ab.py` (tile table on vs off).

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py
python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_config_shape_collision -v

PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 csrc/flydsl_conv3d/conv3d_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/model_configs/qwenimage_vae_bf16_untuned_conv3d.csv \
  -o aiter/configs/model_configs/qwenimage_vae_bf16_tuned_conv3d.csv \
  --max_configs 32 --mp 8 --compare --update_improved

PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_three_way.py
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_conv_tuned_ab.py
```

All results below: gfx950 / 256 CU, bf16.

## Test Result

### Correctness

`test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py`: **75/75 `checkAllclose`**, `rtol=atol=2e-2`.
`flydsl err` **0 on all 33 model shapes** (the one non-zero cell is torch's
own bf16 rounding at K=27, `err_ratio` 4e-05).

`test_config_shape_collision.py`: 18/18, including `conv3d_bf16_tuned`.

Every tuned row has `err_ratio = 0.0`. Instrumenting `_lookup_tuned_tile`
over the op_test: **1236 hits / 12 distinct shapes**, all non-default tiles
(e.g. `(96, 96, 2, 3)`, `(192, 128, 2, 2)`, `(128, 192, 1, 4) wgm=8`).

### Performance (gfx950 / 256 CU, bf16)

One table for the published buckets. **vs X** is `X_ms / current CSV` (or
`torch / orig flydsl` only where current is missing). Torch and original
flydsl † are the PR-open three-way (NCHW, includes pre-transpose). hip is
`three_way.json` library-best `torch.mm` on materialised `M×K` (no im2col).
Current CSV is NDHWC (`ed7b5a5a8`). ‡ NCDHW-tuned CSV (`05f919868`). Mixed
sessions; hip/a16 traffic is not the conv gather.

| bucket | torch | orig flydsl | hip | current CSV | vs orig flydsl | vs hip | vs torch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan2.1 `T>1`/cached, 480×832, 81f (8 shapes, 440 calls) | 505.32 ms | 310.37 ms † | — | **200.91 ms** | **1.55x** | — | **2.52x** |
| Wan2.1 same 8, 368×544, 81f | — | 128.70 ms ‡ | — | **110.43 ms** | **1.17x** | — | — |
| Qwen-Image, 1024² (10 shapes, 52 calls) | 20.37 ms | 12.00 ms † | 8.70 ms | **7.76 ms** | **1.55x** | **1.12x** | **2.63x** |
| Qwen-Image, 1024² (16 layers, 58 calls) | — | — | 10.02 ms | **8.92 ms** | — | **1.12x** | — |
| Qwen-Image, 1328² (10 shapes, 52 calls) | — | 16.13 ms ‡ | — | **12.68 ms** | **1.27x** | — | — |
| Wan2.1 resamplers + pointwise (15 shapes) | 34.67 ms | 32.07 ms † | — | — | — | — | 1.08x † |

† Three-way at PR open (NCHW in). Orig flydsl vs torch on that row is **1.63x**
(Wan 8-shape) / **1.70x** (Qwen 10-shape) / **1.08x** (resamplers). Wan conv3d
matches the Lumen 81-frame report (1.59x). Minus the two `time_conv`, the
pointwise bucket is 0.99x (stay on torch); `time_conv` alone is 1.54x
(`3x1x1`, `K=C*3`). `time_conv` is not in the tuned tables, so the 15-shape
row has no current CSV. Hip was not measured for Wan T>1 (A up to ~8 GB,
omits 27× im2col). Qwen 1328² hip exists for only 2 of 10 shapes.

CSV rows outside those buckets (same weighting):

| | resample 3×3 (6 shapes, 63 calls) | decode extras (8 shapes, 103 calls) | all CSV rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan 480×832 | 6.69 ms | 41.88 ms | 249.49 ms (22 shapes, 606 calls) |
| Wan 368×544 | 4.02 ms | 21.92 ms | 136.36 ms |
| Qwen 1024², 16 layers (adds 3 downs + 3 ups) | — | — | 8.92 ms (58 calls) |
| Qwen 1328², 16 layers | — | — | 14.63 ms |

#### Wan2.1 `T>1`/cached conv3d, weighted (81 frames)

| shape | calls | 480×832 `us` | 480 contrib | 368×544 `us` | 368 contrib |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `conv_in` 3→96 | 20 | 183.46 | 3.67 ms | 114.62 | 2.29 ms |
| `down_0_1` 96→96 | 80 | 1017.87 | 81.43 ms | 515.87 | 41.27 ms |
| `down_3_in` 96→192 | 20 | 469.12 | 9.38 ms | 245.18 | 4.90 ms |
| `down_3_4` 192→192 | 60 | 907.95 | 54.48 ms | 467.67 | 28.06 ms |
| `down_6_in` 192→384 | 20 | 226.62 | 4.53 ms | 128.58 | 2.57 ms |
| `down_6_7` 384→384 | 60 | 456.06 | 27.36 ms | 247.35 | 14.84 ms |
| `down_9_10_mid` 384→384 | 160 | 114.82 | 18.37 ms | 92.70 | 14.83 ms |
| `conv_out` 384→32 | 20 | 84.46 | 1.69 ms | 82.91 | 1.66 ms |
| **weighted** | **440** | | **200.91 ms** | | **110.43 ms** |

#### Qwen-Image conv2d, weighted (one encode+decode)

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Kernel] Add 32x32 block-scaled MXFP4 quantization
body:
## Summary

- Add `dynamic_mxfp4_quant_blockscale`, which uses one deterministic EVEN E8M0 scale per 32 x 32 input tile.
- Return row-major packed E2M1 bytes with shape `(M, N / 2)` and raw E8M0 scales with shape `(M / 32, N / 32)`.
- Reuse the existing MXFP4 E8M0 conversion and E2M1 packing helpers in `quant.py`.
- Include kernel `repr`, bit-exact unit tests, and a runnable benchmark.

The existing `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` uses independent 1 x 32 row scales, so it cannot provide the transpose-invariant 32 x 32 scale semantics of this operator. The fixed tile is part of the output contract rather than an architecture-specific tuning choice.

Closes #5547.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Merge MoE MXFP8 GEMM into existing _moe_gemm_a8w8 kernel
body:
## Summary

  Follow-up to #5310. Per reviewer request, removes the standalone `_moe_gemm_mxfp8_kernel` and reuses the existing `_moe_gemm_a8w8` kernel for MXFP8 MoE GEMM.

  The two kernels share the same computation structure. The only difference is the FP8 format: `_moe_gemm_a8w8` uses OCP `float8e4nv` (gfx950) while `moe_gemm_mxfp8` needs AMD fnuz `float8_e4m3fnuz` (gfx942). A new `USE_FNUZ: tl.constexpr` flag handles this: when `True`, it replaces `tl.dot_scaled` (OCP-only) with manual E8M0→fp32 dequant + `tl.dot`.

  ## Changes

  - `_moe_gemm_a8w8`: add `USE_FNUZ=False` constexpr (default preserves current behavior). Relax FP8 dtype assert to accept fnuz when `USE_FNUZ=True`. Fix bias dtype mismatch in SPLIT_K>1 else-branch.
  - `moe_gemm_mxfp8` wrapper: route through `_moe_gemm_a8w8(USE_FNUZ=True)`. Tile params moved out of Python into `configs/gfx942/triton/moe/mxfp8_fnuz/DEFAULT.json`.
  - `moe_utils.py`: add `group_sizes_to_expt_tensors()` to convert the `group_sizes` routing interface to the `ExptHist/ExptOffs/ExptData` format expected by `_moe_gemm_a8w8`.
  - Delete `_triton_kernels/moe/moe_gemm_mxfp8.py` (the duplicate kernel).

  ## Test results

  773 passed, 576 skipped (gfx942 does not support OCP FP8 blockscale configs) on MI308X (gfx942).

  Tested: `test_moe_gemm_mxfp8`, `test_moe_gemm_a8w8`, `test_moe_gemm_a8w8_blockscale`.

title: [HIP] [Activation] Add standalone relu2 (Squared ReLU) elementwise kernel for non-gated MoE MLPs
body:
## Motivation

NemotronH's non-gated MoE MLP layers use Squared ReLU (`relu(x)^2`) as their activation function. aiter currently only implements *gated* activations (`silu_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul`) and a plain (non-gated) `gelu_fast`, but has no plain Squared ReLU op. 

Improving performance for the ``NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-BF16`` model requires enabling relu2, fused MoE GEMM support, and vLLM AITER backend integration. This PR's scope is limited to enabling relu2.

This PR adds a standalone `relu2` elementwise kernel so non-gated MoE architectures like NemotronH can use aiter's fused activation path instead of falling back to eager PyTorch.

This is Tier 1 of a 3-PR series adding end-to-end relu2 support:
1. **This PR** standalone aiter elementwise kernel (no dependencies)
2. aiter CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM support for relu2 (depends on this PR). The draft [PR](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5708) is ready.
3. vLLM AITER backend integration (depends on the Tier 2 PR above)

**Note**: For end-to-end results and performance, refer to the related Tier 2 and Tier 3 PRs.

## Technical Details

Mirrors the existing `gelu_fast` pattern end-to-end:

- Declared the `relu2(out, input)` op signature alongside the other elementwise activations
- Implemented `relu2_kernel<T>` (`r = max(x, 0); return r * r`, computed in fp32) and its launcher, using the same vectorized launch macro as the other elementwise activations
- Added explicit tensor validation (GPU, contiguous, matching numel/dtype/device) before dispatch
- Added the pybind11 binding so the op is exposed to Python
- Added the Python-side `@compile_ops(...)` stub (JIT-compiled on first call, same as all other activation ops)
- Added `test_relu2` plus a driver loop matching the existing `test_gelu_fast` benchmark pattern

No changes to gated/MoE-fused activation paths, this is a plain elementwise op only.

## Test Plan

Validated on MI350 (gfx950):

- **Correctness**: compared `aiter.relu2(out, x)` against a  `torch.nn.functional.relu(x.float())**2` reference across 4 shapes:
  (1024,4096), (1024,8192), (4096,4096), (4096,8192), bf16 dtype.
- **Performance**: benchmarked `aiter.relu2` vs. the same eager PyTorch reference across the same 4 shapes.

## Test Result

| M    | N    | aiter_us | torch_us | speedup | max_abs_diff | result |
|------|------|----------|----------|---------|--------------|--------|
| 1024 | 4096 | 8.038    | 22.051   | 2.74x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |
| 1024 | 8192 | 7.858    | 31.297   | 3.98x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |
| 4096 | 4096 | 13.158   | 55.536   | 4.22x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |
| 4096 | 8192 | 21.431   | 107.907  | 5.04x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |

Exact-match correctness (`max_abs_diff: 0.0`) and 2.74x–5.04x speedup
vs. eager PyTorch across all tested shapes.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Bugfix] [Perf] Support page size 8 in paged MQA logits on both layouts, and fix large KV offsets
body:
## Problem

On `main` the non-preshuffle ("plain") Gluon paged MQA logits kernel has no block-paging path at all: it indexes `kv_indices` with the *token* position, which is only correct when `KVBlockSize == 1`. A KV cache paged at more than one token per page therefore reads the wrong pages — and nothing rejects it, because `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` only asserts `KVBlockSize == 1` on gfx1250. On gfx942/gfx950 a paged cache is silently mis-scored rather than refused. The preshuffle path cannot stand in for it either: it requires `KVBlockSize % 16 == 0`, because the shuffled KV feeds the 16-token MFMA B operand directly and a page of 8 is half a tile.

That leaves **page size 8** — what DeepSeek V4.1 decode uses for the indexer KV cache — unreachable on `main` on either layout.

Separately, both paths form KV and FP32-scale addresses through 32-bit strides, so a cache past the 2 GiB buffer-descriptor range wraps; and the preshuffle logits store is not bounded by `max_model_len`, so a short final chunk spills into the next output row.

These are all silent-wrong-answer bugs: the indexer logits feed a top-k, so a corrupted tail turns into wrong sparse-KV indices rather than a crash.

## What this changes

### Plain path

- **Block paging in the plain kernel.** Derive the page index as `token // KVBlockSize` and the in-page offset as `token % KVBlockSize`, instead of treating the token position as a page index. The backward-shifted first tile can carry negative positions, so those lanes are clamped to token 0 of page 0 before the offset is formed, including for the scale.
- **64-bit KV addressing on the plain path.** `stride_k_seq` and `stride_scale_seq` become `i64`, and the K and scale reads become global loads, so a cache beyond 2 GiB still addresses correctly. The plain path builds per-token addresses from the page table, so the 32-bit stride product was the overflow site.
- **Preshuffle large offsets and tail store.** Widen the page index to 64 bit before scaling by the stride, and bound the logits store by `max_model_len` so a short final chunk cannot reach into the next row.

### Preshuffle path

Page 8 on the plain path works but is the slow layout. No new load structure is needed to reach the fast one: the per-lane page index already varies at `KVBlockSize` granularity, and a page shorter than `ChunkK // 2` already takes the "page index per lane" branch, so the two pages behind one tile are already addressable. What was hardcoded is the shuffle group.

- **`ShuffleRows = min(KVBlockSize, 16)`** in both `_gluon_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` and its `_varctx` twin, replacing the literal 16 in the B-operand offset. One tile is then assembled from two pages.
- **The wrapper admits 8**, and only 8, below the tile size. The addressing generalises to any page that divides 16, and pages 1, 2 and 4 do run correctly — max abs error 0.0043 to 0.0058 against FP32, the same band as page 16, and faster than plain at the same page size (on a one-off probe, page 1: 271.0 us vs 398.1 us; page 4: 189.2 us vs 287.7 us). They stay rejected because no caller asks for them and the sweep does not cover them. gfx1250 preshuffle reshapes by a literal `KVBlockSize // 16` for its TDM block load, so pages below 16 stay rejected there outright.
- **The row-group stride** goes from a literal `16 * 128` to `ShuffleRows * HiddenDim` to stay consistent with the above. This is not what makes page 8 work — a page that short holds one group, so the term is zero either way — and at `HiddenDim` 128 the two expressions are equal. No configuration a caller can reach today changes; every caller runs `HiddenDim` 128.
- **The bench gets the host side of this.** `--kv_preshuffle` used to fall back to plain whenever the page was not a multiple of 16, quietly reporting the wrong path, and it shuffled at a fixed 16 rows. It now honours the flag, derives the layout from the page size, and reports `kv_tokens` so a run can be turned into bandwidth. Defaults do not move: 16 preshuffled, 1 plain.

**Caller-visible:** a page of 8 must be shuffled in groups of its own length, `shuffle_weight(kv, layout=(8, 16))`, rather than the default `(16, 16)`. Getting this wrong is not silent — `shuffle_weight` asserts `shape[-2] % 16 == 0` on the default layout.

## Performance

Measured with the bench in this PR on gfx950, heads 32 / head-dim 128, three shapes x two layouts x page 8/16, three rounds per point with the arms rotated inside a round, medians below. Round-to-round spread is under 1.9 us everywhere. The rows below carry a 286 MB working set, past the 256 MB MALL, so their TB/s is DRAM-bound; the other two shapes fit in MALL and their TB/s is not an HBM figure.

batch 16, next_n 1, 1M context:

| page | path | latency | effective BW |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 8 | plain | 431.384 us | 5.125 TB/s |
| 16 | plain | 410.064 us | 5.382 TB/s |
| 8 | **preshuffle** | **379.863 us** | **5.820 TB/s** |
| 16 | preshuffle | 359.784 us | 6.134 TB/s |

Halving the page costs 5.58% here, and 3.01% to 5.20% across the five other shape and layout pairs. Both layouts move together, so what is paid for is the page and not the shuffle: one tile's contiguous run drops from 256 B to 128 B, and the page table doubles in width. The page table is 0.18% of the byte model, which leaves the contiguity.

That cost does not change what a page-8 caller should do, because page 16 is not one of its options. Against the only alternative it has — page-8 plain — preshuffle is **11.9% faster**, and it also beats page-16 plain by 7.4%. The speedup preshuffle already had is essentially kept at the smaller page: 1.096x to 1.692x over plain at page 16, 1.088x to 1.664x at page 8 across the three shapes.

## Testing

`op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py`, 105 cases, all passing on gfx950 (MI35x):

- `test_paged_mqa_logits_non_preshuffle` — block sizes 1 / **8** / 16 / 64 / 128 x ChunkK 64 / 256 x compact / padded page tables x the decode and MTP shapes. Compact tables expose token-indexed out-of-bounds reads; padded tables keep those reads in allocated memory and expose wrong scores instead. Output rows are sentinel-guarded on both sides so a store that walks off a row is caught.
- `test_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` — new, and the sweep the preshuffle path never had; previously only the large-KV-offset cases reached it, all at the default ChunkK. Pages **8** / 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 x ChunkK 128 / 256 x compact / padded tables x the decode and MTP shapes. The page sizes pick out how the B tile gets assembled: 8 is half a tile and draws from two pages, 16 is exactly one, 32 through 128 are several row groups inside one page, and 256 exceeds `ChunkK // 2` and so takes the one-page-per-stage branch. ChunkK 128 and 256 are the two the callers ask for — the bench runs preshuffle at 128, the indexer at 256.
- `test_paged_mqa_logits_large_kv_offsets` — plain and preshuffle, including a `preshuffle-B8` row, with the referenced pages placed around the 2 / 4 / 8 GiB boundaries, so the offset arithmetic is exercised without allocating a multi-GiB reference.
- `test_paged_mqa_logits_wide_output_no_tail_drop` — the dense `[rows, 1<<20]` layout whose row 512 store lands exactly on 2**31 bytes.

Everything is compared against an FP32 reference built from the same FP8 inputs. Before the preshuffle commit, the 8 page-8 rows of the new sweep fail — rejected by the wrapper before they reach the device — and the other 40 pass unchanged.

The bench was run in all three configurations it can take — `--kv_preshuffle` (page 16), `--kv_preshuffle --blocksize 8`, and plain (page 1) — with `logits_diff` at 0.00046 to 0.00047 in each.

## Relationship to #5614

#5614 carries the plain-path fixes plus a batch of decode-grid and persistent-CTA perf work, and its review surface has grown accordingly. This PR is page size 8 on both layouts, plus the addressing bugs in the way of it, split out so it reaches `main` without waiting on that perf review. The decode-grid and persistent-CTA commits stay in #5614.

The preshuffle half arrived here through #5768, which was merged into this branch rather than reviewed separately.

title: [ASM] [HIP] MLA PS mode asm and opus kernel support nhead12,8
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950, fp8/fp8 MLA persistent decode only accepted head counts that are 16 or a multiple
of 16 (16 / 32 / 64 / 96 / 128). Anything else was either folded down to 16 heads — which is
only possible when `num_heads % 16 == 0` — or rejected outright by
`get_mla_metadata_v1_2_device`. A model with 12 query heads per KV head therefore had no path
at all, on either the asm or the opus kernel.

This PR makes both kernels accept head counts that are not a multiple of 16.

## Technical Details

### Why a non-multiple-of-16 head count broke the causal mask

Both kernels give each wave a fixed tile of packed Q rows — `W_M = 16` for the opus 16mx8
kernel, `SUB_Q = 32` for the asm qh32 kernel — and packed row `p` belongs to query token
`p / nhead`. While `nhead` is a multiple of that tile, every row of a wave lands on the same
token, so the causal bound is wave-uniform and lives in an SGPR:

```cpp
diag_kv_bound = (warp_id * T::W_M) / nhead + causal_diagonal;
```

With `nhead = 12` a token boundary falls *inside* a wave: rows 0–11 of warp 0 are token 0,
rows 12–15 are token 1. All 16 rows still got token 0's bound, so 4 of every 16 query rows
were masked one KV column too early. The bound has to be per lane:

```cpp
row = warp_id * T::W_M + lane_id % T::W_M;   // lane_id % W_M is the MFMA M index,
diag_kv_bound = row / nhead + causal_diagonal;   // same one make_layout_o and the LSE store use
```

Measured on the unmodified opus kernel, `-n 12,8` over the default grid: **16 of 64 cells
failed**, max |delta| 2.58 with 33% of elements off. The asm kernel had the same defect.

- **asm (SP3 `MLA_A8W8_QH32_1TG_4W_32mx4_64nx1_PS`)**: a third branch in `causal_mask` computes
  the token per lane with a `v_rcp_f32` divide plus a 1/256 bias before the truncating convert
  (`p < 128` and `gqa_ratio <= 128`, so `p/gqa_ratio` is either integral or at least 1/128 from
  the next integer, which absorbs the ≤1ulp reciprocal error in both directions). The existing
  fast paths — `gqa_ratio` a multiple of `SUB_Q`, and `gqa_ratio == 16` — are kept and take the
  same instructions as before. Only the four rebuilt `.co` files are in this PR; the SP3 source
  lives in a separate repo.
- **opus (`mla_decode_fp8_16mx8_32nx1.hpp`)**: `causal_kv_bound` takes `lane_id` and is gated on
  a new compile-time trait `WAVE_SPANS_TOKENS`, which the host sets from `H % W_M != 0`. Head
  counts that are a multiple of `W_M` keep the wave-uniform SGPR form, so their codegen is
  untouched; only the new head counts pay the extra live VGPR in a kernel that already sits at
  256.

### The causal diagonal is not confined to the last KV tile

A work item's bounds span its `q_len` columns ending at `valid_kv_len - 1`, so they sit inside
the last KV tile only when `valid_kv_len % KV_TILE_SIZE >= q_len`. Otherwise they reach back
into the previous tile, which `tile_idx == tile_end - 1` left unmasked, and the rows bounded
there attended past their diagonal. With only the per-lane fix applied, `-n 12,8 -c 33` still
**failed** at max |delta| 1.41 over 58% of elements.

`mask_oob_scores` now masks the last two tiles. Two is always enough: a work item holds at most
128 packed rows over at least 4 heads, so `q_len <= 32 == KV_TILE_SIZE`. Deriving the exact tile
set from `causal_diagonal` instead was tried and is slower — it keeps `causal_diagonal` live for
every tile's test, which measured −0.7% across the existing shapes versus −0.3% for the fixed
two-tile window.

This defect predates the PR and applies to every causal shape; the default test grid never hit
it because all of its ctx values are ≡ 0 or ≥ q_len mod 32.

### Dispatch and metadata

The same predicate is added in the five places that have to agree, alongside the existing
`natively_supported` clauses:

```
arch == gfx950 && q_fp8 && kv_fp8 && (nhead % 16 != 0) && (nhead * max_seqlen_qo <= 128)
```

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `csrc/kernels/mla/metadata/v1_2_device.cuh` | metadata `natively_supported` (no head folding) |
| `csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mla.cu` | routes to the qh32 kernel: `config_gqa_ratio = 32`, `config_max_seqlen_q = 4`, real gqa in `args.s_MQA` |
| `aiter/ops/attention.py` | metadata buffer sizing + `decode_update_mla_metadata_v1` |
| `aiter/mla.py` | `mla_decode_fwd` native-support check |
| `op_tests/test_mla_persistent.py` | the reference path's matching check |

Two smaller pieces:

- `csrc/kernels/mla/reduce.cu` gains the `(12 heads, 512 dim)` instantiation; the dispatch table
  is a whitelist and 12 was not in it.
- `get_mla_metadata_info_v1`'s `assert num_head_qo % 8 == 0` is relaxed to `% 4`. Nothing in that
  function divides by the head count — it only sizes buffers.

`opus_mla_decode_fwd.cu` needs no head-count gate of its own; the metadata check upstream of it
is the gate, and `WAVE_SPANS_TOKENS` is picked from the runtime `H`.

### Supported range

128 is what one work item holds: 8 waves × `W_M` 16 for opus, 4 waves × `SUB_Q` 32 for asm. The
gate is deliberately `nhead * max_seqlen_qo <= 128` — i.e. one qo tile per batch — rather than a
per-tile test, because the metadata splits qo tiles in *tokens*: `ceil(packed / 128)` tiles of
`ceil(seqlen_qo / tiles)` tokens. Two ceilings in a row can hand back a tile over the limit
(12 heads × 21 tokens → 2 tiles of 11 tokens = 132 rows), which the kernels would silently
truncate. Keeping the batch inside a single tile avoids that case entirely.

Combinations outside the range are rejected at metadata with the existing "only supports #heads
…" error rather than producing wrong results.

## Test Plan

```bash
# new head counts + the established shapes, both kernels, full default grid
for n in 12,8 12,6 16,8 32,4 64,2 128,2; do
  for opus in 0 1; do
    AITER_MLA_USE_OPUS=$opus python3 op_tests/test_mla_persistent.py -d fp8 -kvd fp8 -n $n
  done
done

# against origin/main, same grid, 3 reps, both kernels
AITER_MLA_USE_OPUS={0,1} python3 op_tests/test_mla_persistent.py -d fp8 -kvd fp8 \
    -n {12,8|12,6|24,8|16,8|32,4|64,2|128,2} -b 16 32 64 -c 5200 8192 16384 65535
```

Verdicts below are against the `golden fp8` reference — the one that quantises the same way the
kernel does. gfx950 / MI355X, ROCm 7.1.

## Test Result

### Accuracy, full default grid

`-b 1 3 5 16 32 64 128 256` × `-c 21 64 256 512 1200 3200 5200 8192`, 64 cells per shape.

| shape | asm passed / warn / **failed** | max abs delta | opus passed / warn / **failed** | max abs delta |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| **12,8** | 37 / 27 / **0** | 0.055 | 31 / 33 / **0** | 0.094 |
| **12,6** | 38 / 26 / **0** | 0.070 | 35 / 29 / **0** | 0.086 |
| 16,8 | 35 / 29 / **0** | 0.051 | 31 / 33 / **0** | 0.094 |
| 32,4 | 33 / 31 / **0** | 0.047 | 29 / 35 / **0** | 0.109 |
| 64,2 | 34 / 30 / **0** | 0.055 | 32 / 32 / **0** | 0.086 |
| 128,2 | 36 / 28 / **0** | 0.043 | 28 / 36 / **0** | 0.109 |

`12,4` and `24,4` were also run over the full grid: 0 failed on both kernels. `24,8` is rejected
at metadata (24 × 8 = 192 > 128), as intended.

Before the fix, for reference: `12,8` opus **16 / 64 cells failed**, max |delta| 2.58;
`12,4` opus **16 / 64 failed**, max |delta| 2.88.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Perf] Support page size 8 in the preshuffle MQA logits kernel
body:
## Problem

DeepSeek V4.1 decode pages the indexer KV cache at 8 tokens per page. #5749 makes that page size *work*, but only on the plain (non-preshuffle) path, which is the slow one. Preshuffle is refused outright:

```python
assert KVBlockSize % 16 == 0, "Preshuffle mode only supports KVBlockSize aligned to 16."
```

The shuffled KV feeds the 16-token MFMA B operand directly, and a page of 8 is half a tile, with the other half in a physically unrelated page.

This is not hypothetical. ATOM's V4.1 index scorer already calls this op with `Preshuffle=True` (`atom/model_ops/deepseek_v41/paged_scoring.py`), and its `candidate_block_size` is 8, so the plain-path fix alone does not reach it.

## What this changes

No new load structure is needed. The per-lane page index already varies at `KVBlockSize` granularity, and a page shorter than `ChunkK // 2` already takes the "page index per lane" branch, so the two pages behind one tile are already addressable. What was hardcoded is the shuffle group: the B-operand offset assumed 16 rows per group.

- **`ShuffleRows = min(KVBlockSize, 16)`** in both `_gluon_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` and its `_varctx` twin, replacing the literal 16 in the B-operand offset. The tile is then assembled from `16 // KVBlockSize` pages.
- **The wrapper accepts a page that divides the tile**, not only one that is a multiple of it. gfx1250 preshuffle reshapes by a literal `KVBlockSize // 16` for its TDM block load, so pages below 16 stay rejected there rather than mis-addressed.
- **The row-group stride** goes from a literal `16 * 128` to `ShuffleRows * HiddenDim` to stay consistent with the above. This is not what makes page 8 work — a page that short holds one group, so the term is zero either way — and at `HiddenDim` 128 the two expressions are equal. No configuration a caller can reach today changes; every caller runs `HiddenDim` 128.
- **The benchmark can now express a page-8 run.** `--blocksize` applied only to the preshuffle path and had to be a multiple of 16, `Preshuffle` was inferred from it rather than taken from the flag, and the host shuffle used the default `(16, 16)` layout. Those are the same assumptions the kernel drops. It also records the scored token count, which a bandwidth figure needs.

**Caller-visible:** a page below 16 must be shuffled in groups of its own length, `shuffle_weight(kv, layout=(KVBlockSize, 16))`, rather than the default `(16, 16)`.

## Performance

gfx950, heads 32 / head-dim 128, via `op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_deepgemm_attention.py`. Three rounds per point with the arms rotated inside a round, medians below; round-to-round spread is under 1.9 us everywhere. Every point passes the benchmark's own FP32 reference check, and the four arms of a row share a seed, so their context lengths and page tables are identical.

The rows below carry a 286 MB KV working set, past this card's 256 MB MALL, so their TB/s is DRAM-bound.

**batch 16, next_n 1, 1M context**

| page | layout | latency | effective BW |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 8 | plain | 431.384 us | 5.125 TB/s |
| 16 | plain | 410.064 us | 5.382 TB/s |
| 8 | **preshuffle** | **379.863 us** | **5.820 TB/s** |
| 16 | preshuffle | 359.784 us | 6.134 TB/s |

**Halving the page is not free: it costs 5.58% here**, and 3.01% to 5.20% across the five other shape and layout pairs measured (batch 32 / next_n 2 / 128K and batch 128 / next_n 1 / 128K, each on both layouts). Plain and preshuffle move together, so what is being paid for is the page and not the shuffle — one tile's contiguous run drops from 256 B to 128 B, and the page table doubles in width. The page table is 0.18% of the byte model, which leaves the contiguity.

That cost does not change what a page-8 caller should do, because page 16 is not one of its options. Against the only alternative it has, page-8 plain, **preshuffle is 11.9% faster**, and it also beats page-16 plain by 7.4%. The preshuffle speedup itself barely changes with the page: 1.140x / 1.692x / 1.096x at page 16 against 1.136x / 1.664x / 1.088x at page 8, over the three shapes.

An earlier revision of this PR claimed page-8 and page-16 preshuffle were level. That came from a single point measured with a throwaway probe whose KV allocation differed from the benchmark's; the numbers above replace it.

## Testing

`op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py`, 105 cases, all passing on gfx950 (MI35x).

The new `test_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` gives the preshuffle path the sweep the plain one already had — previously only the large-KV-offset cases reached it, all at the default ChunkK. It covers pages 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 x ChunkK 128 / 256 x compact / padded page tables x the decode and MTP shapes, 48 cases, against an FP32 reference built from the same FP8 inputs, with the output rows sentinel-guarded on both sides.

The page sizes pick out the ways the B tile gets assembled: 8 is half a tile and draws from two pages, 16 is exactly one, 32 through 128 are several row groups inside one page, and 256 exceeds `ChunkK // 2` and so takes the one-page-per-stage branch. ChunkK 128 and 256 are the two the callers ask for — the bench runs preshuffle at 128, the indexer at 256.

Against the parent commit the 8 page-8 rows fail, rejected by the wrapper before they reach the device, and the other 40 pass unchanged. `test_paged_mqa_logits_large_kv_offsets` also picks up a `preshuffle-B8` row at the 2 / 4 / 8 GiB boundaries.

## Relationship to #5749

Stacked on #5749, which is the plain-path half of the same page-8 requirement. Only the top two commits belong to this PR; please review it after #5749 lands, or with base set to that branch.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Perf] Add persistent CTA scheduling for paged FP8 MQA decode
body:
## Summary

This re-opens the same single commit as #5723. That PR was merged into #5614's branch, then the branch was rolled back to `95e292923` so this change can be reviewed on its own instead of being folded into #5614. Commit content is unchanged.

Add a reusable, GPU-built persistent CTA schedule for paged FP8 MQA decode logits. `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_persistent_schedule` builds a `[CTA, 4]` work table once; passing it as `PersistentSchedule` makes the compute kernel read its tile from that table instead of deriving it from `pid`. Work is balanced across variable-length contexts, so one long sequence no longer strands the rest of the grid.

This PR targets **#5614's branch**, `zhiding512/fix-paged-mqa-block-paging-20260917`, based on `95e292923`.

## Motivation

The regular SplitKV path maps CTAs per (batch, query, head tile, split). With ragged or skewed contexts most CTAs finish early and idle behind the longest sequence. The schedule finds the smallest per-CTA chunk budget whose CTA count still fits the grid, gives empty sequences no slots, and balances chunks within each sequence so its last CTA is not a short straggler.

## Changes

- Add `_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_persistent_schedule` and the `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_persistent_schedule` helper. The table can be rebuilt in place into an existing buffer, and stays valid while `context_lens` is unchanged.
- Add a `PERSISTENT` compile-time branch to both the plain and preshuffle Gluon compute kernels; tiles are read through `_load_persistent_mqa_tile`. The regular path is untouched.
- Specialize the persistent query count; cover MTP causal masks in every stage, output guards, zero contexts and large KV offsets.
- Persistent AOT binaries use a distinct `_persistent` name.

This PR carries the kernel and dispatch changes only. Tests and the benchmark harness are kept out to keep the diff reviewable; the validation they produced is summarized below.

## Performance

gfx950 / 256 CU; H=32, D=128, next_n=1, KVBlockSize=64, ChunkK=256, WavePerEU=2, output bound 131072. Six alternating-order rounds, median; CPU work and output initialization excluded. `schedule` is the table build measured on its own — the kernel column excludes it because the table is reusable across calls that share `context_lens`.

Uniform context 131072, plain layout, helper-default CTA counts:

| Batch | CTAs | baseline μs | persistent kernel μs | schedule μs | kernel change |
| ----: | ---: | ----------: | -------------------: | ----------: | ------------: |
| 1     | 512  | 6.774       | 6.396                | 1.823       | -5.58%        |
| 4     | 512  | 15.942      | 16.140               | 2.428       | +1.24%        |
| 16    | 512  | 46.084      | 45.907               | 2.417       | -0.38%        |
| 64    | 1024 | 232.865     | 227.337              | 2.401       | -2.37%        |
| 128   | 2048 | 398.570     | 395.846              | 1.886       | -0.68%        |

Variable-length contexts, where the schedule actually pays off. `ragged` is `ctx[0]=0`, `ctx[i]=(i+1)*131072//128`; `skewed` is one 131072-token sequence plus 257-token sequences:

| Workload         | Layout     | baseline μs | persistent kernel μs | kernel change |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ----------: | -------------------: | ------------: |
| B16 skewed       | plain      | 31.403      | 8.545                | -72.79%       |
| B16 skewed       | preshuffle | 21.441      | 6.257                | -70.82%       |
| B128 skewed      | plain      | 110.212     | 9.100                | -91.74%       |
| B128 skewed      | preshuffle | 72.325      | 6.655                | -90.80%       |
| B128 ragged      | plain      | 266.589     | 209.158              | -21.54%       |
| B128 ragged      | preshuffle | 270.079     | 228.483              | -15.40%       |
| B64 uniform 4096 | plain      | 10.957      | 11.385               | +3.90%        |
| B64 uniform 4096 | preshuffle | 8.438       | 8.748                | +3.68%        |

Two caveats for callers. Uniform long contexts gain at most about 2%, so the schedule is not worth it there. Rebuilding the table on every call costs a fixed 1.8–2.4 μs that does not scale with the workload, which dominates at small batch — B1 plain goes from 6.396 to 8.219 μs end to end. Build the table once per decode step and reuse it across layers while contexts are unchanged.

Measured on ROCm device 6 with unlocked clocks using a local harness that is not part of this PR; absolute values are not comparable with earlier reports on other devices, but all variants within a row were timed in one process on the same inputs in alternating order.

## Testing

No test files are touched by this PR. The existing suite is unaffected, and the new path was validated with a separate local suite that is not included here.

- [x] **62 passed** — `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py` on gfx950, unmodified, confirming the regular SplitKV path is unchanged.
- [x] **47 passed** — local persistent suite: schedule reuse after changing contexts inside one CUDA Graph, random physical pages, per-token scales, compact and padded page tables, zero contexts, short tails, `KVBlockSize > ChunkK`, 2/4/8 GiB KV address boundaries, output row offsets across 2 GiB, output guards, and `next_n=65/129` cross-stage MTP.
- [x] AOT load verified for plain and preshuffle with `next_n=3`, including the distinct `_persistent` name.
- [x] Every benchmark variant above was checked against the full FP32 reference before timing: 0 mismatches.
- [x] Black, Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] gfx942 hardware validation (not available in this session).

Happy to bring the persistent tests and the benchmark in as a follow-up PR, or fold them back into this one if reviewers prefer them together.

## Dependencies

Depends on #5614. No new third-party dependencies.

## Breaking Changes

None intended. `PersistentSchedule` defaults to `None` and the regular SplitKV path is unchanged. The persistent entry point requires Triton >= 3.5 and gfx942/gfx950.

title: [HIP] Fix grouped topk tie handling for GLM-5.2 accuracy
body: ## Motivation PR [#5632](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5632) added a register-resident kernel for the single-group Top-K path. However, its output did not exactly match the original `grouped_topk_kernel`: ties at the Top-K cutoff could change the selected expert set, and the selected experts and weights could be emitted in a different order. This changed downstream floating-point accumulation and caused an accuracy regression on GLM-5.2. This PR makes the register-resident kernel match `grouped_topk_kernel` exactly, including selected expert IDs, output order, and weights, while retaining the register-resident fast path. ## Technical details - Retain the register-resident fast path introduced in #5632. - Emit experts in the same score order as the legacy kernel. - When multiple experts have equal scores at the Top-K selection boundary, use the deterministic priority and comparison rules of the legacy kernel, including the register-resident fallback path. - Accumulate the renormalization denominator in the same serial order as the legacy implementation, producing bitwise-equal weights. - Handle NaN/`-Inf` inputs without producing invalid or duplicate expert IDs. There are no API, dispatch-gate, dtype, or supported-shape changes. ## Test plan No new test file is added. Compatibility cases are added to the existing `op_tests/test_moeTopkSoftmax.py`. They cover the GLM-5.2 router shape (`biased`, BF16, `E=256`, `topk=8`, `G=1`) with random inputs, all-equal scores, and a 16-way cutoff tie. The register output is compared directly with the legacy LDS output, including expert order and bitwise-equal weights. ## Performance ### gfx950 gfx950, bf16, `topk_reg_kernel` vs `grouped_topk_kernel (LDS)` (µs): | token | E=128 k=4 | E=128 k=32 | E=256 k=8 (GLM) | E=896 k=16 | E=2048 k=4 | E=2048 k=32 | |------:|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2.64 vs 2.62 (1.0x) | 6.57 vs 11.86 (1.8x) | 3.40 vs 3.72 (1.1x) | 5.26 vs 10.67 (2.0x) | 5.06 vs 5.96 (1.2x) | 12.46 vs 27.67 (2.2x) | | 32 | 3.78 vs 4.31 (1.1x) | 7.78 vs 12.81 (1.6x) | 4.56 vs 5.35 (1.2x) | 6.54 vs 12.98 (2.0x) | 6.14 vs 8.84 (1.4x) | 14.05 vs 30.07 (2.1x) | | 1024 | 4.00 vs 4.52 (1.1x) | 8.14 vs 12.83 (1.6x) | 4.90 vs 5.75 (1.2x) | 7.08 vs 12.85 (1.8x) | 7.27 vs 11.37 (1.6x) | 13.74 vs 33.62 (2.4x) | | 4096 | 5.29 vs 6.14 (1.2x) | 10.76 vs 18.27 (1.7x) | 6.99 vs 8.23 (1.2x) | 10.37 vs 19.73 (1.9x) | 10.84 vs 22.02 (2.0x) | 18.20 vs 82.20 (4.5x) | gfx950, bf16, `PR` vs `main (this kernel before)` (µs): | token | E=128 k=4 | E=128 k=32 | E=256 k=8 (GLM) | E=896 k=16 | E=2048 k=4 | E=2048 k=32 | |------:|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2.33 → 2.64 (+13%) | 2.34 → 6.57 (+181%) | 2.50 → 3.40 (+36%) | 3.26 → 5.26 (+61%) | 4.78 → 5.06 (+6%) | 7.25 → 12.46 (+72%) | | 32 | 4.06 → 3.78 (-7%) | 4.07 → 7.78 (+91%) | 4.24 → 4.56 (+7%) | 5.09 → 6.54 (+28%) | 6.48 → 6.14 (-5%) | 8.93 → 14.05 (+57%) | | 1024 | 4.29 → 4.00 (-7%) | 4.29 → 8.14 (+90%) | 4.57 → 4.90 (+7%) | 5.59 → 7.08 (+27%) | 7.56 → 7.27 (-4%) | 10.14 → 13.74 (+36%) | | 4096 | 5.39 → 5.29 (-2%) | 5.40 → 10.76 (+99%) | 5.73 → 6.99 (+22%) | 7.76 → 10.37 (+34%) | 10.26 → 10.84 (+6%) | 14.47 → 18.20 (+26%) | Compared with the previous unordered implementation, the current kernel preserves deterministic legacy ordering for accuracy at the cost of lower performance. ## GLM-5.2 end-to-end accuracy ## Submission Checklist - [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

## Summary

- **torch.symm_mem transport**: Add `torch.distributed._symmetric_memory` (backed by `mori.allocator`) as a new transport for custom all-reduce on gfx1250. Opt-in via `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_USE_SYMM_MEM=1`. Replaces manual IPC handle exchange (TCPStore / Unix socket VMM fd) with `symm_mem.rendezvous()` which handles fabric handles or POSIX fds internally. Reuses existing gfx1250 VMM-style C++ ops (pointer-list interface) — no C++ kernel changes for this part.
- **Collective P2P probe**: Before init, allocates a small buffer + rendezvous across all peers. mori's rendezvous validates P2P via `hipMemSetAccess(RW)` for each peer — all ranks agree on pass/fail, safe fallback to VMM/IPC with no hang risk.
- **world_size 6/8**: Extend gfx1250 template instantiations from {2,4} to {2,4,6,8} across all dispatch points (allreduce, allgather, reduce_scatter). Introduce `DISPATCH_NGPUS_1250` macro to unify the dispatch pattern. No algorithmic changes — kernels are simple `for(i<ngpus)` loops and `Signal`/`RankData` structs already have 8 slots.

title: [HIP] fix(custom_all_reduce): uniform trip count for the block barriers
body:
## What is wrong

Three kernels in `csrc/include/custom_all_reduce.cuh` stage their operands through shared memory
and bracket that with two block-wide `__syncthreads()` — inside a grid-stride loop whose trip
count is **not uniform across the block**:

| kernel | loop |
|---|---|
| `cross_device_reduce_2stage` | stage 1, reduce-scatter |
| `cross_device_reduce_2stage_write_mode` | stage 2 |
| `reduce_scatter_cross_device_store` | fused allreduce+rmsnorm, first step |

Taking the first as the example:

```cpp
for(int idx = start + tid; idx < end; idx += stride)
{
    *(reinterpret_cast<P*>(&tmp_smem[0]) + threadIdx.x) = ptrs[warp_id][idx];
    __syncthreads();
    if(warp_id == 0) { /* sum the ngpus operands out of smem */ }
    __syncthreads();
}
```

`end - start` is this rank's partition, `size / ngpus`, which is not generally a multiple of
`stride = gridDim.x * (THREAD_NUM / ngpus)`. The lanes that cover the tail therefore run one
iteration more than the rest, so the barriers pair up across different iterations — and against
the ones in `end_sync`. Two consequences:

* the `warp_id == 0` reduction can read `tmp_smem` before the other wavefronts have written
  their operands into it;
* a wavefront can reach `end_sync` and publish "stage 1 done" while another is still producing
  `tmp_out`, so the stage-2 all-gather can read a partition that is not finished.

Either way the output is wrong at a fixed relative position inside each rank's partition.

## How it shows up

`size` is flat, so each rank owns a contiguous `size / ngpus` slice — one quarter of the rows of
a `[bs, hidden]` tensor at `ngpus == 4`. The damage lands at the same offset in every quarter:

```
bs = 120  ->  bad rows {1, 31, 61, 91}      (stride 30 = 120/4)
bs = 160  ->  bad rows {11, 51, 91, 131}    (stride 40 = 160/4)
```

Found in an RL workload; reproduced standalone below.

## Standalone reproduction

Four ranks on MI355X, bf16 `[bs, 2880]`, 32 shapes × 600 reductions each. Every reduction is run
twice and compared bitwise (no tolerance needed), and also compared against RCCL's `all_reduce`
(bf16 rounding on a 4-way sum is ~0.05, so anything above that is a wrong answer rather than a
different summation order):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| wrong vs RCCL, and non-deterministic | **64 of 19200** | **0 of 19200** |
| shapes affected | bs = 120, 121, 127, 157, 160, 161 | none |
| worst \|diff\| | **12.4** | 0.0625 (pure bf16 rounding) |
| 48 reductions back to back, bs=160 | **300 of 11520** wrong, worst 13.1 | 0 of 11520 |
| world_size=2 (1-stage path) | 0 of 5120 | 0 of 5120 — no regression |

It is a race, so the counts move between runs; an earlier sweep over a slightly different set of
shapes gave 43/19200 and 173/11520. Most shapes pass either way — the race needs the partition
remainder to land mid-block, which is why this has survived.

The numbers above were measured on a build based on `d9e5ef7ce` that also carried a second
commit, since dropped, which widened two sync scopes. @TennyWang1223 re-measured `6110f00f`
on its own and reproduced the fix, which attributes it to the barrier change alone. The
three patched hunks are unchanged on `main`, and the rebased diff is byte-identical to the
one that was tested.

## The fix

Round the loop bound up to a multiple of the stride, which makes the trip count exactly uniform
(`tid < stride` by construction), and predicate the work. No added synchronisation and no change
to the reduction order.

`reduce_scatter_cross_device_store` is fixed by inspection — same defect, same file — but the
reproducer above does not exercise the fused-allreduce path.

Timing, 7 reps × 500 calls, median us/call taken as the max over ranks, whole measurement
repeated twice: within run-to-run noise at bs=120..161, and **3-6% slower** at bs=256
(19.2 → 20.3) and bs=512 (32.2 → 33.1).

title: [FlyDSL] [CI] gfx950 FP8 paged-prefill attention with asymmetric head dim and varlen support
body:
## Motivation

This PR aims to integrate the native gfx950 FP8 paged-prefill attention with asymmetric Q/K and V head dimensions and packed variable-length sequence support from [ROCm/FlyDSL#1066](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/pull/1066) into AITER.

AITER already supports FlyDSL dense FP8 attention through [ROCm/aiter#5326](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5326), but paged prefill still needs a native path that consumes the serving both kv cache layout used by sglang [SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/references/environment_variables#amd-&-rocm) directly:
- `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=nhd`: Linear KV-cache layout with page size 1 
- `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`: Vectorized 5D KV-cache layout with page size 16/64/1024

## Technical Details

- Add native causal packed-varlen FP8 paged attention for gfx950 based on FlyDSL `0.3.4.1` runtime.
- Support `D128/V128`, `D192/V128`, and `D192/V192` with BF16 output.
- Support page-1 linear/linear3d caches and page-16/64/1024 vectorized caches.
- Accept both block-table metadata and native CSR metadata (`kv_indptr`, `kv_page_indices`, and `kv_last_page_lens`).
- Add public API aiter.ops.flydsl.flydsl_flash_attn_paged_prefill_func for downstream farmwork integration.
- Preserve preallocated output, custom stream, graph replay, runtime softmax scale, ragged requests, odd page counts, and large cache addressing contracts, LSE.
- Share common dense/paged FP8 pipeline helpers and split paged GEMM, LDS, softmax, and epilogue helpers into focused modules.
- Add correctness, API, dispatch, metadata, stream, graph, and regression coverage to the standard AITER test shard.


## Performance

MI355X (`gfx950`) with ROCm/HIP `7.2.26015`, Torch `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0`, `B=1`, `Hq=16`, `Hkv=1`, causal `Q:KV=1:2`, page size 64, vectorized FP8 K/V, and preallocated BF16 output.

title: [CK] [Bugfix][Perf] fused_moe: tune the non-temporal load hint per tuned row
body:
## What's wrong

`get_2stage_cfgs()` initialises the non-temporal load hint to `False` and assigns it only
inside the heuristic branch:

```python
use_non_temporal_load = False
if cfg is None or bypass_tuned_config:
    use_non_temporal_load = use_nt(token, topk, expert)   # heuristic branch only
else:
    ...                                                   # tuned branch: never assigned
```

A shape loses non-temporal weight loads the moment it gains a tuned CSV row, and
`AITER_USE_NT` is dead there as well, because the override lives inside `use_nt()`.

An earlier revision of this PR simply derived the flag on the tuned path too. Review pointed
out why that is not sound, and measurements agree: the tuner never passes `non_temporal_load`
(`gemm_moe_tune.py` -> `ck_moe_stage{1,2}_fwd_out`), so **every** candidate in every shipped
row was ranked with the hint off. Turning it on at runtime runs the selected kernel outside
the conditions it was selected in, and the recorded `us1`/`us2` stop describing runtime. On
gfx942 that shows up directly: the shipped `ds_v3` row for `7168x2048 e33 topk9` at token 128
(`block_m=32`) is **6.6 % slower** with the hint on, while the same shape at tokens 16 and 64
is 5.0 % / 3.5 % faster. One shape family, no constant right answer.

## Fix

Make the hint part of what gets tuned instead of something derived next to the tuned row. The
tuner sweeps both values for the quant types whose kernels read it, ranks
`(kernel, block_m, nt)` jointly by `us1 + us2`, and records the winner in a new `nt` column;
the runtime reads that column.

```diff
     else:
         block_m = cfg["block_m"]
+        # rows tuned before the nt column keep the hint off
+        nt_override = int(os.environ.get("AITER_USE_NT", "-1"))
+        if nt_override != -1:
+            use_non_temporal_load = bool(nt_override)
+        elif "nt" in cfg:
+            use_non_temporal_load = bool(int(cfg["nt"]))
```

`use_nt()` and the heuristic branch are untouched, so nothing changes for shapes without a
tuned row. Rows without the column keep `nt=False`, which is today's behaviour, so no shipped
config changes until it is retuned. `AITER_USE_NT` now overrides both paths, as it was
documented to. On the tuner side `nt` is threaded exactly like the existing `flat` / `xbf16`
columns: it rides in the candidate tag, becomes a column in the candidate table, joins the
dedup key and the stage1 x stage2 merge key (so both stages of a row agree on it), and is
written out. The sweep is gated to `per_1x128`, so every other quant type keeps its candidate
count.

## Results, MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU)

DSv3 EP shape `7168x2048 e33 topk9`, per_1x128 fp8 blockscale, preshuffled weights.

**Tuner level** — same box, same harness, the extra dimension is the only difference:

| token | without the nt sweep    | with the nt sweep               | gain   |
| ----- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------ |
| 16    | `block_m=16`, 360.34 us | `block_m=16`, `nt=1`, 329.59 us | +8.5 % |
| 64    | `block_m=32`, 375.48 us | `block_m=32`, `nt=1`, 358.88 us | +4.4 % |
| 128   | `block_m=64`, 404.58 us | `block_m=64`, `nt=1`, 395.84 us | +2.2 % |

**Runtime level** — whole `fused_moe` op, CUDA-graph replay, 200 iters after 40 warmup, 8
rotated weight sets, 3 interleaved rounds per config, median:

| token | shipped rows | retuned, no nt sweep | retuned, nt swept | vs shipped |
| ----- | ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| 16    | 383.2 us     | 374.5 us             | 329.6 us          | +14.0 %    |
| 64    | 398.0 us     | 411.5 us             | 365.0 us          | +8.3 %     |
| 128   | 455.4 us     | 431.2 us             | 417.2 us          | +8.4 %     |

Retuning with the hint in the search is worth +3.3 % to +12.0 % over retuning without it on
the same box.

**Why this cannot be a heuristic.** The `block_m` the tuner picks and the best value of the
hint are coupled: what the hint discards is weight reuse between M-tiles of the same expert,
so it wins while an expert stays inside one tile and loses once it spans two. At token 128 on
this shape, stage2 measured alone with `rocprofv3` is 161.0 -> 191.8 us with the hint at
`block_m=32`, but 153.1 -> 135.7 us at `block_m=64`; `rocprofv3 --pmc TCC_HIT_sum TCC_MISS_sum`
attributes the whole difference to cache hit rate (42.8 % -> 28.5 %, 722 MB -> 920 MB below L2
against 2 x 484 MB of logical B reads, both arms sustaining ~4 TB/s). A predicate over token
count cannot see `block_m`, and under imbalanced routing it cannot see the tail experts that
cross into a second tile before the mean does either. Tuning it removes the guesswork.

## Results, MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU)

Second architecture, independent box. 26 shapes from three families (`4096x384 e128 topk8`,
`7168x512 e257 topk9`, `3072x1536 e256 topk8`), same machine, same harness, same
single-process settings, one card, tuned **three times per arm** at the PR's parent `c3caa55`
and at the head `c26f391`. 23 of the 26 resolve a winner on every run of both arms (the other
three are under *Caveats*). Times are the tuner's own per-candidate measurement for the
winning row; gain is median-of-three, spread is max-min within an arm.

The result separates by winning path. The 16 asm 1-stage shapes do not read the flag and do
not move: all keep `nt=0`, median gain +0.07 % over a range of -0.7 % .. +0.8 % against
per-arm spreads up to 1.4 %. The 7 CK 2-stage shapes are one family, `4096x384 e128 topk8`,
`doweight_stage1=1`, all at `block_m=16`:

| token | parent    | PR        | gain   | per-arm spread | `nt`                |
| ----- | --------- | --------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------------- |
| 1     | 38.62 us  | 38.19 us  | +1.1 % | 7.1 % / 4.6 %  | `0`/`1`, unstable   |
| 2     | 42.65 us  | 41.38 us  | +3.0 % | 6.2 % / 1.5 %  | `1`                 |
| 4     | 50.69 us  | 47.30 us  | +6.7 % | 6.2 % / 3.6 %  | `1`                 |
| 8     | 61.86 us  | 57.14 us  | +7.6 % | 1.3 % / 2.7 %  | `1`                 |
| 16    | 83.12 us  | 76.54 us  | +7.9 % | 1.4 % / 1.7 %  | `1`                 |
| 32    | 113.93 us | 105.10 us | +7.8 % | 0.3 % / 0.4 %  | `1`                 |
| 64    | 122.32 us | 113.05 us | +7.6 % | 0.2 % / 0.4 %  | `1`                 |

From token 8 up, the gain is several times either arm's spread and holds within half a point
across four shapes. At tokens 1-4 the shape runs in tens of microseconds, the arms overlap,
and token 1 does not even settle on a value across repeats — the flag genuinely does not
matter there, so nothing is claimed. Both arms pick the same kernel pair at tokens 1-16; at
tokens 32 and 64 the PR arm's winner is the `128x16x128x128` variant rather than
`256x16x128x256`, which is the ranking doing its job once `nt` is in the search space. An
isolated single-shape rerun where both arms converged on the identical kernel and `block_m`
isolates the flag on its own: 121.76 us -> 114.31 us, +6.1 % (stage1 +7.0 %, stage2 +4.5 %).


## Cost and compatibility

* CK candidates double for `per_1x128` only: 10 -> 20 per shape here, one shape 19 s -> 38 s,
  roughly 10 min for a full model file. Verified that a `per_Token` tune is unchanged.
* Rows without the column behave exactly as today. The 46 shipped blockscale 2-stage rows with
  `use_nt() == True` (38 at `cu_num` 256, 8 at `cu_num` 304) keep the hint off until someone
  retunes them; retuning shipped configs is out of scope here.
* No C++ change: `ck_moe_stage{1,2}_fwd` already take the flag and `gen_instances.py` already
  compiles both NT instantiations.

## Verification

* Runtime decision table, all five cases checked against `get_2stage_cfgs` on **both** gfx942
  and gfx950: legacy CSV (no column) -> off; `nt=0` -> off; `nt=1` -> on; legacy +
  `AITER_USE_NT=1` -> on; `nt=1` + `AITER_USE_NT=0` -> off. At the parent commit all five
  return off, which is the bug.
* Shipped-config regression, exhaustive: all **179** `cu_num=256` blockscale 2-stage rows across
  the 7 shipped CSVs (`ds_v3`, `glm5`, `minimax-m2_5`, `qwen3_235b`, `qwen3_5_397b`, and the
  untuned files) resolved through `get_2stage_cfgs` on both arms and compared field by field —
  `block_m`, `ksplit`, both kernel names, `nt_stage1`, `nt_stage2`. **Zero differences.** 119 of
  those rows are ones where `use_nt()` would return `True`; they stay off on both arms,
  confirming the heuristic was already inert on the tuned path and that this change does not
  switch it on.
* Tuner smoke test: the dispatch list shows each CK kernel twice, once per value; the candidate
  table and the tuned CSV carry `nt`; `per_Token` keeps its candidate count.
* Hand-written rows confirm the column drives the kernel: the same shipped config with `nt=1`
  reproduces +5.0 % / +3.5 % / -6.6 % at tokens 16 / 64 / 128.
* Numerics: the flag only selects `AmdBufferCoherenceEnum`, no arithmetic changes. Measured on
  gfx950, per-candidate reference error is identical between the two arms and between `nt=0` and
  `nt=1` (stage1 0.1 % in every group; stage2 within 0.1 pp).
* `op_tests/test_moe_blockscale.py` exits 0 with the same six checks; instrumenting
  `get_2stage_cfgs` shows it never enters the tuned branch (asm path only), so it does not cover
  this change.
* `ruff` clean on both files; no new findings (3 pre-existing in the tuner, 34 pre-existing E501
  in `fused_moe.py`, unchanged).

## Caveats

* The rankings above were produced with the catastrophic-mismatch check relaxed locally, because
  the tuner's reference comparison rejects blockscale stage1 candidates — asm and CK alike — on
  both of my boxes, while `per_Token` is unaffected. That blocks blockscale tuning independently
  of this change: the two files involved are untouched by this PR, and the parent commit fails
  identically on the same shapes. On gfx950 it is what leaves the three shapes above unresolved.
  The measurements are unaffected, since both arms are gated identically and the per-candidate
  errors match between them.
* Per-stage tuning of the hint is deliberately not attempted: the runtime passes one flag to both
  stages, so the merge forces stage1 and stage2 of a row to agree.

## Duplicate check

This updates my own #5443. Of the 640 open PRs, none touch `use_nt` / `non_temporal_load` in
`aiter/fused_moe.py`: #5117 is MXFP6 non-temporal *stores* in GEMM, #2947 is a gfx942 CK stage2
OOB fix, #3493 adds gfx942 tuned rows (12 more `cu_num=304` blockscale 2-stage rows, all of which
this PR leaves at `nt=0` until retuned).

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.
