title: fused_moe: remove incorrect topk adjustment in get_2stage_cfgs for EP
body:
## Summary

  Removes `topk -= int(is_ep)` from `get_2stage_cfgs` in `aiter/fused_moe.py`.

  ## Root Cause

  When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSED_MOE_SHARED_EXPERT=1` is set together with EP (`expert_mask is not None`), the removed line incorrectly reduces
  `topk` by 1 before building the config lookup key. This strips the Fused Shared Expert column from the key, causing a wrong tuned-config to be
  selected (or a cache miss falling back to untuned defaults).

  The adjustment was originally intended to strip the fake always-masked expert slot that EP callers append to `topk_ids`. That convention no longer
   applies uniformly — fused shared expert uses the last expert slot as a real expert, so subtracting 1 is invalid in that path.

  ## Change

  Removes 4 lines from `get_2stage_cfgs` — the comment block and the `topk -= int(is_ep)` mutation.

  ## Test Plan
  - Reproduce with EP + `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSED_MOE_SHARED_EXPERT=1` and confirm correct config is selected
  - Run `op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py` to verify no regression on standard EP path

  Fixes #5595

title: [CI] ci: add @aiter-bot review (self-hosted GLM PR reviewer)
body:
## Why aiter-bot (and not just Copilot review) | | Copilot review | **aiter-bot** | |---|---|---| | **Domain knowledge** | generic model reading the diff | `SKILL.md` / `rules.md` — aiter failure modes distilled from 200+ merged PRs (dispatch gate holes, gfx arch gating, tuned-config collisions, perf-claim scrutiny, AI-code tells) | | **Evidence** | reads the diff; executes nothing — every claim unverified | **can** run the PR's test target base-vs-head on a locked GPU and time it (deterministic correctness + perf, with a reproducer) when validation is enabled — **opt-in, off by default**; otherwise runtime claims are marked `[inferred]` | | **Self-check** | emits; does not audit itself | an independent refuter (a second GLM pass by default; cross-family with an Opus endpoint is stronger) kills false positives, then 7 mechanical gates check every finding is grounded (citations anchor to changed files, evidence exists, verdicts match runtime state) | | **Cost / privacy** | always-on SaaS; code leaves your boxes | on-demand, self-hosted runner + your own model — code never leaves your infra | | **Ownership** | black box | the methodology is a skill in this repo you own and evolve | Advisory and complementary — not a Copilot replacement. --- ## What it is Comment **`@aiter-bot review`** on any PR and aiter-bot posts one review card. Push fixes and comment again for a fresh pass — the same commit is deduped, so it never spams. One command, nothing else to remember. Runs on a self-hosted runner, posts as the **aiter-bot** account, and is **advisory — it never gates merge**. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TD A["aiter-team member comments:
@aiter-bot review on a PR"] --> B{"Gate: commenter on the
allowlist? real trigger line?
(quoted '>' lines ignored)"} B -- no --> Z["ignored (just a notice)"] B -- yes --> C["aiter-bot adds a 👀 reaction"] C --> D["self-hosted runner (box308)"] D --> E["fetch: PR diff, merge-target
worktree, validation triage"] E --> F["GLM worker → review card
(SKILL.md Steps 1b–8)"] F --> G["independent refuter (Step 7.7)
— a second pass kills false positives"] G --> H["7 gates verify the card"] H --> V{"review verdict"} V -- "✓ no findings / ⚠ needs work" --> P["aiter-bot posts the card on the PR"] V -- "🔴 HIGH RISK" --> R["posted too (advisory) +
a HIGH RISK warning
annotation in the checks"] P -. "push fixes, comment
@aiter-bot review again
(new head → fresh pass,
same commit → deduped)" .-> A ``` Each run posts one card: a one-line summary, a `Review` / `Validation` / `Perf` verdict line, and ≤5 ranked findings (problem → impact → **Author must…** / **Reviewer should ask…**, each tagged `[verified]` / `[inferred]`). A `🔴 HIGH RISK` card is posted too — it is exactly what the reviewer asked to see — and stays advisory (never a merge gate); a warning annotation also flags it in the checks. ## Example review A real card aiter-bot posted for PR #5599 (a data-only config PR, so validation/perf are correctly `NOT RUN`, with one `[verified]` process finding): > ## ROCm/aiter PR #5599 — [Config] configs: GLM-5.3 routed MoE rows for gfx950 > > **Adds a gfx950-specific GLM-5.3-Flash fused-MoE tuned-config table (six rows: M=4/8 → one-stage 16x128, M=2048–16384 → one-stage 64x256) plus its 15-shape untuned tuner-input ladder, moving that dispatch key off the generic fallback kernel.** > > Review (advisory): ⚠️ NEEDS WORK > Validation (deterministic): NOT RUN — triage required a target but the PR ships none; the changed paths are a tuned-config table plus its untuned tuner input — data-only, nothing a test target could cover, so the missing target is not a defect on this diff > Perf (advisory): NOT RUN — the PR ships no benchmark entry point, and it cannot be re-measured on this box (gfx942-only; the rows are gfx950-only) > > 📝 [verified] The duplicate-shape guard for the tuned_fmoe config family runs only in the daily Tuning Tests job, not in PR CI, so nothing enforces no-collision for the new CSV against config PRs landing while this one sits in queue — a racing duplicate dispatch key would make the first fused-MoE call on main raise RuntimeError and auto-rewrite the installed CSVs. **Reviewer should ask** for a fresh guard run (or a green post-merge Tuning Tests result) before relying on the new rows. ## Who can use it, & safety - **Who can trigger it — set the `AITER_REVIEW_AUTHORIZED` repo variable (required):** the job runs only for the comma-separated GitHub logins in that variable, checked at the job level **before any checkout**, so an unlisted commenter never starts a runner job. **Until you set it, the bot ignores every comment** — no spam, but no reviews either. `authorized.txt` in the skill dir seeds the initial list (`zufayu`) and is re-checked (exact match) inside the job; copy its logins into the variable at merge. A command in a quoted (`>`) line is ignored. - **Inert until merged** to the default branch (`issue_comment` only triggers from there). The `box308` runner and aiter-bot token are already provisioned — safe to merge and wire incrementally. - `permissions: contents: read`; comments use the aiter-bot token, not `GITHUB_TOKEN`. - **By default reads the PR diff as data and executes no PR code** (`REVIEW_AUTO_VALIDATE=0`); enabling validation (opt-in, per-need) runs the PR's own test target on a locked GPU. Runs in the base (main) context; comment body read via env, not shell-interpolated. - The review **agent runs headless** (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`) and reads the PR diff, title and description as prompt input — untrusted content from any PR author, so indirect prompt injection is in scope. Containment relied on: the aiter-bot token is never in the review step's environment (only the claim / publish / notify steps carry it), the runner is a dedicated self-hosted box, and no PR code runs by default. Keep the runner's credentials and network egress minimal — the agent's blast radius is that box. Because the agent can read the runner account's **files** (not just its environment), that account's GitHub credential should be a **dedicated read-only token** (e.g. the aiter-bot `public_repo` PAT), never a personal one.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add rotating-buffer GEMM A16W16 benchmark
body:
## Motivation

Add bench_gemm_a16w16_rotating.py — a GEMM benchmark that uses rotating buffers captured in a HIP graph to measure realistic L2-cold kernel latency while eliminating host launch overhead.

## Technical Details

- Allocates a buffer pool sized to exceed L2 capacity so each kernel dispatch within a graph replay is an L2 miss.
- Captures N kernel dispatches (round-robin through the pool) into a single graph, replays it multiple times for stable statistics.
- --bias flag (default off) to control ADD_BIAS kernel variant.
- --kernels-per-graph, --num-replays, --warmup-replays, --pool-size, --target-pool-mb for fine-grained control.

## Test Plan

As this is a benchmark test I have been running it to test certain gemms.

## Test Result

Output from this fix is more consistent with expectations (rotating buffer results in benchmark times that do not get faster after first run)

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] Add GPT-OSS IQ2R 2-bit MoE support
body:
## Summary

- Add a self-contained AITER implementation of the GPT-OSS O0/IQ2R approximately 2.39-bit expert-weight format, encoder, checkpoint ABI, loader, and overlay support.
- Add gfx950 IQ2R expert GEMMs plus fused top-k routing, stable task construction, dynamic MXFP8 packing, GPT-OSS SwiGLU/packing, and route-weighted BF16 reduction.
- Add graph-safe GPT-OSS TP1/EP1 orchestration through `QuantType.iq2r_2bit`.
- Add captured-production-route correctness and performance harnesses.
- Optimize decode and 16K-scheduler prefill shapes with route-qualified projection-specific dispatch.

## Scope

This is strictly a GPT-OSS MoE change. It does not modify or quantize QKV, O-projection, attention, or LM-head execution. Activations use dynamic per-1x32 MXFP8/E8M0 scaling; only expert weights use IQ2R. The implementation has no Redline source or runtime dependency.

Companion integration: ROCm/ATOM#2295.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] triton: add Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 GDN in_proj_ba AFP4WFP4 tiles (gfx950)
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #5350 (A4W4 CSV for `gemm_a4w4`). Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 GDN `in_proj_ba` is dispatched through AITER Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4`. Those kernels load `GEMM-AFP4WFP4-N=<N>-K=<K>.json` by shape. gfx950 currently has no tiles for this model's BA widths.

TP1 N=96 is scale-swizzle legal and stays on ASM unless a per-layer Triton force is applied, so that JSON is for the fallback / correctness path, not the default ASM path.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [CI] [Kernel] Gluon paged-decode attention with sigmoid output gate and group-128 FP8 epilogue (gfx950)
body:
# [Kernel] Gluon paged-decode attention with sigmoid output gate and group-128 FP8 epilogue (gfx950)

## Summary

Adds `paged_attention_output_gate_group_fp8_quant`, a Gluon paged-decode
attention op for gfx950 whose epilogue applies a sigmoid output gate and
optionally emits group-128 FP8 alongside the BF16 result.

It replaces **three launches with two** at the Qwen3-Next full-attention
boundary — paged decode attention, then `out * sigmoid(gate)`, then the
per-group activation quant the next GEMM consumes — by folding the gate and the
quant into the split-K merge the attention already performs.

## Motivation

**aiter has no op that fits this shape.** Checked at HEAD:

| existing op | KV layout | why it does not fit |
|---|---|---|
| `pa_decode`, `pa_decode_gluon` | block-table, `kv_block_size ∈ {16,64,1024}` | the target runs `page_size = 1` with a CSR index list; and neither has an epilogue seam — the store is a bare `tl.store` in eight kernel bodies |
| `pa_decode_sparse` | CSR, `page_size = 1` ✓ | **MLA-style: K and V are the same tensor.** Measured, not assumed — feeding a `[pages, 2D]` pool and testing three candidate references, only `K = V = kv[:, :D]` matches (mean rel 0.0019; reading `V = kv[:, D:]` is off by 1.48). It cannot express distinct K and V caches. |

So there is currently **no separate-K/V CSR paged-decode op in aiter at all**,
with or without an epilogue. That gap is worth filling independently of the gate.

**Both halves of the epilogue already exist here, unfused.**
`fusions/fused_sigmoid_mul.py` is exactly `out * sigmoid(gate)`;
`_triton_kernels/quant/fused_fp8_quant.py::_fp8_quant_op` is the same
`max(abs)/FP8_MAX` group formula with a `1e-10` floor. This op folds both into a
merge that is already reading the partials, so they cost no extra pass over
`[tokens, H*256]`.

**Emitting `(fp8, scales)` is an established argument in this repo.**
`fusions/attn_res.py:352 attn_res_gate(..., out_quant_dtype=None)` makes it in
its own docstring — *"an `(fp8, scale)` pair a GEMM can consume directly instead
of a BF16 tensor that each consumer quantizes for itself."* This op follows that
convention, and the FP8 output is opt-in via `quant_dtype=None`.

## Changes

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `_gluon_kernels/gfx950/attention/paged_attention_output_gate.py` | long-context body: split-K attention producing `(numerator, denominator, maximum)` partials, plus the merge carrying the gate + group-FP8 epilogue |
| `_gluon_kernels/gfx950/attention/paged_attention_output_gate_short_context.py` | short-context body |
| `attention/paged_attention_output_gate.py` | wrapper, body selection, `paged_attention_output_gate_supported() -> (bool, reason)` |
| `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_paged_attention_output_gate.py` | fp32 reference, `torch.testing.assert_close`, `pytest.skip` off-gfx950 |
| `op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_paged_attention_output_gate.py` | `run_benchmark(args)`, CSV + PNG |

No tuned config JSON: no `pa_*` op in the tree ships one, and
`configs/CLAUDE.md` forbids reusing the GEMM `M_LEQ_x`/`M_GEQ_x` scheme for
attention.

### API

```python
paged_attention_output_gate_group_fp8_quant(
    query,            # [T, H, 256] bf16
    key_cache,        # [pages, 1, 256] fp8_e4m3
    value_cache,      # [pages, 1, 256] fp8_e4m3
    kv_indptr,        # [T+1] int32, true prefix sum
    kv_indices,       # [total] int32, per-token slots (page_size = 1)
    gate,             # [T, H*256] bf16
    *,
    scale: float,
    max_context: int | None = None,         # body selector; never clamps
    k_scale=None, v_scale=None,             # per-tensor
    quant_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None, # None -> skip the FP8 epilogue
) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor | None, Tensor | None]
#    (bf16 [T, H*256], fp8 [T, H*256], fp32 scales [T, H*2])
```

**Two bodies, one range check.** `max_context <= 32768` selects the
short-context body, above it the long-context one; they differ in the split-K
decomposition, which is what the two regimes want differently. `max_context` is
a body selector only — it never clamps, the live length always comes from
`kv_indptr`.

**Neither body is specialised to batch.** `BATCH` is not a kernel constant in
the long body (the row comes from `gl.program_id(0)`), so one binary serves any
batch size at any context length.

That matters for coverage: a CUDA graph capture asks for decode
batches of 1, 2, 4, 8, **12**, 16, **24**, 32, **40**, **48**, **56**, 64, and
dispatch happens once at capture — a miss is baked into the captured graph
permanently rather than retried per step. The test parametrizes over exactly
those sizes.

## Performance

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.0, Triton 3.8, torch 2.9.0a0. Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B shapes:
`H=4`, `head_dim=256`, `page_size=1`, fp8_e4m3 KV.

**Method.** A CUDA graph holding one kernel costs ~9.3 µs to replay on this host
regardless of the kernel, so every measurement captures 50 invocations per graph
(live floor 1.70 µs). This matters for the comparison and not just the absolute
numbers: `triton.testing.do_bench` has no graph mode in this Triton, and the
distortion is **not** common-mode — the fused op is two launches and the stock
composition is four — so `do_bench` reads this as 1.31× where graph capture reads
2.12×. The shipped benchmark graph-captures by default; `--do-bench` restores the
conventional path.

**Configuration: vs. the three launches this op replaces** — `paged_attention_ragged`
(what SGLang's aiter backend calls today) + a sigmoid-gate multiply + a group-128
activation quant. Microseconds per decode step for one attention layer,
`H=4`, `head_dim=256`, `page_size=1`, fp8_e4m3 KV.

34 (context, batch) cells, 3 rounds each with measurement order shuffled and the
fixture seed varied per round; live floor 1.70 us and no cell within 2x of it.
Representative batches shown.

| context | batch | Before (us) | After (us) | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 536 | 1 | 16.81 | **5.15** | **3.26x** |
| 1 536 | 8 | 17.22 | **5.04** | **3.41x** |
| 1 536 | 32 | 17.78 | **7.05** | **2.52x** |
| 1 536 | 64 | 23.89 | **10.59** | **2.26x** |
| 8 192 | 1 | 17.50 | **5.92** | **2.96x** |
| 8 192 | 8 | 18.74 | **8.09** | **2.32x** |
| 8 192 | 32 | 39.28 | **22.89** | **1.72x** |
| 8 192 | 64 | 63.57 | **41.18** | **1.54x** |
| 32 768 | 1 | 19.74 | **8.60** | **2.29x** |
| 32 768 | 8 | 41.22 | **24.13** | **1.71x** |
| 32 768 | 32 | 119.28 | **95.81** | **1.24x** |
| 32 768 | 64 | 237.59 | **172.01** | **1.38x** |
| 65 536 | 1 | 23.69 | **12.49** | **1.90x** |
| 65 536 | 8 | 68.49 | **45.78** | **1.50x** |
| 65 536 | 32 | 222.82 | **167.56** | **1.33x** |
| 65 536 | 64 | 483.62 | **336.17** | **1.44x** |
| 131 072 | 1 | 37.42 | **19.23** | **1.95x** |
| 131 072 | 8 | 139.00 | **90.00** | **1.54x** |
| 131 072 | 32 | 480.82 | **333.73** | **1.44x** |

**Geomean 1.97x over all 34 cells; range 1.24-3.41x.**

### Bandwidth utilisation and roofline

The roofline shows why the long-context ratio settles where it does. Traffic is
`bs * context * 256 * 2` bytes and is **identical for both implementations at a
given cell** -- same bytes, same gather. Achieved bandwidth is therefore just
`traffic / time`, i.e. the same fact as runtime re-expressed against the hardware
limit. It is reported because it answers what a raw speedup cannot: **how much
headroom is left.** MI355X HBM3E peak is 8.0 TB/s, and at the largest cells:

| | achieved | % of peak |
|---|---|---|
| this op | 6.52 TB/s | **81%** |
| stock | 4.82 TB/s | 60% |

4.82 / 6.52 = 0.74, which is exactly the long-context ratio in the table above.
At 81% of peak
there is at most 19% more available to any implementation, so the asymptotic win
is gather efficiency, not fusion. Below bs~8 the kernel is latency-bound rather
than bandwidth-bound (9% of peak at bs=1) -- only a few MB to move, and the limit
is occupancy and launch, which is why the fused epilogue matters most there.

## Testing

- [x] Unit test added — fp32 PyTorch reference, `torch.testing.assert_close`,
      over batch ∈ {1,2,4,8,12,16,24,32,40,48,56,64,128}, heads ∈ {4,8,16},
      context ∈ {1,129,1024}, a `max_context` on each side of the crossover so
      both bodies are exercised, with and without `quant_dtype`, plus a
      non-contiguous-gate case, a case proving `max_context` never clamps, a
      both-bodies-agree case, and predicate coverage.
      **488 passed, 9 skipped on gfx950** (the skips are heads 1/2/3, which
        have no short-body path, and say so). Correctness is additionally established outside
- [x] Benchmark added.
- [x] `pytest.skip` on non-gfx950.
- [x] `FILE_TIMES` entry added in `.github/scripts/split_tests.sh` (7.6 s
      measured, registered at 20 for headroom on a loaded runner).

**The epilogue's numerics are contract.** Three BF16 rounding boundaries —
attention→bf16→fp32, sigmoid→bf16→fp32, product→bf16 — before the group absmax.
The test reproduces them exactly; an implementation that keeps the intermediates
in fp32 produces different FP8 codes.

**Two guards the reference implementation lacked**, both now asserted by tests:
the gate is indexed through its row stride rather than assuming
`stride(0) == heads*256`, and the support predicate checks the cache dim stride
the gather relies on.

## Documentation

A Quick Reference row plus a detail section in
  `aiter/ops/triton/gluon/README.md`, matching the format the other two attention
  kernels use. The bandwidth quoted there is the output of the command that row
  cites (`--context 8192 --compare --metric bandwidth`, tokens=64: 6530 GB/s),
  since that column documents the perf of the typical test.

## Dependencies

- [x] No new third-party dependencies.

## Breaking changes

None — new op, no existing signature touched.

## Scope

- **gfx950 only.** Guarded by `arch_info`; `paged_attention_output_gate_supported()`
  returns `(False, reason)` elsewhere so callers fall back rather than crash.
- **No CUDA path affected.**
- `page_size = 1`, `head_dim = 256`, `heads ≤ 16`, per-tensor `k_scale`/`v_scale`,
  fp8 e4m3 KV. All checked by the predicate, all reported with a reason.

## Reproduction

The measurements use a public base image plus one change — Triton upgraded to
3.8. **The upgrade is required, not incidental:** the Gluon launcher passes
`llvm_fn_attrs=`, which does not exist in Triton 3.7, and the first launch fails
without it.

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
ARG BASE=lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm700-mi35x-20260910
FROM ${BASE}

# Gluon needs llvm_fn_attrs, added in Triton 3.8. The base ships 3.7.
ARG TRITON_VERSION=3.8.0
ARG TRITON_INDEX=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/rocm7.0
RUN python -m pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall --pre \
      --index-url "${TRITON_INDEX}" \
      "triton==${TRITON_VERSION}"
```

```bash
docker build -t pa-gate:local \
  --build-arg BASE=lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm700-mi35x-20260910 .

docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
  --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --group-add video --group-add render \
  --ipc=host --shm-size 32G -e ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  -v $PWD:/w -w /w pa-gate:local bash -lc '
    python3 -m pytest op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_paged_attention_output_gate.py -q
    python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_paged_attention_output_gate.py \
      --context 8192  --compare
    python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_paged_attention_output_gate.py \
      --context 65536 --compare
  '
```

Exact versions the numbers above were taken on:

| | |
|---|---|
| base image | `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm700-mi35x-20260910` |
| ROCm | 7.0.0 |
| torch | `2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe` |
| triton | **3.8.0** (upgraded from the base's 3.7.0) |
| aiter | `4ad99832` + this PR |
| GPU | 1x MI355X (gfx950) |

**ROCm 7.0 specifically.** The same base is published for 7.2
(`...-rocm724-...`); this op has not been validated there, and on ROCm >= 7.2
SGLang additionally enables FP8 weight preshuffling, which changes surrounding
behaviour.

## Numerical note on the stock baseline

The stock FP8-KV path is **not numerically equivalent** to this op: it diverges
from an fp32 reference by ~14% mean relative error (13.7–14.8% at every measured
cell), where this op agrees to **0.18–0.27%**.

That is a defect in `paged_attention_ragged` — it casts already-normalized
softmax probabilities to e4m3, where at `partition_size = 256` they sit at ~2⁻⁸
and are **subnormal** (`csrc/cpp_itfs/pa/pa_kernels.cuh:586-588`, `:633-647`).

**It is already fixed: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5642.**

**The fix is timing-neutral, so every "Before" number in this PR stands as
measured.** Verified directly on the same container before and after: FP8 kernel
time 13.49 → 13.51 µs at bs=1 and 59.68 → 59.50 µs at bs=64, i.e. within noise,
while the error drops 0.142 → 0.027 (5.2×) and the BF16 path is bit-identical.
The defect is a scaling choice with no instruction-count, branch or
data-movement consequence.

The two columns should still be read as *not computing the same thing to the
same accuracy* until #5642 lands.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [gfx950] pa_decode_sparse: bound split-K by wave count and tile budget (up to +22%)
body:
Bounds the split-K count in the gfx950 gluon sparse-decode driver from both sides: the launch stops
overshooting one wave of workgroups, and it stops cutting splits once each workgroup carries enough
KV tiles to pay for itself.

## What changes

`_decode_num_splits_occ` bounds the split count by `cta_cap = 2 * num_sms // base_wg`, which lets
`base_wg * splits` exceed `num_sms`. Capping that alone is not enough, though — past a point, cutting
splits stops removing overhead and starts removing parallelism. So the count is bounded by both:

```python
wave_cap = 1 << max(0, (num_sms // base_wg).bit_length() - 1)
return max(1, min(cta_cap, tiles, max(wave_cap, tiles // 4)))
```

`tiles // 4` is not a new constant — it is the split floor the `base_wg >= num_sms` branch of this
same function already uses. Only the `base_wg < num_sms` branch changes.

## Why both bounds are needed

Every split costs a fixed amount — its own partial write and its own Q re-read, both paid **inside the
attention kernel** — and that cost does not depend on how much KV the split actually covers. So the
tradeoff is per-split fixed cost against parallelism, and where it balances depends on how many KV
tiles a workgroup has to amortise it over. That is set by top-k, which is why one bound cannot do it.

An earlier revision of this PR had only `wave_cap`. Measured over 24 shapes, that is a **net
regression**:

| | wins | losses | worst | best | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wave_cap` only | 6 | **15** | **-43.1 %** | +22.1 % | **-7.6 %** |
| with the `tiles // 4` floor | **10** | **0** | -1.0 % | +21.9 % | **+4.2 %** |

## Measurements

MI355X / gfx950 (256 CU), DeepSeek-V4.1 decode shape: 16 heads, head_dim 512 (448 NoPE + 64 RoPE),
packed fp8 cache, 128-slot SWA window plus a top-k list per query, 8 GiB KV pool. Median of 100
samples of 4 calls in one HIP graph. Each arm runs its own `_decode_num_splits_occ` — `kv_splits` is
not pinned — so this is what merging actually gives you. Speedup against current `main`:

| queries | top-k 512 | top-k 1024 | top-k 2048 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | +0.4 % | +0.5 % | -0.2 % |
| 36 | **+15.6 %** | **+21.9 %** | **+14.8 %** |
| 48 | **+16.3 %** | +5.7 % | +6.0 % |
| 96 | +5.5 % | +8.1 % | -0.2 % |
| 126 | +5.2 % | -0.1 % | +0.3 % |
| 150 | -1.0 % | -0.5 % | +0.0 % |
| 192 | -0.3 % | -0.2 % | +0.1 % |
| 252 | +0.4 % | +0.2 % | +2.9 % |

Against a per-point sweep of `kv_splits` over {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 14, 16} at every shape, the
guarded rule lands on or within 2.5 % of the measured optimum at every one of the 24 points. The
worst cell is -1.0 %.

## Tests

`test_decode_num_splits_occ_bounds` asserts the four bounds the split count is built from — at most
`tiles`, at most `cta_cap`, at least `tiles // 4`, and within one wave where the tile floor is not
what holds the count up — plus monotonicity in top-k, over 165 shapes.

`num_sms` is patched rather than read from the device, so the body allocates nothing and the bounds
are checked at partitioned CU counts (256 / 128 / 64 / 32) rather than only whatever the runner has.
The `torch.cuda.is_available()` guard matches the in-body form the other tests in this module use.

It discriminates, and the two failing arms fail for different reasons:

```
main                4 failed   cu=32 q=1 topk=8192: 64 workgroups over 32 CUs    <- the wave ceiling
wave cap, no floor  4 failed   cu=32 q=6 topk=2048: 4 splits leaves 8 tiles/WG   <- the floor
this PR             4 passed
```

Note it fails on `main` by design: the wave ceiling is behaviour this PR introduces, so asserting it
makes the contract explicit rather than incidental. The floor assertion is the regression guard, and
it is not masked by the ceiling — the un-floored version trips the floor first.

The H=16 subset of the existing kernel test is **42 passed, 10 skipped**, identical across all three.

## Numerics

Unchanged in kind: the split count only changes how many partials the fp32 combine sums, as it
already does across the existing `cta_cap` and `tiles` bounds. Checked directly — output max
absolute deviation across every split count at every shape is **<= 9.8e-04** against the single-split
result, which is fp8 accumulation order, not a behaviour change.

`op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_pa_decode_sparse.py`, the H=16 subset: **42 passed, 10 skipped**,
identical on `main`, on the bare cap, and with the floor.

## On the mechanism

An earlier revision explained this as a partly filled second wave costing a full wave of latency. A
`rocprofv3 --kernel-trace` of the launch does not support that, and the description is corrected:

- The saving is **entirely in the attention kernel** (103 % of the delta at 48 queries, 8 -> 4
  splits); `_aiter_sparse_decode_reduce_kernel` is flat to +0.1 us. The partial write happens inside
  the attention kernel before the workgroup exits, which is where the per-split cost actually lands.
- The kernel reports `LDS_Block_Size = 0` — no static LDS — so occupancy is VGPR-limited at 128
  VGPRs, giving 4 workgroups per CU. 384 workgroups is nowhere near a wave boundary, and there is no
  partly filled second wave to pay for.

`wave_cap` is still the right shape for the upper bound; the reasoning for it is amortisation, not
wave quantisation.

## Reproducing

Measured with a standalone benchmark that calls `pa_decode_sparse` directly, independent of any
serving stack, and cross-checked against an sglang-based harness that shares no code with it. Both
agree on where the win and loss zones fall. Happy to attach the benchmark if useful.

One methodology note for anyone re-running: a first measurement process reads 3-11 % fast from cold
start, so arms must be compared back to back within one process rather than across processes.

title: [HIP] Guard GroupNorm vectorization at channel boundaries
body:
## Summary

- Require the per-channel element count to be divisible by four before enabling GroupNorm vectorization.
- Keep Python workspace sizing consistent with the HIP launch configuration.
- Make GroupNorm correctness failures fatal and report the worst mismatch.
- Add a regression shape where the group span is divisible by four but the channel span is not.

## Motivation

The vectorized output path applies the affine parameters selected for the vector's first element to all four values. Therefore, a vector must never cross a channel boundary.

The previous condition checked whether the complete group span was divisible by four. That could enable vectorization when an individual channel had an incompatible element count.

This is a general correctness fix and is not specific to gfx908.

## Testing

Tested on AMD Instinct MI100 (`gfx908`) with:

- FP16
- BF16
- FP32
- small tensors
- multi-batch odd spatial dimensions
- aligned channel spans
- the odd `32769` channel-span regression case

All 12 dtype/shape combinations passed with zero tolerance violations.

`git diff --check` also passes.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [JIT] [Feature] Add tuned native group32 A8W8 Triton GEMM for gfx950
body:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash projections use unshuffled E4M3 weights and compact E8M0 group32 scales. This adds a gfx950 Triton backend for those operands to `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`, together with tuned configurations for TP4, TP2 and attention-DP local GEMMs.

### Implementation and dispatch

- Keep activations, weights and scales in their native formats. Support compact 32x32 or per-row 1x32 weight scales, FP32 accumulation, and BF16/FP16/FP32 output.
- Use native microscaling MFMA, packed-K execution for small M, and the existing non-atomic split-K reduction. The public interface accepts an optional native-group32 `split_k` partition count, preserving explicit caller controls while keeping configured backend selection first.
- Query `get_CKGEMM_config` before selecting a fallback. Native E8M0 operands have a separate `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BLOCKSCALE_GROUP32` CSV family, so an identical M/N/K in the FP32 128x128 table cannot select an incompatible kernel. Unsupported configured backends raise instead of silently falling back.
- Add 450 DSV4.1 model-config rows: 18 geometries and 25 M buckets, all selecting `libtype=triton`. Tile, split-K and packed-variant settings remain in the existing Triton JSON configuration system. Of these rows, 262 reuse exact-shape measured timings; remaining timing fields are empty.
- Extend the shared GEMM loader with optional file-defined `M_BOUNDS`, retaining explicit-argument precedence and legacy bounds. Config copies preserve nested mutation isolation while avoiding per-scalar `deepcopy` overhead.

The new native backend requires gfx950. Existing FP32 128x128 operands retain their CK/CKTile paths. Group32 currently supports the Triton backend; configuring legacy CK/CKTile for its E8M0 operands is rejected.

### Performance

Hardware: AMD gfx950, 256 CUs; PyTorch 2.9.1 ROCm 7.1.1 and Triton 3.8.0 ROCm build. Measurements use BF16 output, CUDA graphs and at least 512 MiB of rotating weights. The baseline is the initial imported native group32 configuration in the first commit of this PR.

The sweep evaluated 49,304 candidates across 234 representative M/N/K cases and validated 603 cases, including interval boundaries. The geometric-mean speedup is **1.179x** (15.18% lower GEMM latency). Of 300 intervals checked, 252 use improved configurations and 48 retain the baseline. The largest sampled slowdown among changed configurations is 0.97%. Measurements affected by other GPU users were discarded and rerun on available cards.

| Projection | N | K | Geometric-mean speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| qkv_a | 1792 | 5120 | 1.366x |
| indexer_q | 4096 | 1280 | 1.211x |
| q_b TP4 | 8192 | 1280 | 1.061x |
| q_b TP2 | 16384 | 1280 | 1.063x |
| q_b attention-DP | 32768 | 1280 | 1.112x |
| o_b TP4 | 5120 | 2048 | 1.188x |
| o_b TP2 | 5120 | 4096 | 1.221x |
| o_b attention-DP | 5120 | 8192 | 1.121x |
| shared_up TP4 | 1152 | 5120 | 1.131x |
| shared_up TP2 | 2304 | 5120 | 1.217x |
| shared_up TP1 | 4608 | 5120 | 1.194x |
| shared_down TP4 | 5120 | 576 | 1.273x |
| shared_down TP2 | 5120 | 1152 | 1.268x |
| shared_down TP1 | 5120 | 2304 | 1.243x |
| Engram | 25600 | 6144 | 1.123x |
| draft_main | 5120 | 15360 | 1.180x |
| draft_kv_fused | 1536 | 5120 | 1.176x |
| draft_kv | 512 | 5120 | 1.146x |

These are standalone GEMM results. End-to-end serving throughput was not measured. Tuning covers M through 4096; larger M retains the original JSON fallback. Model CSV entries through M=16384 choose the backend without claiming newly tuned tiles at those larger sizes.

### Validation

- **136 AITER tests passed** on the rebased branch: native numerical contracts, column/K tails, extreme scale codes, per-row scales, split-K, output buffers, live-input graph replay, dynamic-M fullgraph compile, CSV format isolation, and configured-backend precedence. CK/CKTile dispatch-priority tests use stubs; native numerical and graph tests execute GPU kernels.
- **100 ATOM integration tests passed** with the companion migration to the public AITER interface, covering actual backend-config lookup, blockscale projections, accumulation, GPU quantization, graph replay and dynamic batched fullgraph compilation.
- All **294,912** combinations of the 18 model geometries and integer M=1..16384 resolve through the real shared loader to Triton; unknown geometries still miss the table and reach fallback.
- Six representative cases comparing dispatch before/after the configuration-priority change have bitwise-equal BF16/FP32 outputs, identical GPU kernel sequences, and graph-latency differences below 0.5%.
- Black and Ruff pass for all seven changed Python files; `git diff --check` passes.

The sweep compares sampled outputs against an independent FP64 reference and complete BF16 outputs against the baseline. BF16 outputs are bitwise equal in 384/603 cases; the maximum BF16 relative RMS difference is 1.052e-4. One pre-existing FP32 reference-boundary outlier at M=97, N=5120, K=1152 remains: maximum absolute error changes from 0.09451294 to 0.09445190. The experiment accepts that point only when candidate error does not exceed baseline error; repository test tolerances are unchanged.

```bash
# AITER, on gfx950
python -m pytest -q \
  op_tests/test_gemm_group32_interface.py \
  op_tests/test_opus_a8w8_interface.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/gemm/basic/test_gemm_a8w8_blockscale_group32.py

# ATOM integration, with the V4.1 reference weights available
ATOM_DSV41_REFERENCE=/mnt/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash python -m pytest -q \
  tests/model_ops/test_blockscale_packed.py \
  tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_accumulation.py \
  tests/models/deepseek_v41/test_quant_gpu.py
```

title: [FlyDSL] [gfx1250] Optimize A4W4 MoE prefill with A preshuffle
body:
## Motivation

Optimize gfx1250 A4W4 MoE prefill performance while keeping untuned/decode tiles on the baseline producer and GEMM path.

## Technical Details

- Enable GEMM1 and GEMM2 A/ScaleA preshuffle only for the retained tuned `t256x256x256/w2x2/b4` shapes.
- Keep untuned serving shapes, including `t64x256x256/w1x4/b2`, on the original row-major A producer.
- Restore GEMM1 fused quantization when GEMM2 A-preshuffle is not selected.
- Keep the original quant emitter for non-A-preshuffle paths and use the dedicated emitter only for A-preshuffle producers.
- Do not globally force `AITER_FLYDSL_MXFP4_CLUSTER_N` or `AITER_TDM_NEXT_STAGE_PREFETCH`; the tuned prefill CSV entry supplies `cluster_n=4` and `next_stage_prefetch=1`.

## Test Plan

### Model and workload

```text
Model: DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4
ISL: 1024
OSL: 1024
Requests: 256
Maximum concurrency: 64
```

### Baseline server (`314ab7d48a077f3ccc055e7d353040c10a5f7fe5`)

git checkout 314ab7d48a077f3ccc055e7d353040c10a5f7fe5

title: [Triton/Gluon] FlashKDA in-kernel paged state_cache I/O
body:
## Motivation
 
FlashKDA still spoke a dense ABI: `initial_state[N, H, V, K]` plus a freshly allocated `out`. vLLM Kimi-K3 serving keeps recurrent state in a paged pool `[slots, H, V, K]` with `state_indices` / `has_initial_state`.

Wiring that through AITER meant:
 
1. `gather_initial_states` (or `state_cache[indices]`) into a dense tensor

2. run `chunk_kimi_delta_attn`

3. scatter `final_state` back

4. `out.copy_(kernel_out)`
 
Those copies sit in the serving timer. On MI350, a K3-shaped FlashKDA prefill paid ~40–60 µs for them (4K: 171 → 130 µs, 16K: 499 → 440 µs with the same segment pin). The fused vLLM path already reads and writes the pool in-kernel ([vLLM #54038](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54038)); this PR gives FlashKDA the same cache contract so a later vLLM dispatch ([#56036](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56036)) does not have to gather around AITER.

 
## Technical Details
 
Public kwargs on `chunk_kimi_delta_attn` / `flash_kda_fwd`:
 
- `state_cache`: fp32 V-first `[slots, H, V, K]`. Each slot plane is dense; `stride(0)` may pad.

- `state_indices`: int32 `[N]`

- `has_initial_state`: bool `[N]`; false starts that sequence from zero and does not read a dirty slot

- `out`: required with `state_cache`, same shape as `v` (K2 still loads `v`, so `out` must not alias it)
 
K2 and the scan load/store `slot * stride(0) + head * V * K + …`. The last segment writes the final state back to the same row. Segmented pass A does not bind `state_cache` (keeps the existing K2 binary / autotune; binding it here previously ~2× slowed K2).
 
`@input_guard(skip=("state_cache",))` leaves the pool’s storage and `stride(0)` alone. Other operands are still packed. The skip is an AITER decorator default, not a vLLM flag; the caller just passes `state_cache=` as a keyword.
 
Dense `initial_state` is unchanged and mutually exclusive with `state_cache`. `final_state` is `None` when the cache is used.
 
The default five-kernel path indexes a dense `h0` and is GVA / C=64 / K-first. If `state_cache` is set and FlashKDA is not selected,

`chunk_delta_attn_fwd` raises instead of ignoring the argument.
 
 
## Test Plan
 
```bash

pytest op_tests/triton_tests/chunk_delta_attn/test_flash_kda.py \

  -k 'paged_cache or flash_kda' -q

```
 
Added cases:
 
- `test_paged_cache_matches_dense` — paged vs dense `initial_state`, bit-identical `out` and selected slots; empty slots untouched; unsegmented and segmented

- `test_paged_cache_has_initial_state_false` — false flag matches a zero `initial_state`

- `test_paged_cache_padded_stride_writes_live_pool` — non-contiguous `stride(0)` updates the original storage pointer

- `test_paged_cache_rejected_on_default_pipeline` — non-FlashKDA call with `state_cache` raises
 
Serving-shaped A/B (K3 H=12, D=128, `lower_bound=-5`, varlen `cu_seqlens`)

vs gather and vs vLLM fused prefill on gfx950.
 
## Test Result
 
Paged vs dense FlashKDA: `torch.equal` on output and selected cache rows (rel err 0).
 
Paged FlashKDA vs vLLM fused prefill (same op, not e2e): output rel L2 ~4.8e-3, state ~2.5e-3 at 4K/16K.
 
MI350X, official vLLM ROCm image, serving-style call (µs, smaller is better):

 
| shape | gather FlashKDA | paged FlashKDA | fused |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1×4096, H=12 | 171 | **130** | 125 |
| 1×16384, H=12, `--segment 8` | 499 | **440** | 389 |
| 1×16384, H=12, auto segment | — | **380** | 388 |

 
Default-pipeline reject and padded-stride tests pass.

[Bugfix][MLA] Size PS prefill partial buffers from the real token budget
body:
## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5729.

The MLA PS metadata scheduler returns a pessimistic bound on the max number of partial entries needed to be allocated. This could lead to OOM. The pessimism stems from the fact that it assumed that all requests used the same (maximal) number of query tokens which is not true in inference engines with a fixed query token budget per step.

This PR fixes it to correctly give a much tighter bound by accounting for fixed token budget (c.f. max num batched tokens in vllm) if passed.

## Technical Details

A temporary fix was required on serving engine side: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57923/changes

It's better if we do this in AITER.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] Unify gfx950+gfx1250 MXFP4 MQA-logits
body:
## Motivation

gfx950 (#5332) and gfx1250 (#5656) shipped the same operator as two parallel
implementations: two JIT modules, two schedule builders, two Python surfaces and
two op tests. Every fix had to be landed twice, and two of them already diverged
in exactly the same shape of hole (a compile-time stride behind a rank-only
check). This folds them into one module / schedule / API / test, leaving both
device bodies untouched.

## Technical Details

**One JIT module.** `module_pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_opus` carries both device bodies;
a version macro selects which compiles (`__gfx950__` MFMA 32x32x64 wave64 vs
`__gfx1250__` WMMA 32x16x128 wave32/TDM), and the fat binary is built with
`--offload-arch` per arch, the idiom `opus_gemm` already uses. The two
`_gfx1250_` C++ files are deleted, their contents moved verbatim.

**One schedule.** gfx1250's two-phase `build_tiles` + `build_sched` is now the
only builder; gfx950's per-row builder is retired. gfx950 runs at
`q_per_block == 1`, where a tile is one row and the tile-union window is that
row's, so the shared builder emits exactly the per-row record its MFMA kernel
already reads.

**The tile cut is skipped at `q_per_block == 1`.** There the cut is the identity
-- tile `t` is row `t` -- so the boundary array is the arange the host already
knows. `build_tiles` exists to serve `q_per_block > 1` and is no longer launched
at 1: **one fewer kernel per forward** on every gfx950 call and on gfx1250's
MTP=1 decode instance, and `plan_buffers` stops allocating a buffer nothing
reads. `build_sched` takes `q_per_block` and reads the mapping through
`tile_row()` with a NULL `cu_tiles`.

**One runtime-arch dispatch.** `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_fwd_sched` reads
`get_gpu_arch()` and calls the MFMA or WMMA launcher, then dispatches within it
by `(q_per_block, block_k)`. aiter JITs per target GPU, so the arm that launches
always matches the compiled body.

**One Python surface** `aiter/ops/opus/pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4.py`, arch-parameterized
by `MqaLogitsVariant(name, q_per_block, block_k, cta_resident)`. **One op test**
on both arches (`SUPPORTED_GFX = ["gfx1250", "gfx950"]`), building natural
layouts on gfx1250 and MFMA-permuted ones on gfx950.

**`-mllvm -enable-post-misched=1` is load-bearing for gfx950 and must not be
dropped.** aiter's base JIT flags set it to 0; this module turns it back on,
which is the state the tuned standalone uses. The merged module now applies it
to the gfx1250 body as well (its own module did not) -- measured below.

## Test Plan

- Unified op test on both arches: corner cases on every compiled instance, NaN
  E8M0 scale propagation, and the four perf tables.
- Schedule table compared **byte for byte** against the pre-change builder, since
  the kernel consumes only that table.
- Kernel ISA compared against the standalone reference (`tools/fp4_aiter_isa.sh`
  + `tools/cmp_isa_aiter_vs_standalone.py`), to show the device bodies did not
  move.
- `-mllvm -enable-post-misched=1` A/B on gfx1250, since the merged module applies
  it to a body that never had it.

## Test Result

### gfx1250 (ROCm 10.1, clang 23)

| check | result |
|---|---|
| op test, both instances | 28/28 corner cases, NaN E8M0 6/6, `err = 0` on all 50 perf rows |
| schedule table vs built cut | **byte-identical** over 4 reps x 11 shapes (decode 1-2048 seqs, prefill 16384/25000 rows, with `local_starts` and `row_to_batch`) |
| kernel resources | 269 VGPR / occupancy 3 / no spill / LDS 9728 on both instances, unchanged |
| plan-stage launches | `qlen1_kv64` 2 -> 1 (small) and 3 -> 2 (split); `qlen4_kv64` unchanged |
| plan-stage cost | 8.7-9.1 us saved per forward on MTP=1 decode, 12-20 us on prefill |
| kernel time | 6 runs vs 16 pre-change, geomean 0.9982, inside the measured noise |

**post-misched on gfx1250.** The flag is active (`=1` is appended after the base
`=0`, last-wins) and it does change the ISA -- but it is a pure post-RA
reschedule: resources are identical to the digit, and the reordered code has
*fewer* instructions (VOPD packing, fewer `s_delay_alu`/`v_nop`). 16 paired
alternating runs, binary verified per run: **no shape regresses beyond noise, and
7 prefill shapes are 1.0-2.9% faster with the flag on** (13-16/16 sign
consistency, 0.4-3.6% within-arm spread). Decode shows no direction.

### gfx950

gfx950 (#5332) now runs through the unified module / schedule / API. Every call is at
`q_per_block == 1`, where the tile cut is the identity, so the MFMA body is recompiled, not
rewritten. gfx950 runs the `qlen1_kv64` (`block_k = 64`) instance in production; `qlen1_kv256`
is compiled and correctness-checked but not on the production path. Validated on a gfx950 box
(ROCm 7.2.4), module rebuilt fresh.

**Correctness** — op test, both instances (`qlen1_kv64`, `qlen1_kv256`):

| table | rows | err |
|---|---|---|
| corner (13 cases × 2 instances) | 26 | 0 |
| NaN E8M0 propagation | 6 | 0 |

**Kernel and schedule vs. standalone #5332:**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| kernel ISA, both Table kernels (`block_k` 64 / 256) | byte-identical (full text, 223 VGPR / 0 spill, counts, `s_waitcnt`) — `cta_resident`-independent |
| schedule table, identity cut vs. general built cut at equal `cta_resident` | byte-identical, all fields |
| `build_tiles` at `q_per_block == 1` | skipped (identity); `cu_tiles` no longer allocated |
| host row bound `total_q > q.shape[0]` | raises on gfx950 |

The production `qlen1_kv64` keeps #5332's `SCHED_CTA_TARGET = 1024`, so its schedule table is
byte-identical to #5332 across **every** #5332 scenario, verified on hardware:

| scenario | schedule vs. #5332 |
|---|---|
| prefill fresh / causal / chunked | identical (16384 tiles ⇒ one CTA per tile; grid is `cta_resident`-independent) |
| decode (seqs 1 / 8 / 32 / 128) | identical (`cta_resident` 1024 = #5332's, same CTA split) |

(`cta_resident` is a `build_sched` input — it shapes the schedule, not the kernel ISA. `qlen1_kv256`
carries an untuned `512`, but it is off the gfx950 production path, so it does not affect any
number here.)

**Performance** — same-card A/B on `qlen1_kv64` at #5332's chunked shapes (25000 cols, bs 1/2/4),
`run_perftest` 50/10, min-of-25: unified matches standalone #5332 within noise (≤1%, never slower).
This is the expected result and it generalizes to every scenario above: the ISA is byte-identical
and the schedule table is byte-identical, so the timed kernel is the same machine code on the same
table — the unification only drops one `build_tiles` launch per forward.

title: WORKAROUND - fix a1_scale out-of-bounds read in fmoe_fp8_blockscale_g1u1
body:
`fmoe_fp8_blockscale_g1u1` indexes the activation scale by `sorted_ids // topk`, so it can touch row `sorted_ids.numel() // topk`. `sorted_ids` is padded out to whole blocks per expert, but `per_group_quant_hip` allocates the scale with exactly one row per token, so the kernel reads `(num_experts * block_size - topk) // topk` rows past the end of the buffer.

The values there are read and discarded, so the over-read is usually invisible: the caching allocator normally has slack after the buffer. It becomes a hard memory access fault whenever the scale happens to be allocated at the tail of an allocator segment, since the next page is unmapped.

Pad the scale to the row count the kernel can address and return a view with the original shape, so the read lands on mapped memory without changing any observable value.

Reproduced on gfx950 with DeepSeek-V3.2 (per_1x128, topk=2, num_experts=8, block_size=32), where the kernel reads 1024 bytes past the scale. Padding to fewer rows than `sorted_ids.numel() // topk + 1` still faults 3/3; padding to that bound or beyond passes 3/3. Filling the padded tail with 0.0, 1.0, and 1e30 all produce byte-identical model output, confirming the tail is read but unused.

`op_tests/test_moe_blockscale.py` shows the same 6 pre-existing a8w8 asm checkAllclose failures with and without this change, over identical shapes.

---
AI assistance was used for this PR. All changes reviewed by submitter.

title: [HIP] Mask partial vectors in sampling kernels
body:
## Summary

Fix out-of-bounds vector accesses in the sampling kernels when the vocabulary size is not divisible by the vector width.

The implementation separates the branch-free full-vector path from the final partial-vector path, preserving bulk-path performance while making tail loads and stores bounds-safe.

This covers:

- `greedy_sample`
- `random_sample_outer_exponential`
- `random_sample`
- `mixed_sample_outer_exponential`
- `mixed_sample`
- `exponential`

## Problem

The kernels previously entered a vector load or store whenever the vector's starting offset was less than `N`. For a final partial vector, that could access elements beyond the end of the row.

Depending on allocation layout, those accesses could read the next row, sample an invalid token, or overwrite memory following an exponential-output row.

## Implementation

- Keep complete vector loads and stores on a branch-free bulk path.
- Handle only the final partial vector with scalar-masked helpers.
- Pad invalid input lanes with `-inf`.
- Pad invalid external-exponential lanes with `1.0`.
- Store only valid lanes from the final exponential vector.
- Distribute the greedy tail across lanes instead of serializing it in one lane.
- Preserve one Philox vector draw per owned vector, including a partial vector.
- Leave public APIs, launch geometry, and generator ownership unchanged.

The sampling test also now forces an independent FP32 reference buffer. Previously:

```python
logits = input.to(torch.float)
logits.div_(...)
```

aliased and repeatedly modified the original input when it was already FP32. Using `copy=True` prevents benchmark iterations from corrupting their input.

## Validation

Hardware:

- AMD Instinct MI100
- `gfx908:sramecc+:xnack-`
- PyTorch 2.10.0 with ROCm 7.2

Deterministic tail coverage:

```bash
for dtype in bf16 fp16 fp32; do
  AITER_REBUILD=0 python op_tests/test_sample.py \
    --tail-only \
    -d "$dtype" \
    -n 1 17 4097 16385
done
```

All 12 dtype/size cases passed. Each case exercises greedy sampling, both random paths, both mixed paths, and guarded exponential output.

Reference comparisons were also run for:

- BF16, FP16, and FP32
- `M=1,32`
- aligned `N=32000`
- partial-vector `N=32003`
- greedy, random, and mixed sampling
- internal and external exponential generation

All comparisons passed with exact token equality.

Additional large-vocabulary BF16 coverage passed at `N=151936` and `N=151937`.

The translation unit also compiles directly for gfx908 without private-memory use or register spills.

## Performance

The bulk/tail split was compared against the initial bounds-safe implementation, which performed bounds checks throughout the vector loop. Values below are three-run medians on MI100:

| Path | Shape | Initial safe patch | Bulk/tail implementation | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Greedy | M1 × 32000 | 8.612 µs | 7.173 µs | 16.7% |
| Greedy | M32 × 32000 | 8.823 µs | 7.450 µs | 15.6% |
| Greedy | M1 × 151936 | 22.772 µs | 20.468 µs | 10.1% |
| Greedy | M32 × 151936 | 21.687 µs | 20.341 µs | 6.2% |
| Random, external exponential | M32 × 32000 | 39.721 µs | 37.622 µs | 5.3% |
| Random, internal exponential | M32 × 32000 | 41.356 µs | 35.648 µs | 13.8% |
| Random, external exponential | M1 × 151936 | 108.752 µs | 99.754 µs | 8.3% |
| Random, internal exponential | M1 × 151936 | 166.134 µs | 146.698 µs | 11.7% |

Across the measured aligned-shape matrix, the bulk/tail implementation was 5.3%–26.5% faster than the initial bounds-safe version.

This performance comparison is against the first correctness implementation, not a claim of speedup over the previous out-of-bounds upstream path.

## CI impact

No workflow or runner configuration is changed. This does not add a required gfx908 CI job.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Assert SPLIT_UNMASKED_LOOP is not used with sliding window
[SMI] Add opt-in summary plots and raw-sample timelines
body:
SMI benchmark results currently require manual processing to compare cases, and aggregate logs discard the timing of individual observations. This adds opt-in automatic summary reports and lossless raw-sample capture with a standalone per-case timeline renderer.

- `AITER_SMI_PLOT=1` captures summary records and renders a report at normal process exit. `AITER_SMI_PLOT_DIR` defaults to `./smi_plots`; each process gets a separate run directory. Existing stdout and `AITER_SMI_OUTPUT_PATH` output are preserved.
- `AITER_SMI_TRACE=1` independently saves every collected sample and its timestamp, plus window boundaries and benchmark metadata. `AITER_SMI_TRACE_DIR` defaults to `./smi_traces`. Raw records are written after each monitoring window, outside the polling loop.
- `aiter/smi_plot.py` renders existing logs or directories into all-test, per-test, and per-case summary views. `aiter/smi_trace_plot.py` explicitly renders raw traces into per-case timelines, comparing variants in separate columns with clocks, power, activity, temperature, and VRAM panels.
- Reports include PNG/SVG plots, an HTML index, CSV, and a manifest. Timeline plots preserve every observation at its actual timestamp without smoothing, resampling, or downsampling; missing and firmware `N/A` readings remain gaps. Aggregate-only logs cannot reconstruct timelines.

Matplotlib is optional and the renderers work without a GPU. Automatic summary rendering runs in a CPU-only subprocess after the benchmark. Detailed timeline rendering is an explicit CLI step. Identical inputs/options produce deterministic report content within the same rendering environment. Documentation covers toggles, output paths, regeneration, and sample interpretation in `docs/smi_plotting.md`.

Validation: 30 combined CPU unit tests pass, plus Black, Ruff, and `git diff --check`. Tested inside `distracted_wu` on b9-2 across six GEMM shapes with both preshuffle variants: 12 ten-second monitoring windows produced 2,403 timestamped samples at a median 50.097 ms interval. All timestamps and original sample dictionaries were retained in the CSV, and six case plots were checked against the raw data. The existing summary path generated its 12-record/eight-plot report, and all 19 container compatibility tests passed. The benchmark source was preserved.

Two shapes emitted elementwise tolerance warnings but passed the benchmark's relative-L2 gate; A-preshuffle and split-K checks passed.

title: [ASM] [HIP] [CI] Mixed MXFP6/MXFP4 GEMMs
body:
## Motivation

Add production-ready gfx950 GEMMs for mixed MXFP6/MXFP4 operand orders.
These formats target the performance-quality region between A4W4 and A6W6:
they preserve substantially more BF16 cosine similarity than A4W4 while
reducing operand traffic and GEMM latency relative to A6W6.

## Summary

This change adds gfx950 assembly GEMMs for both mixed MXFP operand orders:

- A6W4: MXFP6 E2M3 activations and MXFP4 E2M1 weights.
- A4W6: MXFP4 E2M1 activations and MXFP6 E2M3 weights.
- E8M0 block scaling with one scale per 32 K elements.
- A fused gfx950 HIP path for H32 rotation, MXFP4 quantization, compact C0
  packing, and scale packing.
- Python APIs, ctypes launchers, JIT recipes, AITER-mangled code-object
  manifests, and numerical/ABI/compile tests.
- Shape-tuned runtime dispatch and tuner entry points for both operand orders.

The implementation reuses the upstream MXFP6 H32 packing contract. Applying
the same orthonormal H32 transform to both operands preserves the underlying
GEMM while reducing the impact of per-block outliers.

The shared MXFP6 packer is hardened against oversized dimensions, misaligned
buffers, and extreme-value Hadamard overflow while preserving
`torch.ops.aiter.quant_mxfp6_gemm_hip_out`. The default gfx950 path uses the
full-range HIP packer. The legacy Triton packer remains only as a private
bounded-input parity reference; it is not publicly selectable because it
cannot safely cover the full BF16/FP16 and E8M0 ranges.

## Scope

- Hardware: gfx950.
- Output: BF16.
- Tile: 256x256x128.
- Eight generic MFMA32 code objects are included: four per operand order.
- No model-specific shape branches or Wan-only code objects are included.
- Low-level launch APIs require physically padded M/N multiples of 256 and a
  padded K multiple of 128. High-level APIs accept logical dimensions.

## Tuning

The tuners enumerate compatible prebuilt kernels from each HSA manifest,
validate output against the safe default, and retain a non-default winner only
when every paired repeat wins and median gain is at least 0.5%. Runtime lookup
tries an exact logical shape before its physical 256x256x128 padded shape.

```bash
python3 csrc/gemm_a6w4/gemm_a6w4_tune.py \
  --all --shape_grouped \
  --gain-guard-warmup 30 --gain-guard-iters 150 \
  --gain-guard-reps 15 --min-gain-pct 0.5

python3 csrc/gemm_a4w6/gemm_a4w6_tune.py \
  --all --shape_grouped \
  --gain-guard-warmup 30 --gain-guard-iters 150 \
  --gain-guard-reps 15 --min-gain-pct 0.5
```

Custom runtime tables can be selected with `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A6W4_ASM` and
`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A4W6_ASM`. Tuner-generated keys and runtime dispatch both
honor the `CU_NUM` override.

### Tuning results

Both formats were tuned over the same 57 diffusion GEMM shapes used by the
A6W6 tuning flow. Every non-default winner was revalidated on one MI355X over
15 paired repeats.

| Format | Non-default winners | Maximum gain | Geometric-mean gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A6W4 | 11 / 57 | 10.49% | 0.95% |
| A4W6 | 9 / 57 | 8.24% | 0.54% |

All 114 tuned dispatch cases produced exact output parity with zero
mismatches.

The `N == K` fallback difference is intentional and format-specific. For
`9450x5120x5120`, paired measurements selected:

- A6W4 grouped: 125.904 us versus natural 127.339 us (1.14% faster).
- A4W6 natural: 128.002 us versus grouped 129.181 us (0.92% faster).

## Performance

Measured on one 256-CU gfx950. Values are medians after 30 warmups,
100 iterations, and 15 alternating repeats. Inputs are synthetic BF16 tensors.
Quantization plus GEMM includes dynamic activation quantization; weights are
prepared ahead of time. Cosine similarity is against the BF16 GEMM.

### GEMM-only throughput (TFLOP/s)

| M x N x K | A4W4 | A4W6 | A6W4 | A6W6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 x 5120 x 5120 | 2213.85 | 937.33 | 935.88 | 780.71 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 5120 | 3887.87 | 3881.78 | 3930.84 | 3449.79 |
| 9450 x 13824 x 5120 | 4714.27 | 3889.24 | 3983.04 | 3485.57 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 13824 | 5431.62 | 4330.75 | 4355.72 | 3846.43 |

### Quantization plus GEMM throughput (TFLOP/s)

| M x N x K | A4W4 | A4W6 | A6W4 | A6W6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 x 5120 x 5120 | 1067.14 | 800.22 | 789.74 | 681.28 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 5120 | 3369.79 | 3195.18 | 3129.93 | 2811.88 |
| 9450 x 13824 x 5120 | 4284.04 | 3559.83 | 3601.38 | 3180.85 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 13824 | 4350.68 | 3448.80 | 3360.12 | 3041.51 |

### Cosine similarity versus BF16

| M x N x K | A4W4 | A4W6 | A6W4 | A6W6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 x 5120 x 5120 | 0.986685 | 0.992918 | 0.992917 | 0.999192 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 5120 | 0.986704 | 0.992931 | 0.992928 | 0.999192 |
| 9450 x 13824 x 5120 | 0.986707 | 0.992927 | 0.992927 | 0.999192 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 13824 | 0.986700 | 0.992928 | 0.992926 | 0.999191 |

### A6W6 base-versus-head regression check

The shared MXFP6 quantization path was compared against benchmark base
`49c6fdd4558a45b2cd34e713b74d0280a2a61c88` (main at the time of measurement)
on the same GPU over all 57 shapes from
`a6w6_blockscale_untuned_gemm.csv`.

The protocol used three independent base and head sweeps per backend, each with
30 warmups, 100 iterations, and 15 alternating repeats. Unchanged GEMM-only
latency was the clock/contention control; a sweep sample was discarded only
when that control was more than 2% above the revision's fastest sample.

| Backend | Metric | Geomean delta | Median delta | P95 delta | Range | Shapes >1% |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| HIP | GEMM-only control | -0.023% | -0.021% | +0.572% | -1.059% to +0.677% | 0 / 57 |
| HIP | Quantize + GEMM | +0.181% | +0.138% | +0.815% | -0.886% to +0.949% | 0 / 57 |
| Triton | GEMM-only control | +0.011% | +0.030% | +0.410% | -0.507% to +0.452% | 0 / 57 |
| Triton | Quantize + GEMM | +0.045% | +0.078% | +0.461% | -0.790% to +0.744% | 0 / 57 |

All 57 base/head kernel selections matched.

The Triton figures measure the unchanged private legacy packer as a parity and
performance control. Production gfx950 dispatch uses the full-range HIP
packer.

## Test plan and results

- Clean-cache JIT builds pass for `module_quant`, `module_gemm_a6w4_asm`, and
  `module_gemm_a4w6_asm`.
- 96 focused mixed-MXFP operator tests pass on gfx950.
- 102 fast tuning/configuration tests pass.
- `mp=1` and an explicit two-GPU tuner pipeline pass for both operand orders.
- Tuned `--run_config` validation passes 57/57 shapes for each format.
- The A6W4/A4W6 test files follow
  `.claude/skills/aiter-op-test/SKILL.md`: `@benchmark`, candidate dictionaries,
  `run_perftest`, `checkAllclose`, us/TFLOPS/TB/s/err columns, standard CLI
  sweeps, and markdown summary tables.
- Fast deterministic tuning validation is included in normal PR test sharding.
  Long-running tuner pipeline and all-shape run-config tests remain
  scheduled/manual.
- Quantized-reference checks cover production projection shapes, simultaneous
  M/N/K tails, and every MXFP4 scale-round mode.
- Every retained MFMA32 variant is bitwise checked on simultaneous M/N/K
  padding; grouped and long-K dispatch paths are also exercised.
- Dynamic quantize-to-GEMM paths pass `torch.compile(dynamic=True,
  fullgraph=True)`, including exact and padded tuning-table matches.
- ctypes validation rejects undersized, oversized, and misaligned packed
  buffers.
- Manifest tests enforce exact manifest/directory membership, AITER-mangled
  symbols, layout metadata, ELF format, and tuned-kernel membership.
- Python formatting, Ruff, shell syntax, whitespace, and lint checks pass.

Focused command:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 AITER_MXFP6_QUANT_BACKEND=hip \
python -m pytest -q \
  op_tests/test_mixed_mxfp_manifests.py \
  op_tests/test_quant_mxfp6_gemm.py \
  op_tests/test_quant_mxfp4_gemm_fused.py \
  op_tests/test_gemm_a6w4.py \
  op_tests/test_gemm_a4w6.py
```

The standard operator benchmark tables are emitted by:

```bash
python op_tests/test_gemm_a6w4.py
python op_tests/test_gemm_a4w6.py
```

The cross-format comparison can be reproduced with:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 AITER_MXFP6_QUANT_BACKEND=hip \
python op_tests/op_benchmarks/hip/bench_gemm_mixed_mxfp.py \
  --output /tmp/mixed_mxfp.csv
```

## Downstream integration and relationship to #5358

[xDiT](https://github.com/xdit-project/xDiT) is the planned first downstream
consumer. Its downstream PR will follow after this AITER API lands. The
integration under development uses the public `gemm_a6w4` / `gemm_a4w6` APIs,
prepares packed weights during model setup, packs activations dynamically, and
shares one MXFP6 activation pack across Wan QKV/KV projections.

[#5358](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5358) is an independent FlyDSL W4
backend:

- This PR uses the H32-rotated A6W6 packed ABI and additionally provides A4W6.
- #5358 uses an unrotated, FP8-padded FP6 activation layout.
- The public APIs, packed buffers, dispatch, and tuning namespaces are
  distinct and cannot be substituted without repacking.
- This ASM backend uses `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A6W4_ASM` and
  `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A4W6_ASM`; the FlyDSL backend uses
  `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A6W4`.

## JIT behavior

`develop=True` on the fused packer binding does not disable persistent JIT
caching. Module resolution and reuse occur before that branch. It enables the
torch-free `aiter_tensor_t` conversion, pybind ABI validation, and current HIP
stream handoff required by `module_quant`, matching the existing MXFP6 binding.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused gfx950 correctness tests.
- [x] Fullgraph compile coverage.
- [x] Standard operator benchmark tables.
- [x] Base-versus-head A6W6 regression sweep.
- [x] Shape tuning and runtime configuration.
- [x] Fast tuning validation in PR CI.
- [x] Generic dispatch only.
- [ ] Full upstream CI on the final branch head.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Kimi-K3][ROCm] Add merged MoE front
body:
## Summary

Adds a merged MoE-front kernel for Kimi-K3 on gfx950, plus tuned GEMM
configurations and numerical tests for it.

Kimi-K3's MoE front is three separate projections of the same `x[M, 7168]`:
shared gate/up `7168 -> 1536`, router logits `7168 -> 896`, and the routed
latent `7168 -> 3584`. This kernel combines them into one
`BF16 x BF16 -> FP32` GEMM (`7168 -> 6016`) followed by a Triton split/SiTU
epilogue that emits the BF16 shared SiTU intermediate, the FP32 router logits,
and the BF16 routed latent. Routed experts are untouched and still use the
existing AITER MXFP4 backend.

## Supported shapes

```text
1..16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 192, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048
```

`32..192` is the MTP decode bucket. A pure-decode step submits
`num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens, so with the usual
`num_speculative_tokens=3` any server past four concurrent sequences asks for a
count above 16. The gate itself lives in the companion vLLM change; what this
PR adds for those shapes is numerical coverage, since the decode test
previously stopped at `m=16`.

`kimik3_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` gains FP32-output entries at `N=6016, K=7168,
gfx950, cu_num=256` for `M = 7, 14, 16, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048`. Config lookup
is keyed on output dtype and pads `M` up to the next multiple of 16 below 256,
so every `M` in `1..16` resolves to the `M=16` entry. The `32..192` bucket has
no FP32-output entry yet and therefore runs on torch's default hipBLASLt
heuristic; the end-to-end numbers below already include that fallback, so
tuning those shapes is remaining headroom rather than a prerequisite.

`M=4096` and `M=8192` are intentionally excluded after controlled retesting
showed regressions.

## Kernel results

Single-GPU gfx950, complete front, CUDA Graph:

| M | Speedup vs native front |
|---|---:|
| 1..16 | 1.645x – 2.140x |
| 512 | 1.224x |
| 1024 | 1.185x |
| 1536 | 1.162x |
| 2048 | 1.129x |
| 4096 | 0.960x, excluded |
| 8192 | 0.882x, excluded |

All tested shapes pass numerical checks, including exact router top-16
selection.

## End-to-end results

MI355X, TP8, DSpark MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=3`), via the companion vLLM
change. Both arms of each comparison ran back to back on one node with
identical server arguments, KV configuration and client invocation.

### 8K/1K fixed sequence length

ISL 8192, OSL 1024, prefix caching disabled, 610 requests per arm, zero
failures.

| Concurrency | Decode M | Output throughput | Median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 130.1 -> 135.9 tok/s, **+4.43%** | 7.15 -> 6.83 ms, **-4.53%** |
| 4 | 16 | 369.9 -> 380.5 tok/s, **+2.87%** | 9.25 -> 8.97 ms, **-2.98%** |
| 8 | 32 | 582.8 -> 606.5 tok/s, **+4.07%** | 11.99 -> 11.31 ms, **-5.66%** |
| 16 | 64 | 799.8 -> 814.3 tok/s, **+1.82%** | 18.00 -> 17.65 ms, **-1.98%** |
| 32 | 128 | 1030.2 -> 1044.7 tok/s, **+1.41%** | 28.95 -> 28.55 ms, **-1.37%** |

Median TTFT moves by at most 0.58% in any cell: prefill in this workload is
8130-8190 tokens per step and never matches a supported shape, so the gain is
decode-only. Repeating two of these rows independently bounds their
reproducibility at 0.13-0.80 pp.

### AgenticX trace replay, 3600 s per cell

| Metric | C1 | C4 |
|---|---|---|
| Total throughput | 10212 -> 10533 tok/s, **+3.14%** | 19211 -> 19617 tok/s, **+2.11%** |
| Output throughput | 84.77 -> 87.75 tok/s, **+3.52%** | 139.20 -> 146.61 tok/s, **+5.33%** |
| P90 TPOT | 8.92 -> 8.47 ms, **-5.03%** | 13.52 -> 13.36 ms, **-1.19%** |
| P90 interactivity | 112.1 -> 118.1 tok/s, **+5.29%** | 73.9 -> 74.8 tok/s, **+1.20%** |

Read the total-throughput row with care: it does not measure this change.
Input tokens are over 99% of all tokens in this trace and 97.6% of them hit the
prefix cache, so total throughput is close to (input tokens handed to this arm)
/ wall clock. Trace replay assigns sessions dynamically and the two arms did
not get an identical token mix -- the optimized arm received 3.04% more input
tokens at C1 and 2.81% more at C4. Dividing the measured total-throughput delta
by each arm's input-token and duration ratio leaves a residual of +0.00% at C1
and +0.02% at C4, so that row is token mix and nothing else.

Output throughput and P90 TPOT are the rows that carry the effect: both are
normalized per output token, so neither depends on how much input the arm
happened to receive. Note that they disagree in shape with the total row at C4,
where output throughput is +5.33% against a total of +2.11% -- the smaller
number there is the noisier one, not the more conservative one.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, full 1319-question test split, 5-shot, greedy. This is the check the
numerical tests structurally cannot make: they compare the fused kernel against
a `torch.mm` reference built from the same merged weight, so they are blind to
the merged front slicing its router logits out of a `7168 -> 6016` accumulator
where the native front runs a separate `7168 -> 896` GEMM. Both are
BF16 x BF16 -> FP32, but the wider shape picks a different solution with a
different accumulation order, and that rounding difference can flip a borderline
top-16 expert selection.

Both arms ran back to back on one node at `max_num_seqs=8` with
`num_speculative_tokens=3` and block rejection sampling, so a saturated decode
step submits 32 tokens and the merged front is the decode path for effectively
the whole run.

| Filter | Baseline | Merged |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9659 | 0.9719 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9651 | 0.9712 |

Both arms answer the same questions, so the paired view is the informative one:
1295 of 1319 answers agree, 16 flip to correct and 8 flip to incorrect, an exact
two-sided sign test on the 24 discordant pairs giving p = 0.15. The merged front
is therefore indistinguishable from the native front on accuracy. The +0.6 pp is
run-to-run nondeterminism, not a claimed improvement.


## Validation

- Ruff (`ruff==0.16.0`, the version `pre-checks.yaml` pins), `ruff format` and
  `git diff --check`: passed. The two `EXE001` findings that remain in the
  repository are in unrelated flydsl files and predate this PR.
- gfx950 AITER tests: `17 passed`.
- Dependent vLLM Kimi-K3 tests: `59 passed`.

Companion vLLM PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55811
