## Verification

- Host-side unit tests over the table's structure, the k-group expansion, the bound, and which shapes the early stop is built into -- it is on by default but dropped under `ordered`, under the candidate-buffer path and on an all-short build, none of which run the pass it replaces. They walk whatever the table holds, so a card added later is a table entry and nothing else.
- A GPU-gated test, in the same file, that walks the shipped table: at each band's widths it takes the row counts just inside and just outside the band, asserts the kernel the table names is the one that launches -- by patching the launch site, not by inferring -- and that the selected values are a row's true top k. One k per group, and cells too large to allocate in a unit test are skipped. Every cell runs twice, once on planted logits whose top k sit at known positions and once on random ones; ragged `seq_lens` with the longest row exactly on the bound get the same treatment.
- Across the sweeps above, every arm's output was checked against `torch.topk` over each row's live slice: 7600 cells over four cards, no incorrect result. On the 3600 padded cells everything past the live length held a poison value, so a read past `seq_lens` would have come back as a wrong answer rather than a plausible one.

## What is still open

- **Ragged batches are calibrated optimistically.** The gate decides once per call on the longest row, because the kernel is configured once per launch, and the sweeps hold uniform batches. A row that would win 1.31x on its own measures 0.66x when a much longer row shares its batch. Correctness is unaffected; the win is.
- **Reduce the reps with `min` instead of the median** and two entries show near-ties. 304 CU reads 3 losing cells, worst 0.98x, at k=512 and a live length of 8192; 256 CU reads 2, worst 0.997x, at width 131072 and 32 rows. All five clear the kernel their own card runs -- by 1.16x to 2.19x on 256 CU -- and lose to a third kernel by under 2%.
- **gfx1250 is unmeasured** and has no entry, so the gate declines it and it runs exactly what it runs today. gfx950 is measured at one CU count.
- **CI.** The routing test skips without a device, and the widest band edges are too large to allocate inside a unit test.
- **Indices only.** Emitting values is a kernel change, not proposed here.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Kernel] Add gfx950 stochastic MXFP4 quantization
body:
## Summary

Extend the existing `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` operation with opt-in stochastic
rounding for BF16 and FP32 inputs on gfx950.

Closes #5530.

## Implementation

- Reuse `_dynamic_mxfp4_quant_kernel` through a `USE_SR` constexpr instead of
  adding a second launchable kernel.
- Keep the existing deterministic path unchanged when `use_sr=False`.
- Reuse the EVEN E8M0 scale path and use
  `v_cvt_scalef32_sr_pk_fp4_{bf16,f32}` for stochastic E2M1 payload conversion.
- Expose keyword-only `use_sr`, `philox_seed`, and `philox_offset` arguments.
- Include `USE_SR` in the kernel `repr`.
- Add SR coverage to the existing MXFP4 unit-test and benchmark files.

The Philox counter for each row and packed-pair group is derived from the
global tensor position. A launch consumes `M * N / 8` counters; callers that
need independent noise must use non-overlapping offset ranges.

This PR does not add 2-D scaling, transpose, shuffle, dual-layout output,
dequantization, or RHT/Hadamard functionality.

## Validation

gfx950 correctness and regression tests:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q \
  op_tests/triton_tests/quant/test_quant_mxfp4.py
```

Result: `40 passed, 48 skipped`.

Benchmark smoke tests:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. python \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_quant_mxfp4.py \
  --shape 32 32 --provider triton --dtype bf16 --use-sr --metric time

GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. python \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_quant_mxfp4.py \
  --shape 32 32 --provider triton --dtype fp32 --use-sr --metric time
```

Black, Ruff, `compileall`, and `git diff --check` pass for all four changed
files.

## Performance

MI350X/gfx950, BF16, 25 warmup iterations and 100 timed repetitions:

| Shape | Triton RTN (ms) | AITER SR (ms) | HIP EVEN (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 x 4096 | 0.006936 | 0.008984 | 0.006506 |
| 2048 x 4096 | 0.011835 | 0.011528 | 0.011821 |
| 8192 x 4096 | 0.027784 | 0.028087 | 0.035532 |
| 2048 x 14336 | 0.026253 | 0.024248 | 0.031273 |
| 8192 x 14336 | 0.080494 | 0.080125 | 0.102703 |

`quant_mxfp4_hip` is a deterministic payload conversion and is included only
as a performance reference; it is not a semantic replacement for this SR path.

## Scope

- No new dependency.
- No breaking change; stochastic rounding is opt-in.
- No tuning JSON is added because this extends the existing statically
  scheduled kernel rather than introducing a new schedule or config lookup.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the pull-request guidelines.

title: [CI] Assign a PR to everyone who committed to it
body:
A second step on the existing title and label workflow rather than a new one: it wants the same trigger, the same permissions and the same PR, and the header already offers no-auto-title as the way to opt a PR out entirely, so that label now covers this as well.

For each changed file the step reads the commit history and counts who wrote it, then assigns the heaviest contributors.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [FlyDSL] FlyDSL gemm_decode: small-M dense GEMM kernels (BF16)
body:
## Motivation

LLM autoregressive decode runs linear projections at M=1..5 tokens per step. A standard 16×16 MFMA tile wastes ≥75% of compute slots at these sizes. This PR adds a FlyDSL BF16 decode GEMM optimised for small M, plus the tuned config rows for the shapes where it wins.

Target hardware: gfx942 and gfx950. Measured on MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU) and MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU).
Target shapes: Kimi-K3 TP8 decode GEMMs, N=896…40960, K=128…8448. Generic — no model-specific names in kernel or dispatch code.

## Technical Details

Two complementary FlyDSL policies, selected by a runtime tuner:

**Wave** (`gemm_decode_wave.py`) — warp-per-scalar output-centric GEMM. One wavefront owns one tile of (M×N) output scalars; K split across 64 lanes, reduced by butterfly XOR. `v_dot2_f32_bf16` on gfx950, scalar/packed FP32 on gfx942. Wins at M=1,2.

**BlockMFMA** (`gemm_decode_block_mfma.py`) — MFMA block policy with LDS A-staging and software prefetch. Wins at M≥3.

**Entry point** (`gemm_kernels.py`): `gemm_decode_bf16(A, B, C, config)`, dispatching to either policy via a tuned config from `iter_gemm_decode_configs`. The kernel exists only for M≤5; the dispatcher honours a `flydsl_decode` row on exact M match only, never through M padding.

**Tuned configs** — `flydsl_decode` rows in `kimik3_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` for gfx950 and gfx942, M=1..5, covering the Kimi-K3 TP8 decode shapes. Most land where the dispatcher previously fell through to `torch`. On gfx950 the rest replace an existing `flydsl` or `triton` row, and each of those only where graph replay showed decode beats the incumbent for that exact shape and M. On gfx942 nothing is replaced — see below.

**Duplicate shapes across model configs.** A few keys at `(2112,7168)` also existed in `dsv3_` and `kimik2_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv`, and `(3584,7168)` arrived in main via #5702 while this PR was open. Since the runtime merges every `*bf16_tuned_gemm*` file into one keyspace, duplicates raise at merge time. All were resolved by the repository's own guard — `test_config_shape_collision.py --fix`, lowest-`us` wins — not by hand. That accounts for the deletions in the two other model files.

**Two fixes needed along the way.** The AOT path applied the bias placeholder substitution twice, failing every bias-free row. The tuner's candidate selection discarded valid decode configs before benchmarking them.

## Performance

Measured against the kernel the config named for the same shape before this PR — the existing row, or `torch` where none existed. Both kernels invoked by name, dispatcher out of the loop.

Packed HIP graph, wall clock over launches, four rotating weights, alternating A/B/B/A pairs scored per pair, incumbent timed against itself as a null control (2% threshold). Both sides checked against an FP32 reference before each timing.

gfx950 (MI355X, 256 CU), every row in this PR, **3 independent passes**:

| M | cells | better | tied | worse | ours, µs | previous, µs | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 19 | 1 | 0 | 306.0 | 404.6 | +24.4% |
| 2 | 17 | 17 | 0 | 0 | 299.3 | 379.8 | +21.2% |
| 3 | 18 | 18 | 0 | 0 | 307.7 | 406.5 | +24.3% |
| 4 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 0 | 276.9 | 340.2 | +18.6% |
| 5 | 13 | 13 | 0 | 0 | 270.4 | 329.5 | +17.9% |
| **all** | **82** | **81** | **1** | **0** | **1460.4** | **1860.6** | **+21.5%** |

**Every row confirmed in every pass, zero regressions.** The one tie is `(7168,1536)` at M=1, where the kernels sit 0.3% apart; it never lost a pass.

An earlier revision of this description quoted −9%…−25% against `wvSplitK`. Those were taken against a September-2025 build of that kernel and are withdrawn.

**Downstream:** the same rows measured end to end through vLLM's `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` give +4.7% on M=1..4 against `wvSplitK` — a kernel aiter cannot select, as it lives in vLLM's own extension. Wiring and caveats in [vllm-project/vllm#55860](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55860).

gfx942 (MI325X, 304 CU), every row in this PR, **3 independent passes**:

| M | cells | better | tied | worse | ours, µs | previous, µs | gain |
|---|-------|--------|------|-------|----------|--------------|------|
| 1 | 21 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 419.1 | 560.9 | +25.3% |
| 2 | 21 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 436.6 | 562.8 | +22.4% |
| 3 | 19 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 444.9 | 550.6 | +19.2% |
| 4 | 19 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 421.3 | 516.5 | +18.4% |
| 5 | 11 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 376.3 | 423.0 | +11.0% |
| **all** | **91** | **91** | **0** | **0** | **2098.1** | **2613.8** | **+19.7%** |

**Every row confirmed in every pass, zero regressions, no batch discarded by the null control.** Here `previous` is always the heuristic fallback, which resolved to `torch`: at the branch point no bf16 config carried a `gfx942` row with `cu_num=304`, so all 91 rows are additions and none replaces an existing row. The rows are keyed `(gfx942, cu_num=304)`, which also matches MI300X; that part was not re-measured.

**Shapes deliberately left without a row.** 11 cells at M=3,4,5 where `opus` is faster — `router` at M=5 by 22%, `(7168,8448)` at M=5 by 9%, six other long-K shapes at M=5 by 0.5…6%, `router` and `shared down` at M=3, `latent down` at M=4 — confirmed on two cards with 0–2 wins out of 90 pairs. Plus 3 cells where the tuner and graph replay disagree reproducibly (`(7168,8448)` at M=4, `attention O` and `(4608,1536)` at M=5): five tuner runs rank `opus` first, graph replay ranks the decode kernel first by up to 1520/1520 pairs.

**Full evidence** — protocol, benches, raw records, and the measurement errors made and corrected along the way — is attached as `pr4114_evidence.tar.gz`.

## Architecture support

- **gfx950**: Wave uses `v_dot2_f32_bf16`; BlockMFMA uses MFMA with two-stage prefetch
- **gfx942**: Wave uses scalar_f32 contraction; BlockMFMA uses single-stage prefetch; both paths correctness-tested

## Test Plan

- `op_tests/test_flydsl_decode_gemm.py` — a standard op_test: `python3 <file>` runs the five correctness cases (Wave no-bias, Wave with bias and odd N/K tails, BlockMFMA global, BlockMFMA full LDS with K padding, BlockMFMA persistent-N multi-turn) and then the perf sweep with `checkAllclose` against an FP32 reference. `pytest <file>` runs the same five cases. No CI script changes are needed — the file sits where the runner already scans.
- `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_config_shape_collision` — `Ran 17 tests ... OK`. The config keyspace stays collision-free across every model file; includes a positive control (a planted duplicate must be caught).
- Row-level verification: every row confirmed over 3 independent passes, zero regressions (raw records in the attached archive).
- Black and Ruff 0.16.0 (the CI pin) clean on all changed files.
- CI on MI300X (gfx942) and MI355X (gfx950).

## Attachment
[pr4114_evidence.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32519718/pr4114_evidence.tar.gz)

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: [FlyDSL] gfx950 FP8 paged DSA indexer score-plus-local-TopK
body:
## Summary
- Add a gfx950 FlyDSL operator that scores FP8 paged DSA indexer K (`H=32`, `D=128`) and keeps exact local top-k per history split, then merges the split-local bags with a split-aware decode TopK. The public entry points are `flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_local_topk` and `flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_topk`.
- This is the decode `next_n=1` path only (`q` is `[B,1,32,128]`). It does not include mixed per-request speculated widths, MTP group-max / harvest, or persistent/sorted Stage B.
- Motivation: long decode still pays `O(L)` indexer scoring, but it should not allocate or write the full `[rows, max_model_len]` FP32 logits tensor (128 MiB at 32 rows × 1M; 512 MiB at 128 rows).
- K pages must be `shuffle_weight(..., layout=(16,16))` (packed or split). That matches the vLLM DSA cache for `block_size > 1`.

## Merge path

Stage A holds every retained candidate's key in registers, so it also fills the merge's pass-0 histogram on the way out. The merge then starts at pass 1. Supporting this needed a few hooks on `top_k_per_row_decode`: `split_width` and `use_split_counts` bind one chunk to one split's live prefix, `payload_indices` carries positions through the gather, `combine_histograms` folds the splits into a single histogram and zeroes each bin as the reduce consumes it (which is what leaves the workspace clean for the next call), and `precomputed_first_pass` skips the pass Stage A already did.

The existing public decode TopK path is unchanged: it builds with these hooks off and binds the two extra tensor arguments to operands it already holds.

## Serving / CUDA-graph usage

The extra intermediate is the merge workspace, not the candidate scores. Allocate it **once** outside capture; pass the same pair on every decode step. Do **not** `zero_()` between successful A→B calls. Stage A atomics into the histogram; the merge consumes it and writes every bin back to 0.

```python
from aiter.ops.flydsl.split_topk_merge import alloc_split_topk_merge_workspace

# rows = q.shape[0]
# hist: [rows, 1, 2048] int32    state: [rows, 6] int32
workspace = alloc_split_topk_merge_workspace(device, rows)  # zeros once

values, positions = flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_topk(
    q, kv, None, weights, lens, tables, k=2048, workspace=workspace,
)
```

Two-kernel form (caller also owns the `[rows, S, k]` bags):

```python
bags = flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_local_topk(..., workspace=workspace)
values, positions = split_topk_merge(
    *bags, k=k, precomputed_first_pass=True, workspace=workspace,
    out_scores=out_scores, out_positions=out_positions,
)
```

`num_splits == 1` has no merge and rejects `workspace`. If Stage A runs and merge does not, the histogram is dirty. Tests/benches may omit `workspace`; the wrapper then uses a process cache that zeros on first miss only.

Auto `num_splits` can pick 128; merge currently accepts at most 64 chunks. The numbers below clamp `S` to 64. Default `num_splits=None` raises on 1-row `L >= 256k`.

## Measured vs Gluon logits + decode TopK

Idle MI355X / gfx950, packed page-64 shuffled KV, `k=2048`, `next_n=1`, independent KV pages per request. CUDA-event medians, 10 warmup / 31 samples.

vLLM-shaped logits: always `[rows, max_model_len=1048576]`. Live `context_lens = L`. KV covers `L` only. Gluon and FlyDSL `top_k_per_row_decode` follow `L` (they do not scan the unused 1M tail); the allocation still fixes logits stride and TopK compile width at 1M. Compact never sees that tensor. Merge workspace and TopK outputs are persistent across timed calls.

### Compact speedup (Gluon+TopK ÷ compact). Above 1.00 compact is faster.

| L \ rows | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4k | 1.22 | 1.22 | 1.17 | 1.24 | 1.14 |
| 8k | 1.20 | 1.20 | 1.19 | 1.22 | 1.14 |
| 16k | 1.17 | 1.20 | 1.20 | 1.23 | 1.16 |
| 32k | 1.20 | 1.19 | 1.18 | 1.19 | 0.96 |
| 64k | 1.18 | 1.18 | 1.10 | 0.99 | 0.88 |
| 128k | 1.17 | 1.10 | 0.93 | 0.92 | 1.01 |
| 256k | 0.94 | 0.66 | 0.91 | 1.04 | 1.07 |
| 512k | 0.73 | 0.90 | 1.03 | 1.10 | 1.18 |
| 1M | 0.58 | 1.02 | 1.17 | 1.19 | 1.20 |

Geomean over these 45 cells: **1.07**. Compact wins 34/45.

### Raw device time, compact (µs)

| L \ rows | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4k | 58 | 60 | 62 | 62 | 62 |
| 8k | 58 | 61 | 61 | 62 | 61 |
| 16k | 60 | 60 | 61 | 62 | 63 |
| 32k | 59 | 61 | 61 | 64 | 75 |
| 64k | 60 | 62 | 65 | 76 | 108 |
| 128k | 60 | 67 | 79 | 109 | 171 |
| 256k | 76 | 113 | 113 | 172 | 267 |
| 512k | 101 | 118 | 175 | 268 | 447 |
| 1M | 140 | 188 | 269 | 447 | 836 |

### Raw device time, Gluon + decode TopK (µs)

| L \ rows | 1 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4k | 70 | 74 | 72 | 77 | 71 |
| 8k | 70 | 73 | 72 | 75 | 70 |
| 16k | 70 | 73 | 73 | 76 | 73 |
| 32k | 70 | 72 | 72 | 76 | 72 |
| 64k | 71 | 73 | 72 | 75 | 95 |
| 128k | 71 | 73 | 74 | 100 | 172 |
| 256k | 71 | 75 | 103 | 178 | 286 |
| 512k | 74 | 107 | 180 | 295 | 526 |
| 1M | 82 | 193 | 316 | 531 | 1007 |

- Compact wins short/medium `L` at every batch (`L ≤ 32k`, usually `L ≤ 64k`) and large-batch megatoken (`8–32 × 512k–1M`; **32×1M is 836 vs 1007 µs**).
- Gluon+TopK wins skinny long decode: **1×256k–1M** (worst **1×1M: 140 vs 82**) and a mid-length band at 16–32 rows (`16×64–128k`, `32×32–64k`).
- One-row Gluon stays ~70–82 µs from 4k to 1M; compact grows with `L` after `S` caps at 64. That is the B=1 1M hole. Earlier “we win 1M” numbers were 8/16/32 rows.

PR 4221 paged logits was not re-run here. Prior matched e2e at `next_n=1` did not beat Gluon+TopK; 4221’s edge is K reuse at `next_n≥2`, and it cannot launch large independent 1M caches (signed-i32 numel).

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_local_topk.py` on gfx950 (script-mode CI; edges + compact vs logits+TopK)
- [x] Caller-owned workspace stays all-zero after repeated A→B calls and CUDA-graph replay
- [x] Compact vs Gluon+TopK selected-score multisets agree within 3e-6 on the 1M-width grid
- [x] Public `flydsl_top_k_per_row_decode` still exact vs `torch.topk` at `(1, 1M, k=2048)`, `(8, 32K, k=512)`, `(4, 64K, k=128, next_n=2)`
- [ ] CI FlyDSL gfx950 job collects the new `op_tests` file

title: [FlyDSL] Add gfx950 FHMoE producer on gemm_moe_tune.py
body:
## Summary

gfx950 fused heterogeneous MoE (FHMoE, DSV4 I384) already serves through `fused_moe` + `aiter/configs/tuned_fhmoe.csv`. What was missing is a **producer**: a tuner that sweeps FlyDSL stage1×stage2 pairs, rejects fast-wrong kernels against torch, and writes a native tuned CSV (`block_m`, `kernelName1`, `kernelName2`, `us`).

This PR adds that producer as `FhmoeTuner` on the existing FMoE script (`gemm_moe_tune.py --fhmoe`), wires it into `op_tune.sh` and Tuning Tests like the other families, and **does not** replace the shipped 12-row `tuned_fhmoe.csv`.

FHMoE is its own family, not a flag on FMoE tests: different CLI (`--fhmoe`), different CSVs (`untuned_fhmoe.csv` / `tuned_fhmoe.csv` / `AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE`), gfx950-only, shared-expert + routed FP4 + shared FP8. Serving `fused_moe` / `aiter/fhmoe.py` are not in the diff.

## Tuner (`FhmoeTuner`)

Subclass of `FmoeTuner`, selected with `--fhmoe` (mutually exclusive with `--grouped-gemm` and `--mxfp4-flydsl` on the same `__main__`).

**Catalogue.** `aiter/configs/untuned_fhmoe.csv`: 12 DSV4 I384 rows, tokens 1,2,4,…,2048. Same shape keys as shipped `tuned_fhmoe.csv` (that file has no `us` column; the producer adds `us`).

**Arch gate.** `aiter/fhmoe.py` is `NotImplementedError` off gfx950. `gemm_moe_tune.py` multiplexes four tuners in one file, so the gate is in `__main__`: `--fhmoe` on a non-gfx950 process `SystemExit`s (`--fhmoe is only supported on gfx950`). Grouped GEMM already does the same for gfx1250. This is **not** A6W6’s `RuntimeError` inside `tune()`: A6W6 is its own script, so a unittest subprocess can still import and skip; here the process dies before `FhmoeTuner` runs. Changing FHMoE to `RuntimeError` would not remove the need to skip `--fhmoe` subprocesses in Tuning Tests, and it would be inconsistent with `--grouped-gemm`. The skip belongs in the tests (and in `op_tune.sh`), not by weakening `__main__`.

**How a candidate is timed.** Public `fused_moe()` cannot inject a one-row candidate. `supports_dsv4_i384_fhmoe` requires every padded-M tier in the config file (e.g. `fused_moe(M=16)` needs tuned rows for 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16). The worker therefore times `_fused_moe_impl` with a temporary one-row CSV (`kernelName1` / `kernelName2` / `block_m`). That is kernel-pair search, not the serving lookup.

**Published token is the serving lookup key.** Serving `get_2stage_cfgs` looks up `get_padded_M(token_num)`, not the raw catalogue token (`fused_moe.py`; for M < 32768 that is `nextPow2`, so 3072 → 4096). Candidate timing already wrote that padded key in `_write_candidate_csv`. `post_process` used to emit the catalogue token, so a non-power-of-two untuned row would be timed at the padded tier and published under a key serving never reads: the gap-fill job can exit 0, the CSV grows a dead row, and the shape stays uncovered. The producer now publishes `get_padded_M(X)` through `_lookup_token`, the same helper timing uses. Save the padded token only — not `X`, not both — because serving has a single `token` column.

The 12 shipped catalogue rows are already 1,2,4,…,2048; `pad(X) = X` for them and this does not change `tuned_fhmoe.csv`.

Local check on gfx950, two-pair smoke regex (not the cartesian), `--mp 1`, ~66s: catalogue token=3 → `/tmp/tuned_fhmoe_token3.csv` has `token=4`, `us=47.3686`, cosine OK (0 failed). `BaseTuner.tune_summary` still row-matches the `-i` frame (token=3) against success (token=4), so it prints leftover “untuned” and `[Tuning not Finished]` / exit 1. That is a key mismatch in the shared summary, not a failed kernel. We do **not** pad the catalogue on read and we do **not** rewrite `BaseTuner`’s message (every family uses it). Serving lookup is the contract this producer has to match; the 12-row gap-fill job never hits the mismatch.

**Search.** For each catalogue row, `_kernel_pairs` builds the legal FlyDSL cartesian (`block_m` ∈ {16,32,64,128} × stage1 names × stage2 names, after tile/LDS/`inter_dim` filters). DSV4 I384 INTERLEAVE is on the order of **5632 pairs per token**. Winner = min `us` among pairs with cosine vs torch ≤ `errRatio`. `post_process` drops the whole shape if every pair fails. Fast-wrong pairs must not win on latency.

**Data.** `generate_fhmoe_data` builds routed MXFP4 + shared FP8 tensors on the **host** (FMoE’s `generate_data` stays on CUDA). Dummy expert pad, `gate_mode` preshuffle. Weights are ~6 GiB per shape and **token-independent**. `run_config` regenerates per row sequentially and `empty_cache`s; this is not a 12×6 GiB peak. Left as-is; not a `test_run_config` bug.

**mp_tuner.** Same worker pool as FMoE. `shape_grouped=True` puts every pair of one shape in **one** task group. Default `--timeout` is 1800s **per group**. A full cartesian for one token is hours, so a real producer run needs `--timeout` on the order of a day (see Perf). Pipeline smoke is two pairs and stays under 1800s.

**`--run_config`.** Overrides the parent FMoE path. Iterates the tuned CSV, calls public `fused_moe` with shared-expert args, cosine vs torch, reports `e2e_us`. `--run_config <csv>` sets `AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE` to that file (same env serving uses) and clears FHMoE caches. Tuner `us` and `e2e_us` are different clocks (search vs production); do not compare them.

**`op_tests/test_fhmoe.py`.** `__main__` now runs `pytest.main`. `python3 op_tests/test_fhmoe.py` used to exit 0 without collecting tests. That file is the op oracle, not the tuner.

## op_tune.sh / Operators Tuning

Job, same gap-fill shape as FMoE:
```python3 csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py --fhmoe
-i aiter/configs/untuned_fhmoe.csv -o aiter/configs/tuned_fhmoe.csv
```

**No `--all`.** Without `--all`, `FmoeTuner.pre_process` drops keys already present in `-o` (“only kernels that are not in the tuned CSV”). The 12 catalogue rows **already match** shipped `tuned_fhmoe.csv`, so on gfx950 this job is a **no-op** until someone adds a new untuned shape. `--all` would retune those keys in CI and could overwrite production defaults. This PR is the producer, not a retune of shipped rows.

Operators Tuning’s runner is `linux-aiter-oci-mi300x-1` (**gfx942**). The script walks the **full** `tune_jobs` list, so `--fhmoe` would `SystemExit` and fail the workflow. The fhmoe job **skips** unless `get_gfx() == gfx950`. `get_gfx()` follows `GPU_ARCHS` (same helper as the rest of this script and aiter tests). Live `rocminfo` / `get_gfx_runtime()` is the other clock; we did not switch `op_tune.sh` to it.

## Tuning Tests (family tables, not a one-off yaml)

`tuning-tests.yaml` is unchanged: `test_csv_validation`, `test_tune_pipeline`, `test_run_config`. `GPU_ARCHS=gfx950`, runner `linux-aiter-mi35x-1`. Triggers are **schedule + `workflow_dispatch` only** — not `pull_request`. Opening this PR does not launch that workflow.

Grouped GEMM is **not** a Tuning Tests family (gfx1250; this workflow is gfx950). FHMoE **is** a family, with an explicit gfx950 skip so `--fhmoe` `SystemExit` is not a FAIL if `GPU_ARCHS` is wrong.

### `test_csv_validation.py`

- `TUNED_CSVS` includes `tuned_fhmoe.csv`.
- `test_fhmoe_no_duplicates` uses FHMoE extra keys (`act_type`, dtypes, `shared_expert_id`, pads, `gate_mode`, …), not GEMM `M,N,K`.
- Untuned catalogue file must exist.

### `test_tune_pipeline.py`

- Smoke only: `TUNE_MOE_KERNEL_REGEX` pins **two** kn1×kn2 pairs, not the cartesian (`timeout_mp1` 1200s). Measured ~72s on gfx950.
- **`test_fhmoe_mp1` only** — no `mp_default`. One GPU is enough to prove the tuner writes a CSV; all-GPU cartesian smoke is not the family pattern we need.
- Skip is an `if not _is_gfx950(): skipTest` inside `test_fhmoe_mp1`, not a `required_gfx` dict key. Pipeline methods are one-per-family; there is no loop over `TUNER_FAMILIES` that would miss a dict field. `_is_gfx950()` uses `get_gfx()` (honors `GPU_ARCHS`), same as CI.

### `test_run_config.py`

- Family `fhmoe`: `extra_args=["--fhmoe"]`, `config_property=AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE_FILE`, `required_gfx=gfx950`, `timeout=1800`.
- **Why `required_gfx` lives on the dict:** `TestRunConfig` loops every family, and `TestRunConfigCustom` (`TUNE_TEST_FAMILY=fhmoe`) must skip too. A skip only inside `test_fhmoe` would still blow up Custom on gfx942. Helper `_skip_unless_required_gfx` is called from both. Other families do not `SystemExit` in `__main__` on a Tuning Tests gfx950 box, so they do not need this key.
- **Why 1800s:** 600s died after token=512 cosine OK. 12 shipped rows finished in **690.9s**, all OK. Weights ~6 GiB/row sequential, plus a distinct FlyDSL pair JIT per token.
- `run_config` here is correctness + e2e of the **shipped** CSV, not a producer search.

### `test_fhmoe_replay.py` (in tree, **not** on the yaml)

Producer → serving in a **fresh** interpreter: tuner times `_fused_moe_impl`; this checks that public `fused_moe(...)` with shared-expert args reads only `AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE`. Empty DSV4 CSV must raise; a CSV `FhmoeTuner` actually wrote must be the kn1/kn2 that launch. A planted row is not the contract. M=16 needs the padded-M ladder in the file; the test tunes 1,2,4,8,16 and replays 1 and 16.

Other families do not put a sibling replay on `tuning-tests.yaml`. Listing it there was considered and dropped so FHMoE matches fmoe/a8w8 CI surface. Run it locally if you want the serving lookup proof.


## What this PR does not do (on purpose)

- Does not change serving `fused_moe` / `fhmoe.py`.
- Does not commit a new `tuned_fhmoe.csv`. A producer that beats **one** shipped token is evidence, not a default swap.
- Does not pass `--all` on Operators Tuning (would overwrite shipped keys).
- Does not run the FlyDSL cartesian in CI (token=1 alone is 5632 pairs; default 1800s watchdog would kill the grouped task).
- Does not add replay / extra tests to `tuning-tests.yaml`.
- Does not switch `op_tune.sh` from `get_gfx()` to `rocminfo`.
- Does not unify pipeline’s `_is_gfx950()` with run_config’s `required_gfx` helper. Different dispatch (named method vs family loop + Custom). Both honor `get_gfx()` / `GPU_ARCHS`.
- Does not pad catalogue tokens on read, and does not change `BaseTuner.tune_summary`. A non-power-of-two `-i` row still trips `[Tuning not Finished]` after a successful padded write (token=3 check above). The shipped 1…2048 catalogue does not.

## Perf evidence (token=1 only — not a CSV update)

Quiet gfx950, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` on an idle GPU (device 4; device 1 was 98% and unused). `TUNE_MOE_KERNEL_REGEX` **unset**. `--timeout 86400` because 5632 pairs are one `mp_tuner` group. Tune ~1.5 h, then `--run_config` shipped vs tuner CSV, **same** public `fused_moe`, warmup=2, iters=5.

Producer wrote `/tmp/tuned_from_producer.csv` (1 row, `us>0`, 0 failed). Cosine OK on both clocks.

| | CSV | kn1 | kn2 | e2e_us | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | shipped `tuned_fhmoe.csv` token=1 | `…_t32x64x256_w4_gui_kw4_fp8` | `…_t32x256x128_atomic` | 39.58 | OK |
| After | tuner-written CSV | same kn1 | `…_t32x128x128_atomic_persist` | 37.83 | OK |

Same kn1, **different kn2**: real cartesian, not the two-pair smoke regex. After is not slower (~4%). One token, 2/5 iters; not a reason to replace the 12-row shipped file in this PR. Tuner `us=38.86` on after is a different clock (101 iters in `run_perftest`); compare e2e to e2e only.

## Files

- `csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py` — `FhmoeTuner`, `--fhmoe`, cosine, `run_config`, `_lookup_token` (publish `get_padded_M`)
- `aiter/configs/untuned_fhmoe.csv` — DSV4 I384 catalogue
- `.github/scripts/op_tune.sh` — fhmoe job + gfx950 skip
- `op_tests/tuning_tests/test_{csv_validation,tune_pipeline,run_config}.py` + README
- `op_tests/tuning_tests/test_fhmoe_replay.py` — local producer replay
- `op_tests/test_fhmoe.py` — pytest `__main__`

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_csv_validation -v`
- [x] `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_tune_pipeline.TestTunePipeline.test_fhmoe_mp1 -v` (gfx950, ~72s, 2 pairs)
- [x] `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_run_config.TestRunConfig.test_fhmoe -v` (gfx950, 12 shipped rows, 690.9s, all OK)
- [x] Producer token=1 cartesian (`candidates=5632`) + `--run_config` shipped vs tuner CSV (table above)
- [x] Catalogue token=3 → tuned CSV `token=4` (`pad` publish), two-pair smoke, gfx950, 66s, `us=47.3686`. Summary leftover 3 vs 4 / exit 1 is the unpadded `-i` key, not a cosine fail.
- [ ] `tuning-tests.yaml` GitHub workflow: not a PR check. Equivalent fhmoe tests already ran on gfx950. Full-suite dispatch (`test_tune_pipeline` / `test_run_config` for every family) is optional and not required to land the producer.

title: [ASM] [CI] Remove committed scratch files and stop two from coming back
body:
Six tracked files that nothing reads and nothing will read again.

CI scratch committed by the bot. update-split-tests.yaml writes split-tests-update-summary.md and then pr-body.md into the workspace and hands them to peter-evans/create-pull-request, which has no add-paths filter and so commits every dirty file it finds. Both landed in the repo root that way in #5131. The workflow regenerates them on every run, so the tracked copies are stale by definition; .gitignore now keeps the bot from re-adding them.

Merge and POC leftovers that ship in the wheel.
hsa/gfx950/pa/pa_bf16_noquant_gqa8_1tg_4w.co.orig and .co.poc_kl_merg arrived with #3211 next to the real .co. Nothing references either by name, and the ASM loaders build .co paths explicitly rather than globbing the directory, so neither is reachable. They are not merely inert: setup.py copies all of hsa/ into aiter_meta and MANIFEST.in grafts it, so 48 KB of scratch binaries go out in every wheel. *.orig is now ignored so the next conflicted merge does not leave another one behind.

One-off files their PRs forgot. probe_noqa_check.py is a single line, x = 1, added in #4403 to confirm the pinned ruff config flagged it. REPO_CLEANUP_PLAN.md is a pull request description from #2167 in March. Its Phase 1 shipped -- the .pt test data is gone from main and the size rules are in .gitignore -- and its Phase 2 history rewrite needs a coordinated force push that has not happened in the six months since. Neither file is referenced anywhere in the tree.

title: [CI] Add stale pull request and stale branch cleanup
body:
actions/stale, daily: a pull request is labelled stale after 15 days without activity; a push or comment clears it. Nothing is closed — days-before-pr-close is -1, since leaving it unset would mean the action's 7-day default. Drafts and PRs labelled keep-open, blocked, do-not-close or dependencies are exempt. Issues are out of scope. The action is pinned to the v10.4.0 commit.

Branch cleanup is proposed separately, with archival before deletion, in satya/stale_branch_archive

title: [CI] Satya/stale branch archive
body:
Weekly, off until STALE_BRANCHES_ARCHIVE is 'true'; until then every run reports and writes nothing.

A branch with no commits for 30 days is copied to archive/<date>/<name> and its ref removed. 30 days later a deletion notice is posted; 14 days after that the archive ref is deleted. 74 days end to end, restorable at any stage with git push origin archive/<date>/<name>:<name>, which both bot comments print.

No stored state: the archive date is in the ref name, the notice date is the bot's comment. Deleting that comment opts a branch out. Only refs this workflow created are managed — its own archiving comment is the provenance — and markers name their ref, so two branches on one commit can't share a clock.

Deletion is a leased git push, the only server-side compare-and-swap available; protection and open-PR head/base membership are re-checked immediately before it. Exemptions are the checked-in .github/stale-branch-exemptions.txt, consulted at every stage against the original name, so a line added later rescues an archived branch without restoring it. The policy runs from the default branch only; --max-actions caps a run at 50 so the ~700 branches already past 30 days drain over weeks.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [gfx942] Enable sparse_mla_fwd on gfx942
body:
Enables `sparse_mla_fwd` on gfx942.

Re-land of #5539, which was auto-closed on Sep 18 when its base branch
(`cagri/sparse_pa_optimizations`) was deleted three seconds after #4919 merged.
Nothing was rejected there — the one review comment is addressed and folded into
this commit. Now targets `main` directly; the commit cherry-picks onto it with no
conflicts and no file in it has changed on `main` since #4919 landed.

The Gluon kernel needs no change to run there — the `gl.amd.cdna4` intrinsics it
uses (`async_copy`, `mfma`, `buffer_load`/`buffer_store`) all lower fine on
gfx942 under Triton 3.7.1. The arch gate was the only thing in the way, plus two
launch-config values sized against gfx950's LDS budget.

### Why the tile has to change

gfx942 (CDNA3) has **64 KB of LDS per workgroup against gfx950's 160 KB**. The
bf16 KV tile alone is `BLOCK_K * (kv_lora_rank + LDS_PAD) * 2 B`, so the gfx950
tile of 64 asks for 68 608 B and will not launch:

```
OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory, Required: 68608, Hardware limit: 65536
```

`BLOCK_K=32` is the largest that fits.

**`num_warps` is decoupled from `BLOCK_K` in the same change.** It was derived as
`BLOCK_K // 16`, so capping the tile for LDS would have dropped num_warps from 4
to 2 as a *side effect* rather than as a tuning decision. Keeping it at 4 is
worth **1.19× → 1.55×** on the prefill shapes, so it is worth making explicit.

### `dot_precision="fp8"` is rejected on gfx942

This one is a genuine hardware limit and was the only real surprise. The fp8 dot
path feeds the cache's own code points to the matrix core, which needs **OCP
e4m3 MFMA — that arrives with CDNA4**. CDNA3 has fp8 MFMA in the fnuz encoding
only, so OCP code points read back wrong.

It was **silently wrong (rel-err 7.5e-1) rather than faulting**, which is why
this raises now, naming the alternative. `dot_precision="bf16"` dequantizes the
tile on its way into LDS and works on every arch and every cache format —
including the fp8 caches, which is what production uses here.

Two consequences of that, both in this commit:

- The bench's fp8-dot series is built from `FP8_DOT_ARCHS`. With the arch gate
  widened it would otherwise reach that series on gfx942 and raise on its first
  point; `triton.testing.perf_report` does not catch it, so the run died before
  printing a table. It now prints a note so the omission is visible rather than
  silent. (This was frida-andersson's catch on #5539.)
- The test's cache builders go back to an explicit OCP e4m3 rather than the
  arch-native fp8 dtype. These records are OCP by definition of the format, and
  the kernel's dequant reads OCP code points; on gfx942 the native dtype is
  `float8_e4m3fnuz`, so building with it decoded to garbage (rel-err 1.0) on
  every fp8-cache case. `_classify_flat` already rejects fnuz when a uint8 view
  is not hiding the dtype.

### gfx950 is unchanged

`_arch_block_k` → 64, `_arch_num_warps` → 4, `lds_limited` False, and
`FP8_DOT_ARCHS` contains gfx950, so every value and branch resolves exactly as
before. I do not have gfx950 hardware, so that claim is by construction rather
than by test — worth a second pair of eyes.

### Validation

On MI325X (gfx942), TP4, GLM-5.3-Flash at 131 k context. This matters on that
model because its NoPE MLA has `qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, which has no AITER path
today, so vLLM falls back to a vendored Triton gather+dot — the single largest
kernel in the model in both phases.

`op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_sparse_mla.py`:

```
32 passed, 12 skipped in 23.61s
SKIPPED [12] fp8 matrix-core dots need OCP e4m3, absent on gfx942
```

Kernel bucket, from a real torch profile at concurrency 12 (rank 0):

| phase   | bucket   | Triton (vLLM) | this kernel | speedup   |
| ------- | -------- | ------------- | ----------- | --------- |
| decode  | per step | 3.099 ms      | 0.400 ms    | **7.74×** |
| prefill | per call | 10 988 µs     | 10 330 µs   | 1.06×     |

End-to-end, 131 k in / 1024 out, same image both arms with only the dispatch
switched:

| conc | out tok/s before → after | delta       |
| ---- | ------------------------ | ----------- |
| 2    | 80.92 → 91.36            | **+12.90%** |
| 4    | 110.96 → 121.09          | +9.13%      |
| 8    | 129.61 → 137.74          | +6.27%      |
| 12   | 141.29 → 147.94          | +4.71%      |
| 16   | 143.24 → 149.89          | +4.64%      |

**Won 7/7 rows, mean +7.14% output throughput, zero failed requests.** gsm8k
(5-shot, full 1319 questions) is neutral: 0.9719 vs 0.9712 strict-match, against
a ±0.0046 standard error.

The gain being largest at low concurrency is the signature of this kernel rather
than noise: the operator is batch-independent, so replacing it takes a roughly
constant ~2.7 ms off every decode step, which is 16.6% of TPOT at concurrency 2
but 4.9% by concurrency 16.

### Note on prefill

The 1.06× prefill figure is the honest one, measured in a profile. A
microbenchmark using `randperm` top-k indices reports 1.55× for the same shape,
but that flatters it — random indices give the Triton gather far worse locality
than production does (11.0 ms real vs 15.7 ms synthetic for the same shape),
while this kernel gathers whole 512 B rows and is locality-insensitive.
**Prefill microbenchmarks on this operator should not be trusted without a
profile.**

title: [Config] [Tune] Add GLM-5.3-Flash a8w8 blockscale fused-MoE configs for gfx942
body:
## What

Adds two files under `aiter/configs/model_configs/`:

- `a8w8_blockscale_tuned_fmoe_glm5_3_flash.csv` — five tuned rows for the routed fused-MoE shape GLM-5.3-Flash dispatches on gfx942 / cu_num 304.
- `a8w8_blockscale_untuned_fmoe_glm5_3_flash.csv` — the tuner input, all fifteen token buckets rather than the five that were kept, so the search space behind the numbers below is reproducible.

Kernel-time attribution on a TP4 serving run put the routed MoE at 15.1% of prefill forward time against 2.1% for the a8w8_blockscale GEMMs, and the MoE was still running default kernels, so this is where the remaining headroom is.

## Shape

```
model_dim 4096, inter_dim 512, expert 288, topk 8, Silu,
bf16 activations, fp8 e4m3fnuz per_1x128 blockscale, g1u1, no doweight_stage1
```

`inter_dim` is 512 because `moe_intermediate_size` 2048 is sharded over TP4. Tuning aiter's power-of-two token ladder covers every token count, since the lookup rounds to these buckets.

## Environment

Both tuning runs used the same container and the same aiter working tree,
mounted at `/aiter`.

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 8× AMD Instinct MI325X, device `0x74a5` |
| Arch / CU | `gfx942`, `cu_num=304` — the table key |
| Driver | `amdgpu` 6.12.12 |
| ROCm (host) | 6.4.2-120 |
| Container | `amdsiloai/vllm:vllm-openai-rocm-glm5.3-flash-mi325-08092026` |
| ROCm (container) | 7.2.3, HIP 7.2.53211 |
| PyTorch | 2.12.0+git6bbd260 |
| vLLM | 0.28.1rc1.dev278+g73029d424 |
| aiter | this branch — `d2bb0945e` at the main tuning run, `76cd9af0e` at the small-batch run, `024bae1` as submitted |
| Parallelism | `--mp 8`, all eight GPUs, node verified idle before each run |

`gfx942` alone is ambiguous — MI300X shares it — so the identifying key is
`cu_num=304` together with the part above.

The aiter tree was bind-mounted rather than installed, so the commits above are
the state of the branch at each run rather than a guarantee the working tree was
clean. The tuner, its inputs and its outputs are all in this branch.

## Commands

All three are `csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py`, run inside the
container above with the aiter tree at `/aiter`:

```bash
docker run --rm --device /dev/dri --device /dev/kfd --group-add video \
  --shm-size 32G --ipc host \
  -v <aiter>:/aiter -w /aiter -e PYTHONPATH=/aiter \
  -v <logdir>/compare:/tmp/aiter_compare \
  -e TUNE_ONLY=asm,cktile \
  --entrypoint bash \
  amdsiloai/vllm:vllm-openai-rocm-glm5.3-flash-mi325-08092026 -c "<cmd>"
```

**1. Tuning, all fifteen buckets** — produced the kept rows:

```bash
python3 csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/untuned_fmoe_glm53flash.csv \
  -o aiter/configs/tuned_fmoe_glm53flash_gfx942.csv \
  --mp 8 --timeout 180 --compare --update_improved
```

`--compare` benchmarks the production operator before and after tuning;
`--update_improved` then writes only shapes that improved by at least
`--min_improvement_pct` (default 3%). That gate is what rejected tokens
64/128/256/512.

**2. Verification** — re-runs the production operator against the tuned CSV:

```bash
AITER_CONFIG_FMOE=/aiter/aiter/configs/tuned_fmoe_glm53flash_gfx942.csv \
python3 csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/untuned_fmoe_glm53flash.csv \
  --run_config aiter/configs/tuned_fmoe_glm53flash_gfx942.csv --mp 8
```

**3. Tokens 1–32, default vs tuned** — the measurement that rejected them. Two
arms of `--run_config` differing only in whether a CSV is supplied, over a
six-row input (tokens 1–32):

```bash
# arm A - default kernels, no CSV
python3 csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py \
  -i untuned_small.csv --run_config --mp 8

# arm B - tuned kernels
python3 csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py \
  -i untuned_small.csv --run_config tuned_small.csv --mp 8
```

Run twice; the two runs agree within 1%.

## Results

End-to-end operator time from `--compare`, tuned against the default kernel:

| token | default (µs) | tuned (µs) | speedup |
|------:|-------------:|-----------:|--------:|
|  1024 |       542.18 |     524.53 |   1.03x |
|  2048 |      1002.53 |     670.24 |   1.50x |
|  4096 |      1864.42 |     868.68 |   2.15x |
|  8192 |      2812.08 |    1524.90 |   1.84x |
| 16384 |      4336.83 |    2764.15 |   1.57x |

Time-weighted speedup across the five is **1.66x** (10.56 ms -> 6.35 ms summed), median per-shape 1.57x. The gain concentrates at large token counts, so it matters most for prefill and large batched decode.

All five rows select `block_m` 64 and a 64x256 stage-1 kernel: `fmoe_bf16_blockscaleFp8_g1u1_vs_ps_silu_64x256` at tokens 1024, 4096, 8192 and 16384, and `fmoe_bf16_blockscaleFp8_g1u1_vs_silu_64x256` at token 2048. Stage 2 is unused; every row runs single-stage.

## Why only five of fifteen buckets

The other ten are deliberately absent, because the default kernel is equal or faster there and falling back is the better choice.

**Tokens 64, 128, 256, 512** were rejected by the `--update_improved` gate on two separate tuning runs, at -0.57%/-0.20%, -9.75%/-5.26%, +1.23%/-0.07% and -0.80%/+0.33%.

**Tokens 1 through 32** were rejected after a dedicated measurement. The tuner had marked them `no_baseline` and admitted them on the post-run alone, because the pre-run benchmark returned no timing for them. Benchmarking the default path directly (`--run_config` with no CSV) against the tuned kernels shows the tuned candidates are slower at five of the six:

| token | default (µs) | tuned (µs) | speedup |
|------:|-------------:|-----------:|--------:|
|     1 |        38.70 |      58.02 |   0.67x |
|     2 |        51.55 |      61.83 |   0.83x |
|     4 |        73.88 |      74.33 |   0.99x |
|     8 |       113.85 |     111.26 |   1.02x |
|    16 |       173.23 |     179.94 |   0.96x |
|    32 |       255.15 |     295.34 |   0.87x |

Reproduced over two runs agreeing within 1%. Only token 8 improves at all, by 2.3%, under the 3% threshold. Shipping these would have regressed the small-batch decode path by up to 1.5x.

## Verification

Keys are disjoint from the 35 `tuned_fmoe` tables **in this repo**, so
`get_config_file()` merges this file upstream with no duplicate-shape conflict.
Verified by loading `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE_FILE` with this file in `model_configs/`
and confirming all five rows survive the merge. The untuned file is excluded by
that glob, which skips any name containing `untuned`.

**That guarantee does not extend past this repo, and it is worth stating.** The
glob at `jit/core.py:439-444` accepts any `*tuned_fmoe*.csv` in
`model_configs/`, so a downstream image shipping its own table for this shape
is merged alongside this one. Our ROCm/vLLM nightly does exactly that
(`tuned_fmoe_glm53flash_gfx942.csv`), and the two agree on all 14 shape keys at
all five tokens.

The dedup that would normally protect against this does **not** fire, because
`_tag` is part of the dedup key: a file without the column is filled with `0`
while this one carries `""`, the keys therefore differ, and both rows survive
for the same shape with nothing deciding which the lookup returns. Confirmed by
running the merge over the two tables — 10 rows, 5 shapes, 0 duplicates
detected. It is not a "faster row wins" tie-break; there is no tie-break.

So the rule for this shape is **one table, not two**: whoever adds the second
must retire the first. Flagging it here because the next person to hit it will
have no way to tell from a server log.

title: [FlyDSL] Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm
body:
## Motivation

Current Aiter all-reduce + RMSNorm kernels are not optimal for PCIe interconnects. For tensors of shape [m, 7168], we get on average the following speedup

| Regime | world size 2 | world size 4 | world size 8 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Decode | 1.47× (M ≤ 12) | 1.45× (M ≤ 4)  | 1.35× (M ≤ 4) |
| Prefill (M ≥ 1024), FlyDSL uses quantization | 2.38× | 15.1×  | 31.0×  |

## Technical Details

This PR extends the plain `all-reduce` kernel from #5461 with an RMSNorm eplogue. There is per family (1-stage, 2-stage-mesh, and 2-stage-ring) heuristics to select the best instance per family, as well as a policy to select the best FlyDSL family for the message sizes where they are better than then current Aiter kernels. The policy is integrated to the Aiter's communication dispatcher such that when the FlyDSL kernels are enabled via `AITER_FLY_AR=1`, they are tried first. If they are applicable, they'll be used, otherwise the current Aiter fused all-reduce kernel are used.

## Summary
- Split the layout-v2 GEMM2 body out of `mxmoe_gemm_v2.py` into `aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/mxmoe_g2/` (`atoms` / `kloop` / `epilog` / `scheduler` / `dispatcher`) and point fused_moe, AOT, the tuner, and tests at `aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.mxmoe_g2`. Native `flydsl_mxmoe_g2_a4w4_*` is unchanged.
- Add `epilog=scatter`: GEMM2 writes unweighted `flat_out[sorted_row, hidden]`, then `aiter.mxfp4_moe_scatter_reduce` applies weights. fused_moe sets `output_aux` for that path; the kernel-name parser accepts `atomic|reduce|scatter` (`scatter` is non-atomic). Isolated tuner GEMM2-out raises for scatter (needs `reverse_sorted`).
- Scatter always uses persist-flat tile scheduling (`_flat_persistent_tile`). JIT tags are exclusive: persist-flat `_pflat_cu{N}`, persist-M `_persist_cu{N}`, one-shot empty — never `_persist` + `_pflat` together.
- Point GLM-5 FP4 `token=16384/32768`, `inter_dim=512` at `flydsl_moe2_layout_*_scatter_sbm128` instead of native `flydsl_mxmoe_g2_a4w4_*_f4out`.

title: [HIP] [Perf] Size the MLA metadata LDS scratch to the chunk, not the batch count
body:
## What this fixes

`kn_get_mla_metadata_v1_2_parallel` sizes five prefix arrays by `num_batches`, so its LDS scratch is `4 * (3 + 5 * num_batches)` bytes and the parallel planner is only reachable below 8192 batches on gfx950. Above that the dispatch falls through to the serial planner, which is a single wavefront walking every batch, and it costs 5.6 ms per launch at 16384 batches.

That ceiling is invisible for decode, where `num_batches` is the concurrency and never gets near it. It is not invisible for prefill: a DSA prefill chunk carries one batch per query token, so `num_batches` tracks `--max-num-batched-tokens` and every full 16384-token chunk takes the serial path. Across six GLM-5.2 traces the serial fallback was **83.8% of all `get_mla_metadata` time while being 4% of the calls**, and 95.7% of that sat at `tok >= 12288`. In one c40 prefill step the planner ran 21 times for 119.5 ms of a 1335.5 ms step.

## What changed

**Chunk the scan instead of sizing it by the batch count.** Phase 1 and phase 2 now alternate over chunks of at most `MLA_V12_PARALLEL_BATCH_CHUNK` batches, carrying the scan's five scalars (`curr_cu`, `remain_payload`, `num_works`, `last_reduce_indptr`, `partial_idx`) across chunk boundaries. Stopping at a batch boundary and resuming is exactly what phase 1 already does between batches, so the per-batch prefixes are identical to the unchunked ones. Three barriers bracket each pass: after phase 1 writes the chunk's prefixes, after phase 2 consumes them, and after every thread has taken its private copy of the carry — the last one is what keeps the next chunk's phase 1 from overwriting `p_lds_carry` while a straggler is still reading it.

**Take the totals from the carry rather than a pre-pass.** Phase 2a needs `total_works` before any chunk is filled, which a chunked phase 1 only knows after its last chunk. The obvious fix is a totals-only scan up front, and it costs what you would expect: one lane walking every batch, 245 us at 4096 batches and roughly 980 us at 16384. Instead phase 2a marks every CU with a sentinel, and the entries phase 2 never writes are patched to `total_works` after the loop, where the carry has it. That is an `O(num_cu)` pass over 256 entries. Removing the pre-pass took 4096 batches from 1.41x to 2.05x.

**Size the chunk to the card, not to gfx950.** A chunk fixed at 4096 needs 81,952 B of scratch. gfx950 has 163,840 and gfx942 has 65,536, so the constant quietly meant "gfx950 only" and would have left MI300 on the serial fallback at exactly the batch counts this change is about. The dispatch now asks for the largest chunk whose scratch fits once the qo/kv arrays are accounted for, and passes it in the kernel parameter; on gfx942 at 16384 batches that is 3275 rather than nothing.

**Keep the folded instantiation for the card that fits the full chunk.** Making the chunk a runtime value costs about 19% (2.13x down to 1.78x at 16384), so the kernel is templated on an optional static chunk and the dispatch picks the pinned instantiation whenever the full chunk fits — which is every case on gfx950, including short batch lists, since the choice is about LDS and not about how many batches arrived. Cards that cannot fit it get the runtime instantiation instead of the serial planner. Below `MLA_V12_PARALLEL_BATCH_CHUNK_MIN` the barriers cost more than the pass saves and the dispatch prefers serial.

The serial and xcd planners are untouched, and `MlaMetadataV1KernelParameter` gains one `int32_t` that only the parallel planner reads.

## Numbers

gfx950, `op_tests/test_metadata.py --ctx-len 2048 --nhead 32 --num-iters 21`, us per launch. "before" is whatever actually ran at that shape, which is the serial planner from 8192 up.

| batch | ran before | before | after | |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | parallel | 227 | 204 | 1.11x |
| 2048 | parallel | 421 | 380 | 1.11x |
| 4096 | parallel | 782 | 703 | 1.11x |
| 6144 | parallel | 1145 | 1028 | 1.11x |
| 8192 | **serial** | 2848 | **1351** | **2.11x** |
| 16384 | **serial** | 5650 | **2656** | **2.13x** |

The 11% below the old cliff comes with the pre-pass removal and is consistent across shapes; I have not chased down the mechanism.

2.13x is the ceiling of this design, and the measurements say so directly: per-batch cost is a flat 162 ns from 1024 to 16384 batches, which is the signature of a serial scan rather than of work spread over 512 threads. Phase 2 is now close to free and what remains is one lane walking every batch. Quartering the chunk (16 passes instead of 4 at 16384) costs 3.7%, so the chunking machinery is not where the time goes. Going further means parallelising the greedy bin-packing scan itself, which is a different change.

Applied to the c40 prefill step above, 21 launches drop from 119.5 ms to about 55.8 ms, and the planner's share of that trace goes from 6.50% to about 3.1%. That last figure is arithmetic on trace counts, not an end-to-end measurement.

## Test changes

Three commits here, and the first one is a bug in the harness that is worth taking on its own merits.

**`reduce_final_map` was compared at the wrong indices.** `test_metadata.py` reported `match: False` for every shape at batch >= 512 with `--jitter`, and `reduce_final_map` was the only field that differed. No kernel was involved. Both planners write row `i` only when tile `i` is split, at that tile's own index, so the written rows are scattered over the buffer rather than packed into a prefix. `compare_metadata` sliced the first `num_groups` rows, which at batch=4096 meant 207 of 218 rows that neither planner ever wrote — 414 elements, against an observed 413 — and since `alloc_outputs` hands each run a fresh `torch.empty`, the comparison was between two allocations' leftovers. Uniform KV lengths hid it because nothing splits, so the slice is empty and the check is vacuous. A split tile is exactly one whose `reduce_indptr` step is positive, so `checkAllclose`'s `mask=` gets that predicate. I verified the diagnosis by filling the two sides with different sentinels: every written row agrees and all 15,948 disagreements sit in rows neither planner touched. **With this, `--jitter` passes on unpatched aiter too**, which it did not before.

**The default sweep could not reach the code this PR changes.** `DEFAULT_BATCHES` stopped at 128, so nothing below 8191 batches ever exercised the LDS cap. It now includes 4096, 8192 and 16384 — one chunk of scratch, the old cliff, and several chunks. All 27 rows pass on unpatched aiter as well, and there the speedup column states the problem plainly: 1.97 at 4096, then 1.00 at 8192 and 16384. The whole default sweep takes 5 s.

**Brought the test in line with `.claude/skills/aiter-op-test`:** candidates in a dict with per-candidate `us`/`GB/s`/`err` columns, the card in the row, an allow-list arch gate in `main()`, a markdown summary through `aiter.logger`, and `checkAllclose` in place of hand-rolled element counts. Planner output is indices, so the comparison is `rtol=atol=tol_err_ratio=0`. There is no TFLOPS column because the planner does no floating-point and it would be a column of zeros; GB/s is the number that says something, and what it says is the diagnosis — 0.14 GB/s serial and 0.30 parallel on a card that does TB/s.

## Validation

`validate-kernel-pr` against this base, on an idle gfx950, with an independent shape grid (4095, 4097, 8191, 12288 — none of them in the target's defaults) and `--ctx-len` as a second axis: **PASS, 0 findings**. `merge_sim`, `gpu_claim`, `test_policy`, `baseline_control`, `correctness_repo_tests`, `correctness_s1_grid` and `execution_receipt` all pass; `index_width_scan` found 0 candidates. `test_policy` records tolerances of 0.0 and 0 commented-out shape rows added, so the suite got tighter rather than looser. The grid channel and the axis were each proven by rejecting a deliberately invalid value, and the execution receipt records all four shapes running on both sides.

Shapes covered by hand beyond that: batch 4 through 16384 including the 4095/4096/4097 and 8191/8192 boundaries, `--ctx-len` 1024/2048/4096/8192, `--nhead` 16/32/128, with and without `--jitter`.

## Not covered

Only gfx950 hardware. The adaptive chunk is what lets gfx942 take the parallel path at all, but I have no MI300 to run it on — the runtime-chunk instantiation was exercised on gfx950 by building with the ceiling raised past what this card can hold, where it is correct and runs at 1.80-1.85x. `kLdsBatchInfo=true` at large batch counts, `kIsSparse` and `kQoSplits` go through the same dispatch but were not separately swept. No end-to-end serving run or accuracy regression yet; a wrong work partition does not crash, it degrades quietly, so that is worth doing before anyone leans on this in production.

title: Add adaptive-blocked K5 prefill h-recurrence in GDN
body:
## Motivation

The gated-delta-rule (GDN) prefill K5 hidden-state recurrence currently ships as a serial,
single-launch emit. A blocked parallel-scan implementation existed in the tree but was
reachable only from bench harnesses. A same-harness, cache-defeated A/B showed the blocked
path beats serial at every measured shape once its partitioning is made count-driven rather
than a fixed block size.

This PR adds the blocked path as a single unified FlyDSL K5 path, wired into
dispatch behind a regime gate, with the existing serial emit as the fallback.
There is no public API change: `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h_flydsl_opt` 
keeps its signature and return contract, so any shape the gate rejects behaves exactly as before.

## Technical Details

The K5 recurrence carries a `[V, K]` hidden state across chunks. The blocked path partitions
each sequence's chunks into segments and runs three FlyDSL launches — **build-map**
(per-block local products), **carry** (fp32 carry checkpoints at block boundaries), and
**emit** (re-seed from the block carry and emit outputs).

Partitioning is count-driven per sequence, not a fixed block size:

block_chunks = max(1, ceil(ceil(seq_len / 64) / target_segments))

`target_segments = 8` by default, overridable via `AITER_GDN_K5_TARGET_SEGMENTS`.
This fills the emit grid at small T and self-limits to the saturating block size at large T,
so one default covers the shape range.

**Regime gate.** The blocked path is taken only when all of the following hold; any miss falls
through to the unchanged serial emit:

- `B == 1`; gate `g` present, no `gk`
- `K == V == 128`, chunk size `BT == 64`
- `num_decodes == 0`, `num_decode_tokens == 0`; no state-pool indices
- ≥ 128 total chunks; bf16 inputs; gfx950
- SSM State cache is either fp32 or bf16

**Numerics.** The blocked path is a reassociated affine scan (fp32 carry checkpoints at block
boundaries), so it is ~1 BF16 ULP off the uninterrupted serial recurrence by construction. Its distance to the fp32
reference is of the same order as serial's.

## Test Plan

`op_tests/test_flydsl_linear_attention_prefill.py`: correctness is checked against the fp32 torch reference recurrence
`ref_chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` at `rtol = atol = 2e-2`, applied independently to the h
snapshots, `v_new`, and the final state (the bar the serial path already holds to) — not
bit-exactness against the serial kernel, which the reassociated scan is not expected to match.

Two rows exercise both sides of the gate, plus the existing Qwen3.5-35B sweep:

- **`ragged_coupling_refill` [8257]** — 130 chunks, one-token final chunk, chunk-local
  cumulative gates for genuine inter-block coupling; asserts the gate reaches the blocked path
  (2 blocked dispatches).
- **`empty_sequence` [8192, 0]** — gate rejects; asserts serial fallthrough (0 blocked
  dispatches) and empty-sequence final state equals the initial state.

## Test Result

- `ragged_coupling_refill [8257]`: 2 blocked dispatches, `err = 0`.
- `empty_sequence [8192, 0]`: 0 blocked dispatches (serial fallthrough), `err = 0`.
- Full 16-row FlyDSL sweep: all rows `err = 0`, no traceback or assertion failure.
- Performance (gfx950, cache-defeated, vs serial emit):

| Shape | Stock (serial) µs | Adaptive µs | Difference | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| N=1 / 8k | 262.4 | 160.1 | −39.0% | 1.64× |
| N=1 / 16k | 487.0 | 256.2 | −47.4% | 1.90× |
| N=1 / 32k | 957.5 | 467.1 | −51.2% | 2.05× |
| N=2 / 8k | 297.1 | 251.8 | −15.2% | 1.18× |
| N=2 / 16k | 599.6 | 446.0 | −25.6% | 1.34× |
| N=2 / 32k | 1137.5 | 815.1 | −28.3% | 1.40× |

title: [FlyDSL] QRInt4: INT4 two-shot all-reduce for gfx942/gfx950
body:
## Summary
- Add `QRInt4`: FlyDSL INT4 two-shot all-reduce (reduce-scatter, then all-gather) for gfx942/gfx950, TP 2/4/8.
- Rank tile is 1152 B: 1024 B INT4 + 128 B group-16 E4M3. Fanout is 18×64 B NT stores (8+8+2). Super-tile is 1 or 8.
- Host: HIP IPC inbox, ST pick, bf16 payload. Tests gate SQNR ≥ 18 dB vs fp32 NCCL on every rank.

This is a Python launcher (`from aiter.ops.flydsl import QuickAllReduceInt4`). It is not wired into the HIP QuickReduce dispatch tables.

## Why this is faster than HIP QR INT4
HIP QR INT4 (`CodecQ4`) is one tile per handshake. This kernel packs ST=8 tiles under one last-sector handshake, and uses lockstep 64 B NT fanout.

Group-16 E4M3 also beats HIP CodecQ4 numerics: SQNR ~19.2 dB vs fp32 all-reduce (HIP INT4 is ~18.3 dB / rel MAE ~0.123).

title: [HIP] [CI] [JIT] [ROCm][MoE] Add fused MoE routing preamble for MXFP4 decode
body:
## Motivation

At decode shapes the MXFP4 MoE routing preamble is four short kernels back to back, and the gaps between them cost more than the work inside them. Each kernel is only 5-7us, and every boundary is a full round trip through HBM plus a launch.

This fuses the whole sequence into one kernel (or two kernels above ~104 tokens). End to end this brings up to 9% gain at low concurrency, where the preamble is a meaningful share of each decode step.

The target model is [upstage/Solar-Open2-250B](https://huggingface.co/upstage/Solar-Open2-250B), and the current constraints follow directly from it: gfx950, bf16 in, hidden size 4096, num_experts <= 512, single expert group, biased grouped top-k. Nothing in the design is specific to those values - other hidden sizes, expert counts, topk values, and plain softmax expert selection can be added on top of the same kernel. They are left out here to keep the first version simpler.

<details>
<summary>Performance measurement: M sweep, E=320, topk=8, unit_size=16</summary>

| M | fused (us) | stock (us) | uplift |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9.19 | 18.28 | 1.99x |
| 32 | 11.60 | 22.42 | 1.93x |
| 64 | 12.83 | 22.65 | 1.76x |
| 103 | 14.63 | 22.96 | 1.57x |
| 104 | 13.59 | 23.07 | 1.70x |
| 128 | 14.08 | 23.31 | 1.66x |

torch.profiler `device_time_sum`, i.e. summed GPU kernel busy time. 

Reproduce with the third command in the test plan below. That table was collected with more iterations than the committed harness uses (it hardcodes `num_iters=10, num_warmup=2`).

</details>

Corresponding PR to vLLM: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56420

## Technical Details

At M=64, E=320, topk=8 the profiler shows:

```
--- STOCK (M=64) ---
  6.72us  aiter::grouped_topk_kernel<hip_bfloat16, float4, 1, true, true, false>
  4.96us  aiter::opus_moe_sorting_entry<MoeSortingMultiPhaseKernel_P0_v2<...>>
  4.60us  aiter::opus_moe_sorting_entry<MoeSortingMultiPhaseKernel_P23<...>>
  5.96us  aiter::fused_mx_quant_moe_sort_kernel<bf16, opus::fp4_t, 256, 16>

--- FUSED (M=64) ---
 13.60us  aiter::fmr::fused_moe_routing_kernel<256, 16, bf16, 0, bf16>
```

So `biased_grouped_topk` -> `moe_sorting` (two phases) -> `fused_dynamic_mxfp4_quant_moe_sort` becomes one launch. Note `moe_sorting` is a single Python call but dispatches two kernels. Optional `moe_buf` zero-fill is folded into the same kernel instead of being a separate memset.

The fused kernel uses a self-resetting grid barrier in place of the kernel boundaries. Above ~104 tokens the grid no longer fits co-resident, so the barrier is replaced by a second launch; both paths share the same device code and differ only in where the barrier sits. Selection is deterministic and the sort is stable, so output is bit-identical to the stock chain for tie-free gating.

The kernel writes the full sorted map, including the region past `num_valid`: the downstream stage-1 GEMM reads an id per block before it consults `num_valid_ids`, so that tail is live memory under a caching allocator.

This is inert on its own - a matching vLLM PR is needed to call it, and will be opened shortly. Callers must check `fused_moe_router_supported()` first and own the workspace via `get_fused_moe_router_workspace()`, since a captured CUDA graph bakes the pointer in and the buffer has to outlive the capture. Expert parallelism is supported through an optional `expert_mask`.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Correctness
python -m pytest op_tests/test_fused_moe_router.py -q

# Stress (multi-GPU, graph capture, concurrent streams)
python op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_fused_moe_router_stress.py

# Benchmark + correctness sweep
python op_tests/test_fused_moe_router.py -m 1,32,64,103,104,128 -ek 320,8 -u 16
```

The stress suite covers what unit tests do not reach: barrier churn across grid shapes, fused/split interleaving, scratch staleness, allocator poisoning, determinism soak, CUDA graph capture and replay, graph/eager interleaving, concurrent streams, CU pressure from a competing GEMM, and multi-device use in one process.

## Test Result

All green on gfx950.

```
327 passed in 77.19s
PASSED: 0 failure(s) over 1 round(s), 12 suite(s)
All fused_moe_router tests passed!   (RC=0, all error columns zero)
```

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Attention] Add overflow-guarded per-call int32 varlen strides
body:
## Summary

AITER's Triton variable-length attention currently selects 32- vs 64-bit stride arithmetic through process-global state. This PR adds a **per-call** opt-in so a caller can request 32-bit addressing when the complete launch is safe, without changing other concurrent attention calls.

`prefer_int32_strides=True` uses the int32 specialization only when the checked tensor layout and launch geometry fit safely in int32. Otherwise the existing int64 path is used or, for unsupported metadata/implementations, the opt-in is rejected explicitly.

Defaults are unchanged.

## Safety boundary

The opt-in is currently limited to BF16 inference, matching the qualified use case. FP16/FP32 keep the existing int64 dispatch, as does training.

The guard covers:

- Q/K/V, output and LSE storage offsets and strides
- production tile sizes
- padded and one-past tile coordinates
- sequence-coordinate and sliding-window arithmetic
- flattened launch-grid bounds
- 1D contiguous cumulative-length metadata

Unsupported implementations such as Gluon/DAO do not silently ignore the request.

## Validation

The current test suite runs the new branch in the normal Triton attention pytest path. On MI300X/gfx942, **307 tests pass** across the bounds/configuration suite and GPU dispatch/parity cases. The GPU cases cover output and LSE, graph replay, causal/windowed attention, GQA, strided views, head padding and independent FP32 references. FP16/FP32 fallback is also checked.

For the long MiniMax H3 attention shape that motivated this work, the isolated primitive improved from **134.90 ms to 84.80 ms (1.59x)**.

With the companion SGLang adapter (#39249), a matched 8x MI300X MiniMax H3 run with Cache-DiT off improved full generation time from **208.17 s to 142.12 s**, or **46.48% more serial clips/hour**. The three measured decoded audio/video outputs were identical between the two arms.

Short attention shapes can regress, so this PR does not enable the option by default or claim a universal speedup.

## Review question

The main maintainer question is whether the per-call API and its safety/fallback boundary are the right abstraction for Triton varlen attention. The implementation does not change the attention algorithm or remove overflow protection.

title: [Triton/Gluon] fix: avoid Python 3.10 source inspection failures in MXFP4 JIT imports
body:
## Motivation

While integrating AITER into RTP-LLM, `import aiter` failed during MXFP4 kernel JIT initialization:

```text
ValueError: No function definition found for kernel
```

The import chain eagerly loads MXFP4 Gluon/Triton kernels, including gfx1250 kernels even on MI308. On the affected Python 3.10 environment, inline lambda expressions in heuristic decorators can cause `inspect.getsource()` to return a truncated source block without the subsequent function definition. Triton/Gluon JIT initialization then fails while locating the function definition.

## Technical Details

- Replace inline lambda heuristics with named predicates and `functools.partial` in the gfx1250 Gluon and Triton MXFP4 kernel modules.
- Cover all five affected decorated kernels, including the reduction/activation path whose alignment condition uses `BLOCK_SIZE_N1 * NUM_ITER`.
- Preserve the heuristic conditions, kernel signatures, and GPU kernel bodies.
- Do not patch Python's `inspect` module, alter Triton, suppress import errors, or change architecture dispatch.
- Add an import/source-inspection regression test covering all five kernels and 1,620 alignment predicate checks, including aligned/unaligned dimensions, distinct block sizes, and `NUM_ITER=1/3`.

## Test Plan

Run the import-compatibility regression test from the AITER repository root, using Python 3.10 with Triton/Gluon installed and without any source-inspection monkey patch:

```bash
env -u PYTHONPATH python3 -m unittest op_tests.test_mxfp4_jit_import -v

```

`Mxfp4JitImportTest.test_decorated_kernels_and_heuristics` verifies:

- Both affected kernel modules import successfully, exercising Triton/Gluon JIT initialization.
- `inspect.getsource()` includes the function definition for each of the five decorated kernels.
- All heuristic predicates match the original alignment conditions for aligned and unaligned dimensions and distinct block sizes.
- The middle kernel, `_fused_reduce_act_mul_and_dynamic_mxfp4_quant_kernel`, retains its `BLOCK_SIZE_N1 * NUM_ITER` alignment condition with `NUM_ITER=1` and `3`.

This is an import and host-side heuristic regression test; it does not require a gfx1250 GPU or launch GPU kernels.

## Test Result

- Source import and the regression test passed on Python **3.10.9** and **3.10.12** with Triton **3.8.0** in the ROCm development container.
- One unittest passed, explicitly covering all five decorated kernels and all 1,620 predicate comparisons; no GPU kernel launches are needed by this test.
- AST comparison against the base commit confirmed that all **11 existing function bodies** across the two kernel modules are unchanged.
- No gfx1250 hardware execution, cross-Python-3.11/3.12 validation, or kernel-performance benchmark is claimed. Existing unrelated `ResourceWarning` messages from AITER initialization were observed.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: [CI] Cache Triton wheelhouse across test jobs
body:
## Summary
- Compute a stable Triton wheel cache key from the Docker image, artifact name, and Triton wheel workflow/scripts.
- Restore the Triton wheelhouse cache in `prepare_triton_wheel` first, downloading and saving only on cache miss.
- Ensure `zstd` is available before Triton cache restore on GPU runners so cache versions match the `ubuntu-latest` prepare job archive format.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [FlyDSL] [CI] feat(flydsl): Add paged-attention Tile kernel
body:
## Motivation

Add a FlyDSL paged-attention decode implementation to AITER for FP8 KV caches.

The kernel provides explicit control over MFMA execution, KV-page loading, LDS
layout, softmax, partition scheduling, and native FlyDSL partition reduction.

## Technical Details

- Add FlyDSL paged-attention decode under `aiter.ops.flydsl`.
- Support:
  - FP8 K/V caches
  - BF16/FP16 queries
  - Block sizes 16, 64, and 128
  - Per-tensor and per-token KV scales
  - GQA and multi-token prediction
  - Plain and transposed V-cache layouts
- Process context in 256-token tiles using four wave64 waves per CTA.
- Use wide K=128 FP8 MFMA for the tuned MTP3/MTP4 gfx950 path.
- Split small MTP2/MTP4 grids into one query per CTA; keep larger grids and
  MTP3 fused to share KV/scales.
- Select the single-M per-token V-prefetch pipeline from one layout/workgroup
  policy; static Hkv2 uses the tuned path while high-grid page128 transposed V
  retains the lower-register schedule.
- Support explicit partition counts up to 256 and a caller-configurable clamp for
  automatic partition selection.
- Use the native FlyDSL reducer for partition outputs.

## Test Plan

`op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py` has one generic parametrized pytest function
with 14 real-kernel/reference configurations covering QL1/2/3/4, page16/64/128,
plain/transposed V, BF16/FP16, scalar/per-token scales, automatic/explicit
partitions, Hkv2 prefetch policy boundaries, C200k, and a BS200 smoke case. The
same file also covers dynamic planning, graph replay, high-partition reducers,
and provides a direct correctness + performance CLI for larger sweeps.

```bash
pytest -q op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py \
  -d bf16 -b 200 -q 4 -s 16,1,128,200000 \
  --block-size 16 128 --trans-v 0 1 --per-token 1
```


Black, Ruff, Python syntax, Bash syntax, and `git diff --check` also pass.

## Performance

### Earlier representative cases

MI355/gfx950 CUDA Graph end-to-end latency, including compute and reduce:

| Case | Block size | PA Tile | PA Gluon | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| small | 16 | 11.79 us | 12.24 us | 1.04x |

| batch | 16 | 14.20 us | 20.43 us | 1.44x |

per-tensor; `batch` is B81/Hq8/Q1/C1027 per-tensor; `MTP3` is

measured 3.4866/4.4269/5.1639/4.4958 TB/s. Explicit NP5 is faster than auto

title: [Config] configs: GLM-5.3 fused shared MoE rows for gfx950
body:
## Why

GLM-5.3 shared-expert fusion changes the routed fused-MoE dispatch from `E=288, topk=8` to `E=289, topk=9`. The ninth expert is always selected with weight 1.0, so one AITER launch performs the routed and shared gate/up GEMM, `SiLU(gate) * up`, down GEMM, and routed-weight accumulation.

The two TP-local signatures are:

- TP4: model/intermediate `(4096,512)`, `E=289`, `topk=9`
- TP8: model/intermediate `(4096,256)`, `E=289`, `topk=9`

The existing model-config set does not cover either signature. Without exact rows, both use fallback kernels.

## What this adds

Sixteen gfx950/cu256 rows are added in a dedicated GLM-5.3 fused-shared table:

- TP4: `M={4,8,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384}`
- TP8: `M={8,32,128,256,512,2048,4096,8192,16384}`

The matching untuned table records the complete 15-shape power-of-two ladder for both TP4 and TP8 (30 source rows).

Both signatures were tuned with the standard fused-MoE tuner over the compatible one-stage ASM block-FP8 family. Only rows improving AITER's production operator by at least 3% were retained. The remaining buckets are intentionally absent and keep fallback dispatch.

## Validation

- All 16 retained rows have `err1=0.0%`, `run_1stage=1`, `kernelName2` empty, and `us2=0`.
- Production-operator execution passed for every retained row: 7 TP4 and 9 TP8, all status `OK`.
- TP4 retained rows improve production-operator latency by 10.98-48.12%.
- TP8 retained rows improve production-operator latency by 4.61-45.11%.
- Direct fused-versus-separate tensor comparison passed at TP4 and TP8 from M=1 through M=16384: all outputs finite, minimum cosine 0.999822, maximum mean absolute error 7.45e-6.
- `test_csv_validation.py` and `test_config_shape_collision.py`: 32 passed, 37 subtests passed.
- Every new dispatch key occurs exactly once across the complete current-main fused-MoE config set.
