title: [Config] Tune a8w8 bpreshuffle for Kimi-K3's KDA gate at tp4
body:
## What

Adds the 62 missing `N=3072, K=128` rows to `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv`, plus the matching shapes in the untuned CSV.

## Why

Kimi-K3's KDA gate projection `f_b_proj` is `[M, 128] x [128, 128 * heads/tp]`. K is the KDA head dim, 128 at any tp; N is `num_local_heads * 128`, so the 96 KDA heads give **N=1536 at tp8** and **N=3072 at tp4**. Only 1536 was tuned, so tp4 misses the table on every token.

A miss here is not a slower kernel. `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` falls through to `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_ck`, whose `rowwise_heuristic_dispatch` has branches only for `K >= 512` and `K >= 192 && K % 64 == 0`. K=128 hits:

```
TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported K for heuristic dispatch: 128. Supported K greater than 192 and K % 64 == 0.")
```

so the process raises on its first token. Tuning confirms there is no CK kernel for this shape at all: every `ck` candidate reported `This GEMM is not supported!`, and every winner is cktile or flydsl.

## How

Same M grid the `N=1536` rows carry (64-step between 1024 and 4096), so padded-M lookups behave the same at both widths.

```
python3 csrc/ck_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle/gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_untuned_gemm_kimik3.csv \
  -o aiter/configs/model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv \
  --mp 8 --errRatio 0.01
```

62 shapes, zero failures. 5 pick cktile at small M, 57 flydsl above -- the same split `N=1536` has.

The rows are inserted in the file's existing `(N, M, K)` order rather than letting the tuner re-sort the whole file, so the diff is 62 additions and no deletions.

## Verification

gfx950 / 256 CU, via `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` directly:

| shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tp8 `M=1..16384 N=1536 K=128` | OK | OK |
| tp4 `M=1..16384 N=3072 K=128` | **FAIL** `Unsupported K for heuristic dispatch: 128` | **OK** |

End-to-end: Kimi-K3 at `--pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 4` on MI355X x8 now serves with no framework-side GEMM override, GSM8K 5-shot over the full 1319 questions at **0.9598 flexible-extract / 0.9606 strict-match**, inside the range `recipes/Kimi-K3.md` records for this model (0.9591-0.9659 / 0.9591-0.9666).

title: [CK] [FlyDSL] [FEAT] support fp8/fp4 quant in mega stage2 combine
body:
## Motivation 1. Tune MEGA stage2 for prefill shapes. 2. Support fp8/fp4 quant on the MEGA stage2 combine wire. ## Technical Details **Combine wire quant.** New `combine_quant` on `MegaMoEStage2Config` (`none`/`mxfp8`/`mxfp4`, env `MEGA_COMBINE_QUANT`), chosen independently of `dispatch_wire`. The gemm2 EP-scatter epilogue quantizes in registers to per-1x32 e8m0 before the P2P write, and `ep_combine_fused` dequantizes in the reduce, so the fabric carries 1/2 (fp8) or 1/4 (fp4) of the bf16 payload. A slot is a payload plane followed by a scale plane — split, not interleaved, which drops the 384B chunk pad that was 33% of the wire. The reduce's lane tile is retuned per wire (bf16 `T=16/C=1`, quantized `T=8/C=4`), since the scale plane makes a small `C` pull a whole cache line per row. **Stage2 tuning.** `ep_fused` joins the tuning shape identity, since gemm2 also runs the EP scatter and that moves the tile optimum off the plain-GEMM one; an `ep_fused` row wins over an otherwise equal generic row. `moe_contiguous_psum_remap` also goes grid-strided over 256 blocks; one block left the non-EP row remap latency-bound. ## Test Plan DSV4 Pro, gfx1250 x 4, 61 MoE layers in a single CUDA graph. ## Test Result ### UT accuracy — PASS `--layers 4 -tpr 512 --acc_verify 1`, auto tolerance 0.120107: | combine_quant | avg logits_diff | result | |---|---:|---| | none | 0.079799 | PASS | | mxfp8 | 0.081049 | PASS | | mxfp4 | 0.102634 | PASS | ### tokens/rank = 16,384 (prefill shape) Per-layer self device time (us), averaged over 4 ranks. | operator | no-tuning
combine bf16 | tuned
combine bf16 | tuned
combine mxfp4 | tuning | mxfp4 quant | total | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `mori_ep_dispatch` | 198.9 | 201.4 | 199.6 | +2.5 | −1.8 | +0.7 | | `gemm1` (K7168) | 1,149.5 | 1,191.4 | 1,195.8 | +42.0 | +4.3 | +46.3 | | `gemm2` (K3072 + EP scatter) | 1,244.7 | 1,088.4 | 989.8 | −156.3 | −98.6 | −254.9 | | `ep_combine_fused_0` | 99.5 | 100.3 | 49.7 | +0.8 | −50.6 | −49.8 | | `ep_combine_fused_sync_0` | 46.4 | 49.2 | 40.6 | +2.8 | −8.5 | −5.7 | | `moe_fused_quant_preshuffle` | 150.4 | 162.9 | 154.0 | +12.5 | −8.9 | +3.6 | | **per_layer (wall)** | **3,323.1** | **3,234.0** | **3,077.6** | **−89.1** | **−156.4** | **−245.5** | | **relative** | — | −2.7% | −7.4% | **−2.7%** | **−4.8%** | **−7.4%** | 1. **tuning vs no-tuning: −2.7%.** The `ep_fused` row moves gemm2 from `t256x256x256_cn4` to `t128x256x256`, worth −156.3 us. gemm1 gives back 42.0 and preshuffle 12.5, netting −89.1. 2. **combine fp4 vs no-quant: −4.8%.** `ep_combine_fused_0` halves (−50.6) and gemm2 drops another 98.6, because with `_epq4` its epilogue writes fp4 + an e8m0 plane instead of bf16. Those two are 95% of the −156.4. ### tokens/rank = 512 (decode shape) | operator | no-tuning
combine bf16 | tuned
combine bf16 | tuned
combine mxfp4 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `mori_ep_dispatch` | 35.5 | 36.3 | 37.7 | | `gemm1` (K7168) | 160.3 | 160.1 | 160.3 | | `gemm2` (K3072 + EP scatter) | 111.1 | 111.1 | 110.1 | | `ep_combine_fused_0` | 6.0 | 6.0 | 4.3 | | `ep_combine_fused_sync_0` | 10.6 | 10.2 | 12.0 | | `moe_fused_quant_preshuffle` | 12.4 | 12.4 | 12.4 | | **per_layer (wall)** | **409.7** | **410.9** | **409.9** | Flat within 0.3% on both axes, as expected: - The new tuned rows are keyed on the prefill shape, so this shape keeps the same `t64x512x128` tile in all three legs — tuning is a no-op here by construction. - `ep_combine_fused_0` does drop 1.7 us, but `ep_combine_fused_sync_0` gives back 1.8 us. At this size the pipeline is latency-bound rather than wire-bound, so narrowing the wire buys nothing. Both features default to off (`combine_quant="none"`, and the `ep_fused` rows only match the EP-fused path), so nothing changes unless they are requested. ## Submission Checklist - [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: Fp8 mqa logits gfx950 dsa tune
body:
> **Status: do not submit.** Re-measured on current upstream `main` (`4927f8f5c`, 2026-09-23), the tile change makes the DSA indexer **5.8% slower**. Upstream already fixed the same problem in #5216 and #5603, and fixed it better. This file records the measurement so nobody reopens this.

## What this PR was going to do

On gfx950, give the DSA indexer shape of `fp8_mqa_logits` (32 heads × head size 128) its own tile: 128-wide KV tiles, `waves_per_eu=2`, `num_warps=2`. It also moved the `BLOCK_M=2` threshold from `seq_len > 4096` down to `>= 1024`.

The reason: sglang splits each prefill's indexer call into chunks of roughly 1–2k rows, to keep the fp32 logits under 2 GiB. The old `seq_len > 4096` threshold almost never fired, so every chunk ran `BLOCK_M=1` and re-read the whole cached context once per row.

## Why it no longer applies

Upstream changed this code twice after our base (merge-base 2026-08-29):

- **#5216** (09-09): general optimization of the gfx950 kernel.
- **#5603** (09-16): adds split-k. `BLOCK_M=2` is now also chosen when there are enough workgroups (`cdiv(seq_len, 2) * num_kv_splits >= 1024`), no longer only when `seq_len > 4096`. That is the same gate problem we fixed.

gfx950 also always takes the buffer path now, so the LLVM crash that our `use_buffer_store` guard was avoiding cannot happen.

## Measurements

MI355X, one GPU, Triton 3.7. 39 `(rows × context)` chunk shapes taken from a GLM-5.2 AgentX replay, weighted by each shape's share of GEMM work. Script: `bench_upstream.py`, raw data: `bench_*.json`.

| aiter version | total time | vs upstream `main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| our base (09-21 snapshot) | 81.4 ms | 1.59x |
| our base + this PR | 65.6 ms | 1.32x |
| **upstream `main`** | **49.1 ms** | **1.00x** |
| upstream `main` + this PR's tile | 51.7 ms | 1.06x (slower) |

- On our old base this PR was worth −16.5%. That matches the earlier −23% measured with a different weighting.
- Upstream `main` alone is 25% faster than our patched version.
- Adding our tile on top of upstream makes 96% of the work slower. The worst shape is 1.22x, the best 0.93x. The output is bit-identical to upstream on all 39 shapes, so the tile only costs speed, not correctness.

Correctness was not re-run beyond the bit-exact check above: `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits.py` and GSM8k were skipped because the PR is not going out.

## What to do instead

Bump sglang's aiter to upstream `main`. On this benchmark that gives a 1.59x faster indexer GEMM, far more than this PR delivered. Upstream's output is not bit-identical to our old base because the kernel was rewritten, so the bump needs an accuracy check (GSM8k with GLM-5.2) and an AgentX TTT / Interactivity rerun.

Files in this directory:

- `PR.orig.md`: the previous draft of this file.
- `tile_on_upstream.diff`: this PR's tile ported onto upstream, as measured above.
- `aiter_base/`, `aiter_upstream/`, `aiter_old_base/`, `aiter_old_opt/`: the git worktrees that were benchmarked.

title: [Config] Revert 13 regressed Kimi-K3 A8W8 rows
body:
## Summary

- restore 13 Kimi-K3 A8W8 rows from #5690 to their previous CK/CKTile kernels
- keep the other 5 initially-questionable FlyDSL rows after higher-iteration ABBA repeats confirmed >=2% production speedup
- change config only; no kernel implementation is reverted

## Why

The first post-tune verification loaded CK/CKTile production modules built before the model config, so missing lookup entries fell back to heuristic kernels. After forcing `AITER_REBUILD=1`, the extreme reported gains disappeared (for example, `M=2176,N=576,K=7168` returned from ~213 us to ~24 us baseline latency).

## Verification method

- one fixed MI355X/gfx950 GPU (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`)
- rebuilt CK and CKTile production lookup from the main config
- baseline and candidate run sequentially on the same GPU
- initial run plus reverse-order repeat: 10/20 warmups, 101/201 timed iterations
- six unstable rows received two additional ABBA passes with 30 warmups and 301 timed iterations
- acceptance rule: `baseline_us / candidate_us >= 1.02`

## Result

- 12 rows consistently regressed
- `M=1216,N=576,K=7168` improved only 0.19%, below the 2% threshold
- 5 rows were retained after four-run ABBA medians confirmed 3.6%–18.1% speedup
- worst reverted rows:
  - `M=1472,N=1536,K=7168`: candidate `0.612x` baseline
  - `M=2112,N=576,K=7168`: candidate `0.875x` baseline

## Validation

- final config was rebuilt into the production CK/CKTile modules
- all 18 disputed shapes passed production numerical checks (`atol=0.01`, `rtol=0.01`)
- config contains 1039 unique positive-timing rows
- `git diff --check` passes

title: [ASM] [HIP] feat(fmha_fwd): add bf16 hd=256 forward ASM kernel for gfx950
body:
## Summary

- Add group-mode (varlen) BF16 forward attention ASM kernels for head dimension 256 on gfx950 (MI355X/MI350X)
- **Non-causal**: 14% faster than CK — 497 TFLOPS vs 436 TFLOPS (b=8, s=5121, 18 heads)
- **Causal**: 17% faster than CK — 509 TFLOPS vs 436 TFLOPS (same config)
- Supports variable-length sequences with physical/logical padding (ptr_qseq_padding/ptr_kseq_padding)
- Handles seqlen_q != seqlen_k per segment (cross-attention / ragged batches)
- Adds NRMS and mean diff reporting to test_mha_varlen.py for more meaningful accuracy metrics

## Supported contract

- **Layout**: group/varlen THD (mode=1), causal (mask=2) and non-causal (mask=0)
- **Precision**: BF16, hd_qk=256, hd_v=256
- **Workgroup**: 256 threads (4 waves), bdx=256
- **Heads**: MHA only (nhead_q == nhead_k); GQA/MQA falls back to CK
- **Input**: contiguous packed THD tensors (non-contiguous falls back to CK)
- **Not supported** (fall back to CK): GQA/MQA, dense BSHD, a32, dropout, alibi, bias, sink, logits_soft_cap, non-contiguous Q

### Gaps vs sibling ASM kernels

Callers relying on a sibling kernel's coverage will silently fall back to CK for these cases:

- **mode=0 (batch/dense)**: not supported. Every sibling (including fp8bf16 hd256) has it. Planned for a follow-up.
- **GQA/MQA**: rejected by gate (`nhead_q == nhead_k`). Caller falls back to CK — no wrong-answer risk.

## Accuracy note

BF16 hd256 uses BM=128 (Q-tile size), resulting in more online softmax rescaling steps than hd128/FP8 kernels (BM=256). At long sequences (s>1024), max element-wise diff can reach ~0.016 vs CK reference, but NRMS remains excellent (~4e-5). The stock test_mha_varlen.py tolerance (max(4x pytorch_noise, 0.01)) passes at all tested configs.

For causal with sq > sk (bottom-right alignment), Q rows that see no K columns output O=0 and LSE=-inf, matching the expected convention for fully-masked rows.

## Changes

- **hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fwd_hd256_bf16_group.co** — non-causal kernel binary (4 waves, bdx=256)
- **hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fwd_hd256_bf16_causal_group.co** — causal kernel binary with K-loop trim and NaN-safe epilogue
- **hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fmha_fwd.csv** — add bf16 hd256 entries for non-causal and causal
- **csrc/cpp_itfs/mha_fwd.cu** — bdx=256 for gfx950 bf16 hd256 group mode; tg_div=1 (no tile merging)
- **aiter/ops/mha.py** — enable bf16 hd256 varlen dispatch on gfx950, gated on nhead_q==nhead_k, q.is_contiguous(), no sink
- **op_tests/test_mha_varlen.py** — report NRMS and mean diff alongside max diff

title: [ASM] [HIP] feat(fmha_bwd): add bf16 hd=256 fused dKdV+dQ ASM kernels for gfx950
body:
## Summary

Add hand-written ASM backward attention kernels for **bf16 hd=256** on **gfx950 (MI355X)**:

- **Fused dKdV+dQ kernel**: Two-phase single-launch kernel. Phase 1 computes dK/dV (Q-walk with K/V resident in registers). Phase 2 computes dQ (K-walk with Q/dO resident). Writes dQ directly as bf16 — no atomic accumulation, no post-processing needed.
- **ODO preprocessing kernel**: Computes D = dO · O per token using coalesced loads and LDS tree reduction. Layout-agnostic (reads head stride from args).

## Supported contract

- **Layout**: group/varlen THD (mode=1), non-causal (mask=0)
- **Precision**: BF16, hd_qk=256, hd_v=256
- **Workgroup**: 512 threads (8 waves) for dQdKdV, 256 threads for ODO
- **Atomic**: a16 (atomic32=0) — no post-processing needed
- **Causal / a32 / dense BSHD**: not supported; fall through to CK

### Gaps vs sibling ASM kernels

Callers relying on a sibling kernel's coverage will silently fall back to CK for these cases:

- **mode=0 (batch/dense)**: not supported. Siblings have it.
- **mask=1/mask=2 (causal)**: not supported. The fp8bf16 hd256 backward already supports causal; this kernel does not yet.
- **atomic32=1 (a32)**: not supported. Only a16 mode.
- **fp16**: not supported. Only bf16.
- **GQA/MQA**: rejected by gate (`nhead_q == nhead_k`). Caller falls back to CK — no wrong-answer risk.

## Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/bwd_hd256_bf16_a16_pssk_group.co` | Fused dQdKdV kernel (512 threads, 8 waves) |
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/bwd_hd256_odo_bf16_group.co` | ODO preprocessing kernel (256 threads) |
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/fmha_bwd_dqdkdv.csv` | +1 entry: bf16, hd256, noncausal, group, pssk=1 |
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/fmha_bwd_odo.csv` | +1 entry: bf16, hd256, group mode |
| `csrc/cpp_itfs/mha_bwd.cu` | bdx=512 for hd>=256 |
| `aiter/ops/mha.py` | Enable gfx950 bwd dispatch for hd256: hdim gate, atomic32=0, causal guard |

## Performance

Tested on MI355X (gfx950) using `bwd.exe` with `AITER_ASM_DIR=<repo>/hsa`:

```
./bwd.exe -prec=bf16 -b=16 -h=18 -d=256 -s=2560 -mask=0 -v3_atomic_fp32=0 -mode=1 -kname=1 -v=0
```

Note: stock `generate_seqlens()` randomizes segment lengths in group mode (total tokens preserved). Numbers below are with randomized segments.

| Configuration | CK (baseline) | ASM (this PR) | Speedup |
|--------------|---------------|---------------|---------|
| b=8, h=18, d=256, s=2560, group | 12.1 ms (200 TFLOPS) | **3.65 ms (662 TFLOPS)** | **3.3x** |
| b=16, h=18, d=256, s=2560, group | 23.6 ms (205 TFLOPS) | **7.15 ms (676 TFLOPS)** | **3.3x** |

## Accuracy

PyTorch path (test_mha_varlen.py): dQ/dK/dV max diff ~0.004 at b=2 s=256. NRMSE ~2e-4 through PyTorch (Section 7 of independent repro confirms).

C++ bwd.exe reports higher NRMSE (~9e-2) for dQ/dK due to BF16 ODO D values in the C++ reference — this is a reference precision issue, not kernel accuracy. BF16 D is intentional (avoids extra F32 workspace).

## Test plan

Python (`test_mha_varlen.py`) on MI355X:

| Config | Result |
|--------|--------|
| b=2 h=8 s=256 (main benchmark) | dQ/dK/dV max diff 0.004, 58 TFLOPS bwd |
| b=2 h=8 s=256 (seq_padding: mixed, q_only, k_only, no_padding) | All pass (causal falls through to CK) |
| b=8 h=18 s=2560 | 597 TFLOPS bwd, correct |
| b=8 h=18 s=5121 (~41K tokens) | dQ/dK/dV max diff < 0.005, no ODO fault |

C++ (`bwd.exe`) on MI355X:

- [x] Simulator: 9/9 varlen tests pass (EqualSegments, UnequalSegments, ManySmallSegments, PaddedSegments, PaddedEqualSegments, DiffQKLengths)
- [x] GPU (MI355X): dQ/dK/dV max diff 0.004 at b=2 s=256
- [x] GPU (MI355X): bwd.exe 676 TFLOPS at b=16 s=2560, no ODO fault
- [x] Independent repro: PyTorch NRMSE ~2e-4, C++ ~632 TFLOPS at b=8 s=2560
- [x] C++ API (`bwd.exe`): b*h*s*d layout with sq != sk now passes (`valid:y`) — fixed dQ head stride in varlen SRD rebase

title: [HIP] [JIT] Remove unintended CK dependency from plain top-k
body:
## Summary

- replace CK numeric aliases in the plain top-k kernel with AITER's canonical
  Opus FP16/BF16 scalar and vector types
- define the raw-buffer cache-policy value locally instead of depending on
  `ck_tile::amd_buffer_coherence_enum`
- preserve the existing cache-policy encoding for legacy, CDNA3/4, and gfx12
  targets
- remove `module_topk_plain` from the CK-free exclusion list
- make the correctness test deterministic and configurable
- ensure correctness mismatches cause the test to fail

## Motivation

`module_topk_plain` is implemented as a native HIP/Opus module and does not
otherwise use Composable Kernel. However, its implementation referenced
`ck_tile` numeric aliases and a CK cache-policy enum through a transitive
include.

That accidental dependency prevented the module from building without the full
CK headers, requiring it to be excluded from CK-free builds.

The kernel only needs compiler-compatible FP16/BF16 types and the integer
cache-policy encoding passed to `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load`. AITER already
provides the appropriate scalar and vector types through Opus, so the CK
dependency is unnecessary.

## Behavior

No algorithmic behavior change is intended.

The local raw-buffer policy values match
`ck_tile::amd_buffer_coherence_enum::slc`:

- legacy targets, including gfx908: `2`
- gfx942 and gfx950: `19`
- gfx12: `25`

## Testing

Validated on AMD Instinct MI100 (`gfx908:sramecc+:xnack-`) atop the gfx908
target-enablement changes in #5720.

A clean rebuild of `module_topk_plain` succeeded.

The correctness matrix covered:

- FP16, BF16, and FP32
- largest and smallest selection
- batch sizes 1 and 32
- aligned and odd widths: 3072, 3073, and 32768
- top-k values 1, 8, 512, and 2048

Result: **78/78 cases passed with zero reported correctness error.**

title: [HIP] opt inverse rope group quant gfx1250
body:
## Motivation

Follows #4806. The payload now goes through the gfx1250 tensor engine, the
tier orders apply to row-major, and the op carries one stated policy for
non-finite input. Also fixes an out-of-bounds LDS write, a SIGABRT that
#4806's layout gate introduced, and a dispatch band that was removed by
mistake

## Technical Details

1. Tier sort extended to row-major narrow slices. The orders were restricted
to n32k4, but row-major admits the same sort and it is worth 13-18% once
the slice is narrow. The gain is the narrow quantize path -- a pass whose
groups all miss the rotary tail needs no widening, no cos/sin and no f32 --
which only a uniform segment per wave can select statically. Gated on
TDS == 16: below that a wave spans too few groups to amortize the sort.
2. Payload staged through the tensor engine. Every access order this kernel
uses is a regular 2D tile, tiering included, so the window is
dim0 = run*GROUP_SIZE by dim1 = slots/run and the tier only moves the
origin. Most of the effect is the staged wait: s_wait_tensorcnt<0>
serialises every tile behind the first consumer.
3. WAR stalls removed. s_wait_xcnt was 45% of all stall cycles in the s=16384
ATT trace -- three exec-mask writes landing on a store still in flight:
store_scale's saveexec around a one-byte store whose lanes already agree on
address and value, the cos/sin load's lane-term guard, and a wave-uniform
tdm_wave that divergence analysis could not see through.
4. Four-group heads tier at the exact cut. At GS=128 rope lives only in group
3, so cutting at GROUPS_PER_HEAD/2 filed the pure-nope group 2 under rope
and it paid f32 widening for a rotation it never performs. Held to four
groups per head; the same correction at eight costs 11.7%.

Each scale layout is built only where it can run. mfma_tile feeds CDNA's
V_MFMA_SCALE and n32k4 feeds RDNA's WMMA scaleB, so a third of the module
was kernels the target could never launch.
  gfx1250   372 -> 264 instantiations, 5.31 -> 3.88 MiB device code
  gfx950    372 -> 264 instantiations, 5.31 -> 3.27 MiB device code
  build     26.6 -> 22.3 s
The gate lives entirely in the translation unit; both macros keep an
#ifndef escape hatch for a target that genuinely needs both.


## Test Plan

384 checks pass on gfx1250, HIP graph capture/replay included. gfx942 is
added to SUPPORTED_GFX: its exclusion cited permlane16_swap, which the amax
reduction stopped using, and the op builds and runs there with mfma_tile
included.
Two gaps the sweep could not reach are now covered. Rows whose Ks leaves a
part-wave block, at 9 and 3 heads -- every default shape is a whole number
of waves. And the invalid-group policy, since none of the DATA_DISTS can
produce a non-finite input, which is why that behaviour had moved twice
under optimisation with nothing watching it.

## Test Result

gfx1250, h,g = 128,16, against main. Four interleaved rounds -- both builds
measured inside each round, since absolute timings drift between batches and
only a ratio taken within a round holds up. Median of the per-round ratios:
                          main      branch
  row   GS=128  s=2048   36.18 us   24.89 us   -31.2%
  row   GS=128  s=16384 295.59 us  211.08 us   -28.6%
  row   GS=32   s=2048   35.93 us   27.04 us   -24.7%
  row   GS=128  s=512     7.99 us    6.27 us   -21.3%
  row   GS=32   s=16384 293.00 us  237.78 us   -18.8%
  n32k4 GS=32   s=2048   33.12 us   29.86 us    -9.8%
  n32k4 GS=32   s=16384 261.91 us  238.36 us    -8.9%
The two remaining s=512 points, row/GS=32 and n32k4/GS=32, land around -5%
but spread several points round to round, so they are quoted that way rather
than to a figure.
A wider sweep -- 2 head configs x 3 layout/group-size combinations x 6
values of S -- is uniformly in the same direction with no regression, but it
was collected one build after the other and so carries that batch drift;
treat it as direction rather than magnitude.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: feat(tune): record untuned shapes for every GEMM family, not just bf16
body:
Fixes #5267.

## Why

`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1` makes `tuned_gemm.py` append every missed bf16 shape to `bf16_untuned_gemm.csv`. That single feature is why tuning a real bf16 deployment is self-service: run the server, collect the CSV, hand it straight back to the tuner.

The fp8 per-token, block-scale and mxfp4 families have no equivalent — they log misses at INFO and write nothing — so their shape lists have to be scraped out of server logs by hand. That is also how shape-key mistakes creep in: we shipped a tuned table that never matched anything because the engine fuses two projections and dispatches `N=2688`, while the tuned rows targeted the unfused `N=2624`. A recorded shape list makes that impossible to miss.

## What

`aiter/utility/untuned_shapes.py` — `record(tuned_file, row)` appends one de-duplicated row **in the schema that family's tuner consumes**. The destination name is derived from the tuned table's own name (`*_tuned_*` → `*_untuned_*`), so a family never has to name its untuned file twice, and a merged `/tmp/aiter_configs` copy still resolves to the right destination.

Wired into the miss paths of:
- `gemm_op_a8w8.get_CKGEMM_config` (block-scale, ± preshuffle) → `M,N,K`
- `gemm_op_a8w8.get_GEMM_config_with_quant_type` (a8w8, a8w8_bpreshuffle) → `M,N,K,q_dtype_w`
- `gemm_op_a4w4.get_GEMM_config` → `M,N,K`

## Behaviour

- Same switch as before (`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1`) — nothing new to learn; **off by default**.
- `AITER_TUNE_GEMM_DIR` overrides the destination, for read-only package directories and containers (we had to copy the file out of a container image more than once).
- Hot path cost after a shape has been seen is one set lookup; a serving run repeats its shapes, so the append happens a handful of times.
- Never raises. A read-only configs dir or a full disk must not take down inference — it logs a warning and moves on.

## Checked

Name derivation (including the merged-copy path), per-family schemas, de-duplication across repeats, disabled-by-default, and graceful degradation on an unwritable destination.

Same campaign as #5262 / #5263–#5266.

title: [JIT] Make CK fmha kernel generation follow GPU_ARCHS
body:
Make every `01_fmha/generate.py` call site pass `--targets` derived from `GPU_ARCHS`, instead of either omitting `--targets` (CK's silent default `gfx9,gfx950`) or passing a raw device name that CK's factory does not recognize.

## Why

`mha_recipes._ck_targets_flag()` passed the runtime device name (e.g. `gfx1100`) straight through as `--targets`. CK's fmha factory keys are coarser than device names (`gfx11` covers `gfx1100`-`gfx1103`), so any non-gfx9 host got an empty kernel set and `mha_fwd` failed at dispatch with "invalid argument for fmha_fwd". Every other `01_fmha/generate.py` site omitted `--targets` entirely, which defaults to CK's `gfx9,gfx950` regardless of what `GPU_ARCHS` actually asked for.

## What changed

- `map_gpu_archs_to_ck_fmha_targets` / `ck_fmha_targets` / `ck_fmha_factory_key` / `ck_fmha_batch_prefill_gen_targets` (`aiter/jit/utils/build_targets.py`): a small prefix table mirroring CK's `fmha_fwd.get_factory()`, more-specific prefixes first (`gfx950` before `gfx9`, `gfx115` before `gfx11`, `gfx125` before `gfx12`). Unmapped archs (`cpu`, `gfx1030`, ...) keep CK's default `gfx9,gfx950` so a GPU-less `PREBUILD` still emits FMHA modules instead of silently dropping them.
- Wired into every `01_fmha/generate.py` call site: JIT `cmdGenFunc_*`, `optCompilerConfig.json`, `mha_recipes.py`, and the standalone `op_tests/cpp/mha/compile.py`. `batch_prefill` uses a dedicated helper because CK drops *every* batch_prefill kernel if any `--targets` token is not `gfx9*`.
- fp8 has no CK factory on gfx11/gfx115; `mha_batch_prefill` is gfx9-only (its PREBUILD stub is API-only). Both are now rejected with a clear `NotImplementedError` instead of failing deep inside CK dispatch.
- The gate needs the *live* device (`get_gfx_runtime()`) at the public API and at `compile_ops`'s per-call module-name lookup, but the *build-time* `GPU_ARCHS` value (`get_gfx()`) inside `cmdGenFunc` for PREBUILD. Missing this distinction means `GPU_ARCHS=gfx942;gfx1100` (last token wins) would reject a real gfx942 card at runtime. `compile_ops` calls `gen_func` on *every* invocation for its module-name lookup, not only on cache miss, so the lookup path needed the same runtime-vs-build split as the public API, not just `cmdGenFunc` itself.

## Behavior change

`GPU_ARCHS="gfx942"` wheels no longer also contain gfx950 FA kernels (CK's default was always `gfx9,gfx950` regardless of `GPU_ARCHS`). Set `GPU_ARCHS` to every arch the wheel must run on. `docs/installation.rst` is updated accordingly.

## Verified

1. No-GPU unit tests for the mapping table and every gate (`op_tests/test_ck_fmha_targets.py`, `op_tests/test_ck_fmha_targets_wiring.py`): 43 passed.
2. gfx1201 (RDNA3.5): appended FA cases to `op_tests/test_mha.py` (hdim-80 pad-up fp16/bf16, fp8bf16 hdim64, fp8bf16 GQA) — 4 passed, GQA `max_diff=0.05878` against a `< 0.07` bound (per-tensor quant noise on the GQA broadcast, not a gfx12/GQA kernel defect).
3. `ruff check .` (CI-pinned `0.16.0`) and `black --check` clean on every changed file.
4. No CK change, no submodule bump.

gfx942/gfx950 regression is expected to be covered by CI on this PR; the gate logic itself only changes behavior on non-gfx9 archs and unmapped/no-GPU builds.

title: [HIP] Enable CK fmha LLC head grouping on RDNA (batch mode)
body:
Wire CK's LLC-aware head grouping into `fmha_fwd_ck`, batch mode only.

## Why

aiter launched every q head in one `fmha_fwd` call, so the whole KV working set (821 MB for a 28-head fp8bf16 shape) had to stream from memory every launch. CK's example runner already splits heads into LLC-resident groups — `fmha_fwd_args` even carries `num_head_q_total` / `head_start`, hard-coded to 0 on the aiter side.

## What changed

Reuse `fmha_fwd_head_grouping.hpp` from the pinned CK (`af9e1d1f`, no CK change, no submodule bump, no new kernel instance): `get_head_group_size()` owns the arch table, LLC probe, threshold, and launch cap; `run_fwd_head_grouped()` owns the per-group pointer math. aiter adds only the runtime-string → type-tag dispatch (`fp16` / `bf16` / `fp8bf16`), since `BiasDataType` and `ODataType` do not follow the input dtype.

- Batch mode only. The two group-mode callers of `aiter::mha_fwd` (`mha_varlen_fwd_kernels.cu`, `asm_mha_varlen_fwd.cu`) are out of scope.
- gfx9 is unaffected — `get_head_group_size` returns `nullopt` for non-RDNA archs.
- `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1` restores the old single-launch behavior.

## Verified

Grouped vs `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1` output is bitwise identical, run as a subprocess pair (CK caches `CK_TILE_FMHA_*` in a function-local static, so toggling the env var mid-process is a no-op). Grouping is **forced** via CK's own `CK_TILE_FMHA_LLC_CACHE_MB` override rather than relying on the host's real LLC size, so the comparison cannot go vacuous on a large-LLC part — confirmed on gfx1201 with CK's `CK_TILE_FMHA_HEAD_GROUP_LOG=1` showing 4 groups engage before asserting bitwise equality.

- gfx1201: 7 bitwise-identical cases passed (fp8bf16 ± causal, fp8bf16 GQA 8:2, fp8bf16 batch=2, bf16, fp16, bf16+LSE).

Perf on the shape that motivated this (`[1,114660,28,128]` fp8bf16, ~1.2 GB qkv): **2374 ms → 1392 ms** (1.7x), gated behind an opt-in env var, not asserted in CI.

## Compatibility

No CK change, no submodule bump, no new kernel instance. `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1` is an immediate rollback if a regression surfaces on hardware not covered above.

title: [CI] review-pr: fix agent-timeout envelope so large-diff reviews do not spuriously time out
body:
Follow-up to #5666. A real review (#5778, +1544/-339, 14 files) timed out: the GLM worker hit the 1000s agent timeout on every attempt, so no card.

**Two fixes:**
1. **1000s is too short for a large diff** (GLM generation has high thinking-chain variance) -> raise `AITER_AGENT_TIMEOUT` to **2400s (40min)**.
2. **`run_agent` retried a timeout**, which just burns another full window. Now a **timeout (exit 124) is not retried**; only a transient failure (dropped connection / 5xx) is, up to `AITER_REVIEW_RETRIES` attempts.

**Envelope:** timeout path = one 40min attempt per agent (worker + refuter = 80min worst), under the job cap, raised `90 -> 120min`. 40min is a reasoned start; override per-run via the env vars.

title: Fuse fp8 mqa logits clean
body:
## Summary

Fuse `clean_logits=True` output clearing into the existing gfx950 Gluon FP8 MQA logits kernel. Each workgroup fills its query rows' invalid windows with `-inf`, removing the separate full-output initialization. For the measured `clean_logits=True` prefill cases, latency is reduced by 5.42%–11.98% against the same launch configurations without fusion.

This PR is stacked on [PR #5621](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5621). The [incremental diff](https://github.com/qilihuan/aiter/compare/tune-fp8-mqa-logits-sweep...fuse-fp8-mqa-logits-clean) contains only the clearing fusion and its tests; the gfx950 dispatch buckets from PR #5621 are unchanged.

## Motivation

With `clean_logits=True`, the wrapper initializes the entire output to `-inf` before the compute kernel overwrites valid scores. Filling only the invalid windows inside the compute kernel removes that extra launch and the initial writes to valid positions.

## Changes

- Allocate an uninitialized output for all `clean_logits=True` calls on the gfx950 Gluon path, and pass a compile-time `FUSE_CLEAN_LOGITS` flag to the existing kernel. Fusion is not restricted to the shapes in the performance table.
- Fill the prefix and suffix outside each row's valid window in the same workgroup that computes its scores. Preserve the compute pipeline, grid, and launch settings; include the fusion flag in the kernel's trace representation.
- Keep `clean_logits=False` on the original compute path, with fusion disabled. Other architectures and the non-Gluon fallback retain their existing output initialization.
- Extend `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits.py` to check all invalid positions are `-inf` and all valid scores match the reference, including full, empty, unaligned, and different adjacent-row windows.

## Performance

These are **local measurements on Triton 3.7 / gfx950, not CI results**. Clocks were not locked. The measurement inputs and `aiter.test_common.run_perftest` follow ROCm/aiter PR [#5434](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5434), `op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py`. That script and the local comparison driver are not part of this PR; no sweep scripts or CSV files are submitted.

Fusion applies to all gfx950 Gluon calls with `clean_logits=True`; the table covers only the measured shapes below.

Fixed `M=4096, H=32, D=128`, with FP8 E4M3FN Q/KV, FP32 KV scales and weights, and row i's valid window `[0,N-M+i+1)`. Both public wrappers use the same inputs and the `(BM,BKV,W,C)` settings selected in PR #5621, where the tuple denotes `BLOCK_M/BLOCK_KV/waves_per_eu/NUM_CHAINS`. Launch parameters were compared directly; fusion is the only additional kernel option.

Each measurement uses 2 warmups and 101 calls, summing GPU profiler kernel durations per invocation and discarding the first iteration and IQR outliers. Results are medians from four independent processes, alternating baseline/fusion call order. Input generation, quantization, and reference computation are excluded. Both True timings include the work needed to provide `-inf` outside the valid windows; False excludes downstream masking.

| N | clean_logits | Shared (BM,BKV,W,C) | #5621 without fusion (μs) | This PR (μs) | Latency reduction | This PR TFLOPS | This PR TB/s |
| ---: | :---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4096 | True | (2,64,2,1) | 65.413 | 61.867 | 5.42% | 1111.033 | 1.373124 |
| 16384 | True | (2,64,2,1) | 328.498 | 294.142 | 10.46% | 1635.443 | 0.978776 |
| 65664 | True | (2,128,2,2) | 1439.938 | 1267.444 | 11.98% | 1684.189 | 0.870970 |
| 131072 | True | (2,128,2,2) | 2882.285 | 2551.011 | 11.49% | 1697.109 | 0.855381 |
| 4096 | False | (2,64,3,2) | 55.086 | 55.756 | -1.22% | 1232.802 | 0.921958 |
| 16384 | False | (2,64,2,2) | 303.271 | 302.156 | 0.37% | 1592.070 | 0.841796 |
| 65664 | False | (2,128,2,4) | 1220.794 | 1223.063 | -0.19% | 1745.303 | 0.873432 |
| 131072 | False | (2,128,2,4) | 2458.445 | 2459.531 | -0.04% | 1760.231 | 0.873557 |

False rows are controls with fusion disabled in both versions. The changes in those timings do not represent a fusion benefit. True and False use different configurations selected in PR #5621, so their timing difference alone does not isolate clearing cost. Performance outside these shapes and causal windows has not been characterized.

For valid pair count V and latency t in μs, TFLOPS is `2×H×D×V/(t×10^6)`. TB/s estimates Q/KV/scales/weights bytes plus output bytes, divided by `t×10^6`; output bytes are `4×M×N_padded` for True and `4×V` for False. This is an effective byte estimate, not a hardware bandwidth counter or measured peak-bandwidth utilization.

## Testing

- [x] Extended the existing unit test module with full-output checks for varied windows, the four measured KV lengths, an unaligned short shape, and an odd query-row count. Tests call the public wrapper without tuning overrides.
- [x] Ran the existing and added tests on gfx950. Valid scores are compared against an FP32 reference from the quantized inputs with TF32 disabled and `rtol=atol=0.01`; every invalid element is checked for `-inf`.
- [x] Performance comparison: see above (local gfx950 measurements).
- [ ] Tested on MI250X — not tested.
- [ ] Tested on MI300X — not tested.

From the patched repository root in the ROCm environment:

```bash
export AITER_TRITON_ONLY=1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
python -m pytest -q op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits.py
```

## Documentation

- [x] Clarified the returned logits' window semantics in the wrapper docstring.
- [ ] User guide updated — not needed; the public API is unchanged.
- [ ] Performance guide updated — measurement method and results are documented here.

## Dependencies

- [x] No new third-party dependencies added.

Depends on [PR #5621](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5621) for the selected dispatch configurations used in the comparison. Merge PR #5621 first, then rebase this branch so the upstream diff contains only the fusion commit. The #5434 test script is a measurement source, not a runtime dependency.

## Breaking Changes

None. Valid-score arithmetic and the public API are unchanged. With `clean_logits=True`, positions outside each row's window remain `-inf`; with False, those positions remain unspecified.

On gfx950 Gluon, True changes output allocation from `full(-inf)` to `empty`; the kernel fills the invalid regions with `-inf` to preserve these semantics.

title: [FlyDSL] gfx942 fp8_mqa_logits: let _auto_variant choose rows_per_block
body:
## Motivation

On gfx942 `_auto_variant` returns `f"mfma_r2_w{wpb}"`, so `rows_per_block` is pinned at 2 and
seven of the nine registered variants — including the entire `r4` family — can never be
selected. At the shape vLLM actually issues for long-context indexer prefill (`seq_len` 1024,
`seq_len_kv` 131072) the pinned pick is the median of the nine by speed, with the best 1.65x
faster. vLLM chunks prefill to fit `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` (512 MB), which caps
`seq_len` at 1024 at that context, so the selector's own `seq_len >= 2048` branch can never
fire there. Since vllm-project/vllm#49544 routes gfx942 `fp8_mqa_logits` to this kernel by
default, every MI300X/MI325X user inherits it.

## Technical Details

Sweeping all nine variants over 180 shapes surfaced two separable effects.

**RPB tracks the logits element count, not `seq_len`.** Over
`seq_len ∈ [1, 8192] × seq_len_kv ∈ [1024, 262144]` the boundaries land on the same value of
`seq_len * seq_len_kv` at all six contexts: `r1` below 2^19 (27/27 shapes), `r2` at 2^19 (6/6),
`r4` from 2^21 up (38/38), with 2^20 a transition band split 3/3.

**RPB must also divide `seq_len`.** When it does not, the launcher pads with four `torch.cat`
calls. That is a flat ~44 us of host-side overhead, independent of `seq_len_kv`: at `seq_len` 1,
`seq_len_kv` 131072, `r1` runs 23.1 us and `r2` 67.8 us, of which the four cats measure 44.1 us
(0.7 us unexplained), and pre-padding the input by hand recovers all of it. So the cost is not
proportional to the wasted rows — one padded row of two costs the same as three of four — and the
pinned `r2` walks into it on *every odd `seq_len`*, 37 of the 180 shapes swept, at a median 2.97x
penalty.

The step-down to a divisor has to be gated to small shapes, where the kernel is cheap relative to
44 us. Above the threshold the reuse wins even when padding: at `seq_len` 1025, `seq_len_kv`
131072, the dividing `r1` takes 3880 us against 2601 us for a padded `r2`.

```python
elems = seq_len * seq_len_kv
if elems < 2**19:
    rpb = 1
elif elems < 2**21:
    rpb = 2 if seq_len % 2 == 0 else 1
else:
    rpb = 4
wpb = 2 if (seq_len >= 2048 and seq_len_kv >= 8192) else 4
```

`waves_per_block` is deliberately left unchanged. It is worth a few percent at most here, and
unlike RPB its optimum moves with the head count — at 64 heads the current rule costs 1.61x worst
case where a fixed `w4` costs 1.07x — so it warrants its own sweep rather than a change fitted to
one head count.

## Test Plan

MI325X (gfx942), all nine variants timed at 180 shapes (1620 timings): a power-of-two
`seq_len × seq_len_kv` grid, plus three held-out sets the rule was not fitted on —
non-power-of-two shapes, a fine `seq_len` sweep through the divisibility cliff, and head counts
16 and 64. Selector changes were verified end to end through `flydsl_fp8_mqa_logits(variant=None)`
with no `FLYDSL_FP8_MQA_LOGITS_VARIANT` set, so the selector itself is under test. Every variant's
output was compared against a reference at every shape.

## Test Result

Old pick vs new, no env override:

| seq_len | seq_len_kv | before | us | after | us | speedup |
| ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | 131072 | r2_w4 | 2598.7 | r4_w4 | 1623.5 | 1.60x |
| 1025 | 131072 | r2_w4 | 2609.3 | r4_w4 | 1594.0 | 1.64x |
| 700 | 50000 | r2_w4 | 661.6 | r4_w4 | 440.3 | 1.50x |
| 333 | 12000 | r2_w4 | 118.4 | r4_w4 | 97.1 | 1.22x |
| 3 | 131072 | r2_w4 | 66.4 | r1_w4 | 28.1 | 2.36x |
| 1 | 1024 | r2_w4 | 66.2 | r1_w4 | 22.2 | 2.98x |

No shape measured regresses; the smallest gain is 1.04x. Scored against the fastest of the nine
at each shape, pooled over the held-out data, the geometric mean cost falls from 1.45x to 1.03x
and the worst case from 3.17x to 1.41x.

Logits are bitwise identical across all nine variants at all 180 shapes, so this is purely a
blocking/occupancy change with no numerical trade-off.

End to end on 8x MI325X, TP8, GLM-5.2-FP8, 131072 in / 1024 out, concurrency 8: median TPOT
improves 7.22% and output throughput 6.60%. This kernel is 16.8% of GPU time at that point, the
largest single item in the profile.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: [Triton/Gluon][GFX950] Productize gluon mha kernel from GFX950-gluon-tutorials
[FlyDSL] [Feature] Tiered persistent radix-select decode Top-K + arch/shape dispatcher
body:
# Tiered persistent radix-select decode Top-K + arch/shape dispatcher

**Tickets:** [SILOTIGER-699](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-699) (gfx950 decode Top-K) ·
[SILOTIGER-629](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-629) /
[SILOTIGER-683](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-683) (the kernel this builds on) —
epic [SILOTIGER-606](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-606) (GLM-5 MXFP4, MI355X perf uplift)

## What this is

1. **The FlyDSL decode Top-K kernel** — context-length-independent tiered persistent radix-select
   for the sparse-attention indexer, which calls it ~78×/step. The HIP path it replaces
   (`radix_topk_one_block<12,1024>`) is an O(N_blocks) radix sort: 369 µs @ 8K → 1,165 µs @ 120K,
   ~15× slower than B200's `persistent_topk_kernel`. This one is O(topK·log topK).
2. **A dispatcher inside `aiter.top_k_per_row_decode`**, routing there only where it is measured to
   win. Without it the kernel ships unreachable: the public op still calls HIP.

| | |
|---|---|
| Best cell vs HIP | **1.42×** gfx950, **2.19×** gfx942 |
| Worst in-window cell | **0.61×** (gfx942, k=512 rows=1 width=163840 seq=16384) |
| gfx942 shipped window | **+1371 µs** over 360 cells, median 0.976×, 169 won |
| Same grid, ungated | **−2998 µs** over 928 cells, median 0.861× |
| Correctness | set-equivalence with `torch.topk`, both arch sweeps |

Ungated, this kernel loses on that grid; the gate is what turns it into a win — a routing result as
much as a kernel result.

## Lineage

Sami's and Robin's commits ride along because that base is not in `main` yet. Base branch
[`RElbers/aiter@samremes/topk-per-row`](https://github.com/RElbers/aiter/tree/samremes/topk-per-row).

| who | what | commits |
|---|---|---|
| [@samremes](https://github.com/samremes) | the initial FlyDSL kernel ([SILOTIGER-683](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-683)): K=512 graph-capture-friendly tiered persistent radix-select, runtime `row_len` tiers, row-barrier optimization, long-row cap | [`48f0a93`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/48f0a930f) [`555569b`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/555569b41) [`72c7745`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/72c7745ff) [`5152d4d`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/5152d4db4) |
| [@RElbers](https://github.com/RElbers) | made it the **sole** decode path for **every** K (256/512/1024/2048) by lifting `top_k` to a compile-time parameter; workspace API, batch-aware tier config, deadlock guard, gfx950 params, non-pow2 K, `tier_mode` refactor, AOT entry | [`b3a0d97`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/b3a0d9775) [`c0b6909`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/c0b69091e) [`01741ab`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/01741abb4) [`755df3b`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/755df3bf2) [`c06b8db`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/c06b8db3b) [`135ebca`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/135ebca2c) [`c278797`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/c278797a2) [`f42bb80`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/f42bb802b) [`4abc985`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/4abc9855b) [`c6c30d8`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/c6c30d8c6) ← base |
| [@JH-Leon-KIM-AMD](https://github.com/JH-Leon-KIM-AMD) | gfx950 tuning (below), the dispatcher, the workspace cache, dispatch counters, the gfx942 window, the correctness harness, and the move onto aiter's `buffer_ops`/`vector` shims after [#4501](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4501) | below |

The generic tiering serialized wide decode batches into sequential co-resident waves. The switches
that fix it are **gfx950-only**, since gfx942 runs the frozen configuration: `short_max` +
`dead_block_trim` + midbatch cap
([`d2d2ad6`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d2d2ad6a4) [`5383b16`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/5383b166b) [`d783300`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d78330018)),
`blocks_per_row` floor 1 for the barrier-free short tier ([`2fc5ddc`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/2fc5ddcad)),
`row_proportional_parts` ([`a87146d`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/a87146da7)),
`batch_coresident_cap` ([`197eda0`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/197eda077)),
`early_stop` ([`d839939`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/d839939ce)), and a rows>63 / L≤65536
fold back to bpr=1 ([`e7dde59`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/e7dde5961)).

## The gate

Five checks, cheapest first, all on host values. Per-row lengths live in `seqLens` on the device,
and reading them would sync every decode step.

| | check | rejects to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `AITER_DISABLE_FLYDSL_TOPK_DECODE` | HIP |
| 2 | arch has a row in the gate table | HIP |
| 3 | `k in ks`, and `numRows` inside the row cap that `logits.shape[1]` earns | HIP |
| 4 | `stride1 == 1`, `stride0 == logits.stride(0)`, `next_n >= 1`, `logits.ndim == 2` | HIP |
| 5 | `flydsl` importable | HIP |

Step 4 is a contract check, not a filter: FlyDSL raises where HIP accepts.

```python
# (min padded width, max rows) bands, widest first.
"gfx950": _DecodeGate(((163840, 15), (131072, 9)), ks={256, 512, 1024, 2048}),
"gfx942": _DecodeGate(((163840, 18), (131072, 11)), ks={256, 512, 1024, 2048}),
```

The first band whose width a call reaches sets its cap, and a call reaching none is refused. Each
cap sits two rows below its measured crossing.

| graph-replay sign change | width 163840 | width 131072 |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950 | rows 17 → cap 15 | rows 11 → cap 9 |
| gfx942 | rows 20 → cap 18 | rows 13 → cap 11 |

A wider buffer is more work per row, so cooperation keeps paying for more rows. One number would
refuse a wide band it wins, or admit a narrow band it loses.

**Width asks "long-context model", not "long request".** Callers size the buffer to the model's max
context — vLLM's indexer builds `logits` as `(batch * next_n, max_model_len)` — and under graph
capture the request length does not exist yet. Sweeping width at fixed real length moves the margin
under 2.2 µs, so the check works only because a request cannot outrun its buffer.

**Thresholds come from graph replay only.** Eager charges HIP 11.7 µs of host work per call against
FlyDSL's 2.6 µs, mostly an un-memoized `topk_ob_workspace_size` query; its kinder column (in-window
median 1.135×, 349/360 won) is that artifact.

| env | effect |
|---|---|
| `AITER_DISABLE_FLYDSL_TOPK_DECODE=1` | every shape back to HIP |
| `AITER_FLYDSL_TOPK_ARCHS` | narrows which archs the table applies to |
| `AITER_FLYDSL_TOPK_MAX_ROWS` | replaces the cap in every band |
| `AITER_FLYDSL_TOPK_MIN_WIDTH` | also flattens the table to one band |
| `AITER_FLYDSL_TOPK_COUNT=1` | tallies flydsl vs hip per worker; an earlier PR-image A/B measured ~0% with HIP on both arms |

**Why the gate lives in AITER.** The alternative duplicates arch detection, availability checks,
shape thresholds and the HIP fallback in every calling framework. `gemm_op_a8w8.py` does the same.

Host cost is the same order as the kernel win, so two things came along:

* `workspace` is a parameter, with a buffer cached on `(device, stream, size rounded to pow2)` —
  worth ~2.4 µs, and returning nothing under graph capture.
* The stream context manager around `workspace.zero_()` is skipped when no stream was asked for.

## Measurements

| | conditions |
|---|---|
| gfx950 | rocprofv3 kernel-only min µs, k=2048, `--boost-ms 500 --warmup 10 --iters 40` |
| gfx942 | 928 cells (k × rows × width × seq), eager and graph replay, both arms through this public entry point so each pays the gate and the workspace sizing; dispatch counters checked per cell |
| regimes | A = uniform padded length, B = per-row random causal length, fixed seed |

**gfx950 vs HIP.** `hip/ours > 1.00` is faster. B tracks A, so the win is not a padding artifact.

| rows | L | ours (µs) | hip (µs) | hip/ours (A) | hip/ours (B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8K | 10.0 | 10.1 | 1.01× | 1.04× |
| 4 | 8K | 10.5 | 10.3 | 0.98× | 1.04× |
| 1 | 65K | 21.1 | 30.1 | **1.42×** | **1.42×** |
| 4 | 65K | 27.0 | 30.0 | 1.11× | 1.10× |
| 8 | 65K | 30.0 | 30.6 | 1.02× | 1.08× |
| 1 | 256K | 31.2 | 33.4 | 1.07× | 1.05× |
| 4 | 256K | 42.1 | 55.6 | 1.32× | 1.24× |
| 8 | 256K | 48.3 | 56.7 | 1.17× | 1.16× |

**gfx950 through the dispatcher**, width 163840, 200 back-to-back calls with one sync at the end.
`hip / dispatch`:

| k | rows | seq 4,096 | 65,536 | 163,840 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 1 | 0.97 | 1.16 | 1.05 |
| 2048 | 4 | 1.16 | 1.32 | 1.25 |
| 2048 | 8 | 1.19 | 1.22 | 1.17 |
| 2048 | 16 | 1.37 | 1.11 | 1.03 |

10 win, 1 tie, 1 marginal (0.97 is ~0.5 µs, inside run-to-run noise). The `rows=16` line predates
the staircase; the cap here is 15, so it routes to HIP now.

**gfx942 length curve**, graph replay, median over k × rows, in the window that shipped when this
was measured (width ≥ 131072, rows ≤ 16). The advantage is a function of the real request length,
which the gate cannot see.

| `seq_len` | 4K | 16K | 32K | 48K | 64K | 96K | 128K | 160K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HIP / FlyDSL (higher = we win) | 0.80× | 0.73× | 0.86× | 0.91× | 1.09× | 1.28× | 1.54× | 1.64× |
| cells won | 0/48 | 0/48 | 3/48 | 6/48 | 40/48 | 48/48 | 48/48 | 24/24 |

* Profitable because the wins are larger than the losses (mean +13.3 against −4.6 µs), not because
  most cells win. Break-even needs long requests to be **25.6%** of traffic.
* The staircase came later: it drops rows 12–16 at width 131072 and admits rows 17–18 at 163840,
  both measured as gains (+2.41 and +1.99 µs per cell). The shipped window scores no worse, but this
  table has not been re-run.
* gfx942 is an SR-IOV VF with no clock locking, so band noise is 2–6 µs against gfx950's 0.3 µs.
  Near-threshold cells were repeated in three independent runs.

**vs Robin's gfx950 base**, informational only — that base was not tuned for wide batch and this
path trails HIP there anyway: rows=1 1.15–1.19×, rows 4–8 parity, rows ≥ 16 2.0×–10.5×. Full sweep
in the [SILOTIGER-699 results comment](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-699?focusedCommentId=23219181).

## Correctness

Buffers are padded past the real length with the tail poisoned, so a kernel ignoring `seqLens` fails
loudly instead of passing by accident.

| arch | result | grid |
|---|---|---|
| gfx950 | **504/504** | A 252/252 + B 252/252, over K{512, 2048} × rows{1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256} × L{8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, 120K, 256K} × dist{random, ties, 10LSB}. No out-of-bounds reads |
| gfx942 | all **928** cells, both arms, two independent runs | plus k{256, 1024} × rows{1, 4, 8} × L{131072, 163840} for the newly admitted k, and rows{12, 16} × k{256, 512, 1024, 2048} × L{4096, 70000, 131072} for the row band above the sweep's samples |

Unit tests on gfx950: **195/195** (dispatcher + kernel, including the stable exact-order cases). Two of the 33 pin the staircase —
the bands descend with width, and one row count is refused at 131072 and admitted at 163840.

Run: `pytest op_tests/test_topk_decode_dispatch.py`,
`pytest op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_topk_per_row_decode.py`,
`python op_tests/topk_decode_correctness.py`, and
`python op_tests/benchmark_topk_per_row_decode.py` under rocprofv3.

## stable=True (ordered emit)

Previously `stable=True` forced HIP: FlyDSL returned an unordered set. This commit
adds an **ordered emit** to the tiered kernel and routes `stable=True` through
the **same gate bands** as the unordered path (`ordered=stable` forwarded to
FlyDSL).

Implementation highlights:

- One contiguous vec-block run per workgroup; run counts from pass histograms
  (`s_own_hist`) — no extra row read for a count pass.
- `ordered=True` disables the short-tier atomic scatter and `early_stop`
  (both assume unordered output); persistent path covers all tiers.
- Launcher cache key includes `ordered` (different kernel).

**Correctness contract:** exact index list equality, ascending with
smallest-index tie-break on the kth value — not set equivalence. Tie-dense
inputs in tests.

| check | gfx950 result |
|---|---|
| `pytest op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_topk_per_row_decode.py` + `op_tests/test_topk_decode_dispatch.py` | **195/195** |
| `python op_tests/test_topk_per_row_stable.py` | **ALL PASS** |
| Final bench (3 rep, all shapes) | **exact failures 0** |

**Performance (stable, k=2048, 3-rep median µs, vs #5011 ordered / HIP):**

| rows × L | ours | 5011 | ours/5011 | HIP | ours/HIP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26 × 700K | 126 | 121 | 1.04 | 933 | 0.14 |
| 26 × 1M | 157 | 149 | 1.05 | 1335 | 0.12 |
| 28 × 700K | 128 | 127 | 1.01 | 933 | 0.14 |
| 28 × 1M | 159 | 160 | 0.99 | 1335 | 0.12 |
| 32 × 700K | 134 | 128 | 1.05 | 936 | 0.14 |
| 32 × 1M | 165 | 166 | 1.00 | 1336 | 0.12 |

Gate region (26–32 × 700K–1M): **5011 parity (0.99–1.05×)**, **HIP 7–8×**.
Stable overhead vs unordered: **1.12–1.18×** in that region. Only regression:
rows=8 × 700K/1M ~**1.11×** vs 5011 (gate-outside; HIP ~92/118 µs there).

Raw: `JHK_TASK/.../results_this_node/final/stable_fused_rep{1,2,3}.jsonl`.

## Follow-ups

| | why it is left | blocker |

| Kernel self-reset | the barrier-counter `zero_()` is 3.7 µs of launch latency per call, the largest item left | HIP's multi-block kernel already self-resets; a side stream measured slower |
| gfx942 kernel tuning | the four gfx950 switches are frozen there; enabling them flipped rows=32 from 0.79× to 1.06× and widens the window | needs a full correctness pass |
| HIP multi-block for decode | the C++ decode entry is one-block only, though its own crossover says multi-block should win where FlyDSL does | graph capture freezes `stride0`, this gate's information problem |
